title: Frozen simulation results: knowledge-guided TBM disc-cutter replacement planning
abstract: Frozen simulation results from the knowledge-guided motion planning evaluation on tunnel boring machine (TBM) disc-cutter replacement across nine scene variants. The package provides 828 paired trajectory tasks (knowledge-guided versus from-scratch) and 158,760 point-level configuration queries, together with aggregated JSON summaries for the manuscript tables and figures. Scene parameters, outcome mixes, failure taxonomy counts, baseline-scene ablations, reference Success@K coverage, and an offline guided-budget replay are included; joint trajectories, collision meshes, and the WRS planning platform are not distributed.

title: Interpreting potato disease classification using explainable artificial intelligence
abstract: Timely and accurate crop diseases detection is most important for ensuring global food security. For detecting diseases in crops, many different machine learning (ML) models were proposed. These models work as a black-box, and without proper explanation of these models’ decisions, farmers may find it difficult to trust these systems. For this, many model explainability methods were also proposed. All these methods have been evaluated qualitatively, but their quantitative and cross-comparison are missing. This study addresses this gap by emphasizing quantitative validation of models’ explanations. This study investigates the interpretability and performance of two approaches for potato leaf disease classification: i) manual feature engineering with relief-based feature selection and artificial neural network (ANN) classification with local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) and ii) deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) based on mobile network version 2 (MobileNetV2) with gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM). Quantitative assessment of explanation quality was performed using fidelity and robustness metrics. While LIME achieved a lower average fidelity drop 10.90% and higher robustness 84.27% compared to Grad-CAM 18.68% fidelity drops and 79.38% robustness, Grad-CAM provided clearer visual explanations. These findings suggest that explanation effectiveness is influenced by model design and data characteristics, highlighting the need for careful selection of interpretability techniques in precision agriculture applications.

title: Privacy-Preserving Cross-Chain Asset Tracking: A Threshold PSI Protocol with Real-World Exploit Validation
abstract: Cross-border financial investigations often face difficulties due to isolated data systems, especially when different Financial Intelligence Units (FIUs) independently track illegal funds moving across different blockchain networks. This paper presents an enhanced multi-chain t-out-of-n threshold Private Set Intersection (PSI) protocol for high-throughput, privacy-preserving jurisdictional deconfliction. Built upon Shamir’s Secret Sharing over the Z_{2^{127}-1} Mersenne prime field, the protocol introduces a high-performance cryptographic field-mapping mechanism leveraging the BLAKE3-XOF. The protocol is formally validated under the semi-honest adversarial model, with three theorems establishing sub-threshold privacy, intersection completeness, and a negligible false-positive rate of 2^{-127}. We evaluate scalability on three heterogeneous blockchain corpora (Bitcoin UTXO and Ethereum account-based models) scaled up to 500,000 records per ledger. The BLAKE3-based mapping achieves a 1.88× throughput improvement over a SHA-256/512 baseline, reaching up to 1.55 × 10^6 operations per second. Experimental validation across a multi-ledger testbed using the Elliptic++, BABD-13, and XBlock-ETH datasets in a three-jurisdiction FIU deconfliction setting confirms correct threshold enforcement, full recovery of all three-way illicit intersections without false positives, and near-linear runtime behaviour. In a larger five-jurisdiction setting, the system reliably identifies all threshold intersections while maintaining zero reconstruction errors. The proposed protocol is relevant for FIUs, blockchain analytics researchers, and cybersecurity practitioners engaged in cross-border illicit asset tracing and privacy-preserving data collaboration.

title: Free‐Space Continuous‐Variable Quantum Key Distribution Under Temporal Channel Dynamics
abstract: ABSTRACT Temporal dynamics of free‐space continuous‐variable quantum key distribution (CV‐QKD) are intrinsically complicated by atmospheric turbulence‐induced channel fluctuations. The finite‐state Markov (FSM) framework provides a promising approach for mapping temporal evolution into state transitions. However, its application to CV‐QKD remains challenging due to the need for accurate characterization of both channel statistics and temporal correlations. Here, we derive the joint probability density function (PDF) of channel transmittance and its time derivative for log‐normal (LN) and Gamma–Gamma (GG) turbulence models. Based on a spectral‐domain analytical (SDA) approach incorporating inner‐ and outer‐scale effects, we derive temporal channel parameters and quantify the impact of adaptive optics (AO). Furthermore, the level crossing rate (LCR) of channel loss is derived to construct state transition probabilities (STPs) for the FSM framework, which is then employed to predict the temporal evolution of channel transmittance and achievable secret key rate (SKR).Results demonstrate that the proposed FSM framework accurately captures temporal dynamics of free‐space CV‐QKD and turbulence‐induced fluctuations. Under weak turbulence, AO enhances temporal correlation, increases mean SKR, and suppresses short‐term SKR fluctuations. Under strong turbulence, AO improves mean SKR but provides limited enhancement of temporal correlation and fluctuation suppression due to physical constraints.

title: DART: A DAG-Based Reputation and Incentive Framework via Blockchain-Enabled Governance for Trustworthy LLM Multi-Agent Collaboration
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) predominantly rely on centralized orchestration and lack formal verification mechanisms for agent reliability, participation, and system-level behavioral alignment. These shortcomings leave open environments severely vulnerable to uncooperative or malicious agents. This work proposes DART, a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)-based reputation and incentive regulation framework for trustworthy multi-agent collaboration, combining centralized operational orchestration with blockchain-enabled decentralized governance and accountability. DART unifies DAG workflow orchestration, capability and reputation-aware task allocation, dynamic behavior updates, multi-factor incentives, and smart contract accountability paired with IPFS storage. Under this paradigm, agent selection dynamically balances task alignment, historical reputation, and workload, while post-execution behavioral evidence continuously calibrates agent trust and the probability of future participation. Evaluated across four axes, DART achieves 93.6% Pass@1 on GSM8K and builds a full-stack application in 142 s using two agents, outperforming centralized baselines. Across five independent 150-round longitudinal trials, Full DART achieves a mean task success rate of 93.33 +/- 2.26%, output quality of 0.9357 +/- 0.0117, retry rate of 0.2307 +/- 0.0816, and allocation delay of 1.1153 +/- 0.0408 s, consistently outperforming its ablated configurations DART isolates persistent and intermittent malicious agents, obtaining a 99.3% output containment rate and restoring system success to 99.8%. These results demonstrate the potential of coupling reputation, incentives, DAG-based coordination, and verifiable blockchain-enabled governance to support adaptive and accountable multi-agent collaboration.

title: SDARE-Bench: Evaluating Large Language Models on Conversational Stigma Detection and Response in Dyadic and Group Dialogue
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in advice seeking and decision making that may affect social judgements. Despite stigma's profound effects on people and communities, benchmarks remain scarce. Existing general-domain evaluations typically rely on static prompts and fixed-format tasks, overlooking conversational contexts and audience effects in everyday communication. To address these gaps, we introduce SDARE-Bench, the first scenario-based benchmark evaluating both stigma detection and open-ended response generation in LLMs, comprising 1,138 dyadic queries and 1,388 group dialogue. Empirical results across 8 LLMs consistently demonstrate poor identification of stigma components, especially in group dialogues. In open-ended response generation, stigma expression was substantially higher in group settings than in dyadic, with weaker resistance to stigma and more unrealistic advice. Responses were evaluated using a classifier trained on 1,392 human annotated responses. In constructed group pressure settings, stigma expression rates further increased to a striking average of 97.5%. Our findings identify stigma response as a recurring LLM safety vulnerability, especially in socially complex conversational contexts.

title: Just Talk Once: Communication-Efficient Split Federated LLM Fine-Tuning on Edge Devices
abstract: Large language model (LLM) fine-tuning is increasingly shifting toward data generated on edge devices, where memory, computation, bandwidth, and connectivity constraints make conventional federated learning difficult to sustain. Split federated fine-tuning (SFT) improves client-side efficiency by offloading most model parameters and computation to the server but requires step-by-step bidirectional communication loop across the split interface and forces continuous client involvement throughout training. In this paper, we present L-shaped SFT, a split fine-tuning framework that removes this bidirectional bottleneck. Our key insight is that weight tying in modern LLMs enables server-side hidden activations to be directly supervised using target embeddings, allowing the training loss to be computed on the server without returning server outputs to the client. To further eliminate the need for continuous client participation, based on L-shaped SFT, we introduce one-shot SFT, in which clients upload activations once and then go offline while the server continues optimization over cached representations. We implement our design in a real system testbed with heterogeneous edge clients, including commercial smartphones and NVIDIA developer boards. Experiments demonstrate that our schemes significantly reduce communication costs and client online time compared with existing SFT baselines.

title: The Constitutional Coverage Trilemma in AI Governance
abstract: Frontier AI systems function as \emph{constitutional institutions}: each deployed model encodes an implicit ranking among safety, helpfulness, honesty, autonomy, and equity. We ask whether the supply of frontier constitutional types covers human demand. Combining a paraphrase-controlled audit of the as-shipped default constitutions of $23$ frontier LLM archetypes with a pairwise-tradeoff study of $1{,}649$ US participants on the same instrument, we report three facts. \emph{Demand is broad}: it spans all five values, with the largest constituency under one-third. \emph{Supply is narrow and drifting}: the $23$-archetype hull occupies ${\sim}2\%$ of the demand hull under conservative noise-matched estimation ($0.10\%$ at full audit precision), no archetype puts helpfulness or autonomy first ($37\%$ of users are constitutionally homeless), and across six model families autonomy decreases in $5/6$, equity increases in $5/6$, and safety increases in $4/6$, with monotone within-family version trends (order-permutation $p = 0.013$) and the autonomy decline concentrated in scenarios where safety is not at stake. The drift's importance is directional: \emph{away} from a value already undercovered, mechanically worsening the welfare floor for the least-served users. \emph{The fix is sparse}: a $2$-vertex menu $\{e_{\mathrm{HON}}, e_{\mathrm{AUT}}\}$ beats the full $23$-archetype frontier by $47\%$ on mean regret (CI $[43\%, 52\%]$); three vertex additions cut mean/worst-group regret by up to $81\%$/$64\%$. We formalize these findings as a budgeted-pluralism trilemma, show the binding regime is empirically realized, and verify the conclusions are robust to distance-based welfare and to degraded routing. The instrument and audit harness are described in full in the appendices.

title: PyDoseRT Proton: A GPU Pencil-Beam Engine with a Convolutional Residual-Correction Network for Fast Proton Dose Calculation
abstract: Architecture category. Hybrid method: a physics-based analytical pencil-beam (PB) dose engine followed by a 3-D convolutional residual-correction network (RepVGG-U-Net). We addressed the DoseRAD2026 proton dose-prediction task with PyDoseRT Proton, a GPU-accelerated engine implemented in PyTorch and augmented by a learned residual toward Monte Carlo (MC) accuracy. A double-Gaussian PB kernel was calibrated to GATE/Geant4 integrated depth doses in water in two stages: a classical per-energy curve fit, then a gradient-based fit of the full 3-D dose through the PyTorch physics engine as it retains a differentiable execution path for gradient-based optimization of dose-dependent objectives. The engine computes each beamlet on a beam's-eye-view (BEV) lattice with variance-preserving Gaussian splitting, an analytic nuclear halo, and a Fermi-Eyges heterogeneity term, then rotates the result into the patient frame. Additionally, a compact residual U-Net predicts an additive correction in BEV space. It is conditioned on voxelwise material-label embeddings, a discrete energy embedding and spot size. The same model was used for all anatomical sites (thoracic and abdominal). It was trained with a patient-space L1 objective emphasizing the scored high-dose region and multi-scale BEV deep supervision. The submitted CT configuration obtained preliminary-test beamlet MAE 0.0066, image-z IDD distance 0.0025, plan MAE 0.0049, 98.30\% gamma pass rate (1\%/1 mm), and DVH error 0.460.

title: Solaris: Towards Interfaces That Are Generated, Not Coded
abstract: Digital interfaces are traditionally implemented through intermediate representations such as code, requiring their appearance and behavior to be specified in advance. We introduce Solaris, an interface world model that instead generates an interactive UI directly, frame by frame, in response to user actions. Solaris treats mouse interactions as conditioning signals and autoregressively synthesizes the resulting visual state at interactive speeds. To enable real-time generation while maintaining visual coherence over extended interactions, we combine autoregressive frame generation with few-step distillation and training on the model's own outputs. A language model complements the visual world model by interpreting user intent and specifying how interactions should affect the generated environment, separating high-level reasoning from visual rendering. By generating both the appearance and behavior of an interface dynamically, Solaris enables open-ended interactions that need not be explicitly programmed in advance. title: EEG-VID: Task-Guided Latent Predictive Pretraining for EEG Decoding and Assistive Target Selection
abstract: We propose EEG-VID, a task-guided latent predictive pretraining framework for EEG decoding under session and subject shifts. EEG-VID predicts future latent EEG states from recent history using an exponential-moving-average target encoder and weak task guidance, followed by supervised fine-tuning. Across VIG-48 and BCI Competition IV-2a/IV-2b, Stage 1 improves mean accuracy in 41 of 42 matched backbone-dataset-protocol comparisons, including all 12 leave-one-subject-out settings, with a maximum gain of 16.22 percentage points. On the 48-region cross-day VIG-48 task, EEG-VID achieves 6.52% Top-1 and 30.50% Top-5 accuracy. In a separate six-participant offline robot-scene study, candidate-constrained target selection reaches 40.24% versus a 25% chance level after subject-specific calibration. These results support task-guided latent prediction as a transferable pretraining strategy for EEG decoding and scene-constrained assistive target selection.

title: Penalized FCI for causal structure learning in a sparse DAG for biomarker discovery in Parkinson’s disease
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that lacks reliable early-stage biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic monitoring. While cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers, such as α-synuclein seed amplification assays (αSyn-SAA), offer diagnostic potential, their clinical utility is limited by invasiveness and incomplete specificity. Plasma biomarkers provide a minimally invasive alternative, but their mechanistic role in PD remains unclear. A major challenge is distinguishing whether plasma biomarkers causally reflect primary neurodegenerative processes or are downstream consequences of disease progression. To address this, we leverage the Parkinson’s Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) Project 9000, containing 2,924 plasma and CSF biomarkers, to systematically infer causal relationships with disease status. However, only a sparse subset of these biomarkers and their interconnections are actually relevant for the disease. Existing causal discovery algorithms, such as Fast Causal Inference (FCI) and its variants, struggle with the high dimensionality of biomarker datasets under sparsity, limiting their scalability. We propose Penalized Fast Causal Inference (PFCI), a novel approach that incorporates sparsity constraints to efficiently infer causal structures in large-scale biological datasets. By applying PFCI to PPMI data, we aim to identify biomarkers that are causally linked to PD pathology, enabling early diagnosis and patient stratification. Our findings will facilitate biomarker-driven clinical trials and contribute to the development of neuroprotective therapies.

title: WHEN AI AGENTS BECOME ATTACKERS: A ZERO-TRUST SECURITY BLUEPRINT FOR TOOLS, MEMORY, RAG, AND MCP WORKFLOWS
abstract: Large language model agents convert probabilistic text generation into consequential action by selecting tools, retrieving external knowledge, retaining memory, and coordinating through protocol-connected services. This shift changes the security problem. A model does not need malicious intent to behave as an attacker; it only needs to accept adversarial context, possess excessive authority, and execute an unsafe transition. Prompt injection, retrieval poisoning, malicious memory, confused-deputy behavior, and compromised tool descriptions can therefore transform a helpful agent into an attack path spanning data, credentials, applications, and physical processes. This chapter develops a zero-trust blueprint for agentic systems built around continuous verification, least privilege, provenance, explicit policy enforcement, isolation, and auditable execution. It treats prompts, retrieved passages, memories, tool outputs, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) messages as untrusted data rather than implicit authority. The blueprint separates planning from authorization; places capability brokers and policy decision points between models and effects; gates memory writes and retrieval ingestion; constrains MCP servers by identity, scope, and transaction; and requires signed, replayable receipts for high-impact actions. Three threat-control matrices and three architectural figures translate the analysis into deployable patterns. The central conclusion is deliberately architectural: safety prompting can reduce risk, but only independently enforced controls can bound what a compromised agent is able to do.

title: Avaliação de Táticas de Red Teaming Automatizado em Modelos de Linguagem de Pequeno Porte (SLMs)
abstract: Modelos de Linguagem de Pequeno Porte (SLMs) enfrentam crescentes desafios de segurança relacionados a ataques de injeção de prompt. Este trabalho apresenta uma avaliação empírica automatizada de táticas de red teaming aplicadas aos modelos Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct e SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct. Utilizando um classificador especializado (DistilBERT) como juiz automatizado, foram avaliados 60 vetores de ataque divididos em quatro categorias. Os resultados apontam uma Taxa de Sucesso de Ataque (ASR) global de 45,00% para o Qwen2.5 e 61,67% para o SmolLM2, evidenciando variações significativas de resiliência no alinhamento pós-treinamento entre as arquiteturas.

title: Prediction Of Daily Patient Visits At A Community Health Center Using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) With Laplace Differential Privacy
abstract: This study aims to analyze the performance of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) in predicting daily patient visits using limited-scale Electronic Medical Record (EMR) data and to evaluate the effect of applying Laplace Differential Privacy on prediction accuracy. The data were obtained from the EMR of Puskesmas in Sukabumi Regency, covering the period from January to December 2025. The data were preprocessed through cleaning, aggregation of daily patient visits, exclusion of holidays, and the construction of 14 days sequences. The LSTM model was evaluated using walk-forward validation with an expanding-window scheme consisting of five folds, while privacy protection was implemented using the Laplace mechanism with . The results showed that the baseline model achieved an RMSE of 25.08 and an MAE of 22.19. The application of Differential Privacy increased prediction errors, with higher errors levels observed at smaller Increasing from 1.0 to 2.0 resulted in the largest reduction in prediction error, while further increas provided relatively small improvements. Based on these results, provided the most acceptable balance between privacy protection and prediction performance for the dataset used in this study.

title: Bigger, Better, or Just Bigger: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of scaling laws and compute as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Capricorn Rabbit-rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Zodiac Animals
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Capricorn Rabbit-rat (CRR), inspired by the astrological characteristics and behaviors of the Capricorn, Rabbit, and Rat zodiac animals. CRR combines elements of the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), the Cuckoo Search (CS) algorithm, and a novel mutation operator derived from the foraging patterns of rats. The algorithm utilizes a multi-dimensional search space and iteratively adjusts its population based on the relative dominance and fitness of individuals. The core innovation lies in the adaptive mutation strategy, which mimics the rat's ability to explore the environment and exploit promising regions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CRR through simulations on various benchmark optimization problems, including the Sphere function, Rastrigin function, and the Himmelblau function. Results show that CRR consistently outperforms or achieves comparable performance to existing metaheuristic algorithms like GWO and CS, particularly in challenging, high-dimensional landscapes. The algorithm's adaptability and efficient exploration capabilities make it a promising candidate for diverse optimization tasks.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的算法选择
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of algorithm selection, a crucial step in many scientific and engineering disciplines. Traditional algorithm selection methods rely heavily on human expertise and often struggle to adapt effectively to diverse problem domains. We propose a novel approach leveraging a self-adaptive machine learning model to dynamically optimize algorithm performance metrics. This model learns a set of performance indicators directly from the problem data, enabling a more automated and flexible algorithm selection process. The core mechanism involves adjusting the learned performance metrics to improve the selection of optimal algorithms for given input data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and experimental results, showcasing its potential to significantly enhance algorithm selection efficiency and robustness.

title: On Optimizing Programs Based on Information Entropy
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program optimization by leveraging the concept of information entropy. The core idea is to treat program optimization as an entropy maximization problem, aiming to design programs that are both efficient and robust. We formulate program optimization problems in terms of information entropy, utilizing its properties to guide program design and optimization strategies. This approach expands the theoretical foundation of program optimization and offers a new perspective for program design. We explore the potential benefits of this framework, highlighting its ability to produce programs with enhanced characteristics. The paper presents a foundational exploration of this concept, laying groundwork for future research and development in the field. ---

title: Cuckoo Search: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Cuckoo Bird
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Cuckoo Search (CS), inspired by the brood parasitism behavior of cuckoo birds. The algorithm leverages the principles of cuckoo laying eggs in the nests of other cuckoos, the rejection of similar nests, and the randomization of the search space to efficiently explore and exploit the solution landscape. CS employs a population-based approach, maintaining a set of candidate solutions represented as locations in a multidimensional space. The algorithm's core components include the Levy flight mechanism for exploration, the nest rejection mechanism for exploitation, and a probability-based update strategy. The proposed algorithm is demonstrated through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its effectiveness and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that CS is capable of finding near-optimal solutions for a wide range of problems with minimal computational effort. The algorithm's key parameters, including the Levy parameter (α), the discovery rate (ρ), and the probability of nest rejection (p), are analyzed for their impact on convergence and solution quality. Future research directions include integrating CS with other optimization techniques and exploring its applicability to complex, real-world problems.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Diffusion Processes (QEP)
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Diffusion Processes (QEP) presents a novel approach to diffusion modeling, utilizing quantum mechanics to accelerate and control the spread of information. This research explores the potential of quantum tunneling to enhance the exploration of the state space, leading to significantly faster and more accurate results compared to traditional diffusion algorithms. The core mechanism involves an algorithm that guides the diffusion process using quantum tunneling, enabling a more efficient and targeted spread of data. title: Evolutionary Algorithms for Designing Analog Circuits with Temporal Constraints
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to analog circuit design using evolutionary algorithms (EAs) to address the challenges posed by temporal constraints – specifically, signal propagation delays. Traditional analog circuit design often relies on static analysis and optimization, neglecting the dynamic behavior of signals. This results in circuits that may meet specifications under ideal conditions but fail to perform adequately in real-world scenarios where timing variations and signal propagation delays are significant factors. Our method incorporates temporal modeling directly into the EA framework, allowing the algorithm to explore circuit topologies and parameter settings that minimize the impact of delays. The core of the approach involves an EA that iteratively evolves a population of circuit designs, evaluating each design based on both performance metrics (e.g., gain, bandwidth) and a temporal cost function that quantifies the overall delay experienced by signals propagating through the circuit. The resulting circuits are more robust and predictable, offering improved performance across a wider range of operating conditions. This work demonstrates the feasibility and potential of EAs for designing analog circuits with temporal constraints, paving the way for automated and optimized design processes.

title: ## Borneo Fruit Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Borneo Fruit Bat Algorithm (BFBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of fruit bats in the Borneo rainforest. Fruit bats exhibit remarkable navigation and resource-seeking abilities, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies to efficiently locate food sources. The BFBA leverages these characteristics to develop a robust optimization algorithm suitable for tackling complex, non-linear, and multi-dimensional problems. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic population of bats, each with individual movement vectors and food preferences. Movement is governed by a probabilistic system mimicking the bats' flight patterns, influenced by local food density and global search parameters. The algorithm employs a novel 'social learning' component, where bats share information about promising food locations, enhancing the exploration capabilities. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations and theoretical analysis, showcasing its potential for superior performance compared to established metaheuristic methods, particularly in scenarios demanding adaptability and efficient resource utilization. The core of the BFBA lies in the continuous adaptation of bat movement vectors and the strategic dissemination of food location information, providing a unique approach to optimization. The key mathematical elements include: position vectors (si), velocity vectors (vi), food density (φ), learning rate (α), exploration parameter (ε), exploitation parameter (β), and a social influence factor (γ). The algorithm's performance is evaluated using several benchmark functions, confirming its ability to find near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time.

title: Title: Adaptive Neural Network Feature Selection
abstract: This paper investigates the application of an adaptive neural network-based feature selection technique to improve model performance. Traditional feature selection methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, failing to adapt to evolving data distributions. We propose a novel algorithm that utilizes the inherent dynamics of a neural network to automatically identify and select the most relevant features, enhancing model accuracy and generalization. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting feature importance based on the data's inherent patterns, providing a robust and automated feature selection process. The research addresses the limitations of current methods by offering a flexible and adaptive approach to feature selection that surpasses the capabilities of existing techniques. The presented algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in model accuracy and robustness compared to baseline methods, particularly when dealing with complex datasets exhibiting non-linear relationships.

title: Bolburn's Tuco-tuco
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, "Bolburn's Tuco-tuco," inspired by the foraging behavior of the Tuco-tuco bird ( *Egretta rufascidea*). The algorithm leverages the bird's unique strategy of oscillating between two locations, a concept we represent mathematically as a coupled differential equation system. We formulate the optimization problem as a search space where each point represents a potential solution. The algorithm utilizes a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating a dynamic adjustment of the oscillation frequency and amplitude based on a novel fitness-dependent mechanism. The core of the algorithm revolves around two "Bolburns" – virtual birds – that represent candidate solutions. These Bolburns oscillate between two points in the search space, influenced by their individual and global best positions, as well as an adaptive oscillation parameter. We present a detailed mathematical formulation of the algorithm, including equations describing the movement of the Bolburns and the dynamics of the oscillation parameters. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its efficacy and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic methods. Key performance metrics include convergence speed, solution quality, and computational complexity. The algorithm aims to provide a robust and adaptable solution for a variety of optimization challenges.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of dynamic chaos, specifically leveraging quantum entanglement, to develop novel computational paradigms for complex topological structures. The core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic chaos framework where the system's state evolves through a series of entangled interactions, resulting in a highly adaptable and computationally efficient representation of these topological spaces. This research delves into the theoretical foundations and potential practical applications of this approach, with a focus on its implications for computer graphics and beyond. We examine the challenges and opportunities presented by this new approach, highlighting the advantages it offers over traditional methods.

title: bonezegei/BSL_Hash: Version 1.0.0
abstract: BSL_Hash BSL_Hash is a checksum and hashing library designed for the Bonezegei Scripting Language (BSL). It provides fast non-cryptographic checksums, modern hash functions, and cryptographic digests in .bzg scripts. Table of Contents Installation Getting Started Code Examples 1. Checksums & Non-Cryptographic Hashes 2. Cryptographic Digest Hashes 3. Complete Verification Script API Reference License & Author Citation Installation Install BSL_Hash using the BSL Package Manager (bzg): bzg install hash Getting Started To use the library in your script, include the hash module after installation and instantiate the hash object: include("lib/hash.bzg"); var h = hash(); var digest = h.sha256("Hello, Bonezegei!"); print("SHA256: " + digest); Code Examples 1. Checksums & Non-Cryptographic Hashes Example calculating checksums and non-cryptographic hashes for high-speed data processing and hash table operations: /* Non-Cryptographic Hashes Example Author: Jofel Batutay (Bonezegei) Date: April 17, 2026 */ include("lib/hash.bzg"); var h = hash(); var input = "Hello, Bonezegei!"; print("CRC32: " + h.crc32(input)); print("Adler-32: " + h.adler32(input)); print("FNV-1a: " + h.fnv1a(input)); print("MurmurHash3: " + h.murmur3(input, 42)); // Input and Seed print("xxHash: " + h.xxhash(input, 0)); // Input and Seed 2. Cryptographic Digest Hashes Example generating secure cryptographic hexadecimal digests from string inputs: /* Cryptographic Digest Hashes Example Author: Jofel Batutay (Bonezegei) Date: April 17, 2026 */ include("lib/hash.bzg"); var h = hash(); var input = "Hello, Bonezegei!"; print("MD5: " + h.md5(input)); print("SHA1: " + h.sha1(input)); print("SHA256: " + h.sha256(input)); print("SHA-3: " + h.sha3(input)); print("SHA512: " + h.sha512(input)); 3. Complete Verification Script A full test suite script demonstrating output verification across all supported hashing algorithms: /* BSL_Hash Test Suite Author: Jofel Batutay (Bonezegei) Date: April 17, 2026 */ include("lib/hash.bzg"); function check(label, actual, expected) { if (actual === expected) { print("PASS: " + label + " OUTPUT: " + actual); } else { print("FAIL: " + label + " OUTPUT: " + actual); } } var h = hash(); var input = "Hello, Bonezegei!"; var key = "super_secret_key"; print("--- Checksums & Non-Cryptographic Hashes ---"); check("CRC32: " , h.crc32(input), "ccccf7f8"); check("Adler-32: " , h.adler32(input), "35b905fa"); check("FNV-1a: " , h.fnv1a(input), "59673d46"); check("MurmurHash3: " , h.murmur3(input, 42), "e95a8d40"); check("xxHash: " , h.xxhash(input, 0), "59eafb70"); print("\n--- Cryptographic Digest Hashes (Hex) ---"); check("MD5: " , h.md5(input), "1390f98482b7ebe2668fa8f64a55b71f"); check("SHA1: " , h.sha1(input), "bd46120f02cbe618411cbd70c0cfd37715014347"); check("SHA256: " , h.sha256(input), "67ea37441cb5523681dd7ae769d877ddf2d510af48a052d53dcb736c3b1e5387"); check("SHA-3: " , h.sha3(input), "206a1b8a0d0d8023622551786f1c4f1f5b99b92dcd6412212892d949749294ea"); check("SHA512: " , h.sha512(input), "1c7e571d5f7eaf56af22af63b25d1812640d1a3ea6f758a0fe70d41a485b28a14bfbb1aa0deb671937faeeb3398c6b91853a5f3d67680686a4d018b50ec2db6d"); API Reference | Function Signature | Return Value | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | h.crc32(input) | string (Hex) | Computes a 32-bit Cyclic Redundancy Check checksum. | | h.adler32(input) | string (Hex) | Computes an Adler-32 checksum. | | h.fnv1a(input) | string (Hex) | Computes a 32-bit Fowler–Noll–Vo 1a non-cryptographic hash. | | h.murmur3(input, seed) | string (Hex) | Computes a 32-bit MurmurHash3 non-cryptographic hash with a custom seed. | | h.xxhash(input, seed) | string (Hex) | Computes an xxHash non-cryptographic hash with a custom seed. | | h.md5(input) | string (Hex) | Computes a 128-bit MD5 cryptographic hash digest. | | h.sha1(input) | string (Hex) | Computes a 160-bit SHA-1 cryptographic hash digest. | | h.sha256(input) | string (Hex) | Computes a 256-bit SHA-256 cryptographic hash digest. | | h.sha3(input) | string (Hex) | Computes a SHA-3 cryptographic hash digest. | | h.sha512(input) | string (Hex) | Computes a 512-bit SHA-512 cryptographic hash digest. | License & Author Author: Jofel Batutay (Bonezegei) Website: bonezegei.com Citation [![DOI]) If you use this library, please cite it as below: APA Format: Batutay, J. title: BERT-Based Temporal Sentiment Analysis of Saudi Tourism Events
abstract: This study applies a BERT-based temporal sentiment analysis framework to examine English-language social media discourse surrounding major tourism and sporting events hosted in Saudi Arabia. A dataset of 10,000 tweets collected between December 2023 and December 2024, including discussions related to the FIFA Club World Cup, Formula 1 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and other major Saudi-hosted sporting events, was analyzed to investigate sentiment dynamics across pre-event, during-event, and post- event stages. The fine-tuned BERT model achieved an F1-score of 0.85, outperforming traditional machine learning and deep learning baselines. Results reveal strong positive sentiment during event periods, with measurable variations across different temporal stages. The findings demonstrate the value of transformer-based sentiment analysis for understanding international audience engagement with Saudi mega-events and provide empirical insights relevant to tourism development and Vision 2030 objectives.

title: A Scalable Framework for Developing Viable Ontology-Centric Systems
abstract: Abstract The paper addresses the question of creating long-living software systems. One of the possible challenging comprehensive solutions for this might be to provide a viable framework which supports their complete life-cycle. The concept and architecture of a scalable framework for creating and maintaining software ontology-centric systems are proposed. The basis for the framework is the 2-level approach to the formation of system components of all types. It allows one to separate component models (ontologies) from components themselves. The 3-layer architecture of the framework is proposed. An implementation of the framework concept as a cloud platform was created. Several knowledge portals have been developed with its use. This evaluation showed that the proposed solution is a promising way for the organization of an ecosystem for collaborative development of viable information and software resources.

title: FY26 End of Year Report: Seismic Monitoring of Underground Vibration Sources Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing and Seismometers
abstract: This report shows progress in the development and validation of an end‑to‑end seismic monitoring pipeline designed to detect and locate anomalous underground vibration signals that may indicate containment breaches or other safeguard-relevant activites at geological repositories. Building on the waveform database and ground‑truth event catalog established in FY 2025, we integrated a complementary processing workflow to improve signal characterization by extending the analysis beyond previously identified broadband signals to include spectrally discrete signals. Spectrally discrete signals are commonly associated with mechanical sources, including power generators, ventilation and air-conditioning systems, pumps, and other machinery. To characterize these signals, a network spectrogram is computed by stacking individual station spectrograms, suppressing highly localized signals while enhancing signals with a broader spatial footprint. A moving median kernel is then computed and subtracted from the median spectrogram along the frequency axis to remove broadband noise and improve the detectability of narrowband spectral features. Spectral peaks are identified from the resulting enhanced spectrogram and time-frequency energy maps are constructed. A multi-target Kalman tracking filter then links spectral peaks into signal tracks following a specific physical model. These tracks can remain stable in frequency or exhibit gradual frequency drift and can last from a few minutes to several hours. They are interpreted as signatures of persistent mechanical processes, such as those associated with mining machinery. The time-frequency histories of the identified tracks are further analyzed to extract station-specific amplitudes and relative phase delays for source localization. As these tracks are attributed to stationary machines, those performing highly repetitive tasks, the confidence in location can be improved with additional localization results. The proposed procedure is causal and computationally efficient, making it suitable for ad hoc and potentially real-time applications, while also providing opportunities for further computational optimization. evidence.title: FY26 End of Year Report: Seismic Monitoring of Underground Vibration Sources Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing and Seismometers
evidence.abstract: This report shows progress in the development and validation of an end‑to‑end seismic monitoring pipeline designed to detect and locate anomalous underground vibration signals that may indicate containment breaches or other safeguard-relevant activites at geological repositories. Building on the waveform database and ground‑truth event catalog established in FY 2025, we integrated a complementary processing workflow to improve signal characterization by extending the analysis beyond previously identified broadband signals to include spectrally discrete signals. Spectrally discrete signals are commonly associated with mechanical sources, including power generators, ventilation and air-conditioning systems, pumps, and other machinery. To characterize these signals, a network spectrogram is computed by stacking individual station spectrograms, suppressing highly localized signals while enhancing signals with a broader spatial footprint. A moving median kernel is then computed and subtracted from the median spectrogram along the frequency axis to remove broadband noise and improve the detectability of narrowband spectral features. Spectral peaks are identified from the resulting enhanced spectrogram and time-frequency energy maps are constructed. A multi-target Kalman tracking filter then links spectral peaks into signal tracks following a specific physical model. These tracks can remain stable in frequency or exhibit gradual frequency drift and can last from a few minutes to several hours. They are interpreted as signatures of persistent mechanical processes, such as those associated with mining machinery. The time-frequency histories of the identified tracks are further analyzed to extract station-specific amplitudes and relative phase delays for source localization. As these tracks are attributed to stationary machines, those performing highly repetitive tasks, the confidence in location can be improved with additional localization results. The proposed procedure is causal and computationally efficient, making it suitable for ad hoc and potentially real-time applications, while also providing opportunities for further computational optimization. title: Hybrid lightweight encryption and searchable security framework for secure VANET image and text data sharing
abstract: The increasing reliance on vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) for instantaneous traffic orchestration and data exchange highlights the need for robust, efficient, and privacy preserving security solutions. Classical encryption methods often fail to meet the low-latency and lightweight requirements of vehicular environments. In this study, a hybrid cryptographic framework was designed that integrates searchable encryption (SE) with the Spritz stream cipher, targeting secure keyword-based access to encrypted data. By leveraging bilinear pairing for identity-based key management, the system enables flexible authentication and secure updates. Both text and image data are supported, with minimal computational overhead. Experimental results validate the feasibility of the approach in dynamic, resource-limited vehicular networks.

title: Benchmarking reproducible low-loss wire-bond interconnects for superconducting quantum computing
abstract: Abstract Reproducible low-loss microwave interconnects are essential for scaling modular superconducting quantum processors and networks. Wire bonds provide a simple and flexible route to galvanic connections in such systems, but their microwave loss and reproducibility at millikelvin temperatures remain insufficiently quantified. Here we demonstrate reproducible low-loss aluminum wire-bond interconnects in both superconducting cable resonators and planar tantalum resonators. In the cable devices, a wire-bond connection is placed at the midpoint of a high-quality resonator, where the different current distributions of odd and even modes separate connection-induced loss from intrinsic cable dissipation within the same device. Across devices fabricated with different bond numbers and ultrasonic powers, a stable bonding window yields no resolvable connection resistance above the practical resolution of order 0.1 m Ω . Measurements of planar resonators on two chips independently show no systematic degradation of the internal quality factor from wire-bond ground terminations within the device-to-device variation. These results establish aluminum wire bonding as a reproducible low-loss interconnect for superconducting microwave circuits, supporting the scalable assembly of modular superconducting quantum processors and networks.

title: Optimum design of steel columns for fire safety using swarm intelligence
abstract: Abstract The primary goal of this study is to demonstrate the calculation and optimisation of a compressed steel column in accordance with Eurocode standards without fire protection. A wide range of parametric calculations is performed, in which the column height and steel grade, as well as the compression force and fire‐resistant time, vary. Optimising for fire resistance over time demonstrates the value of safety and the relationship between mass and safety. To boost fire resistance, one needs to add more steel to the structure if fire protection is not used. Particle swarm optimisation (PSO) is a relatively novel and promising optimisation technique, which uses swarm intelligence to make the process more robust and reliable. This evolutionary strategy mimics avian social behaviour. The technique is tweaked to be more efficient in technical applications. It computes discrete optima, employs dynamic inertia reduction, and introduces craziness at certain particles.

title: ToCo-Mesh: Topology-Consistent Dynamic Mesh Reconstruction via Adaptive Tessellation and Surface-Aligned 2DGS
abstract: Reconstructing dynamic meshes with consistent topology from multi-view temporal images remains a challenge. Existing approaches typically face a dilemma between fine-scale shape recovery and topological stability. Frame-by-frame extraction methods capture fine details but break vertex correspondence, leading to flickering meshes. Conversely, template-based deformation ensures consistency but struggles to adapt its surface resolution during optimization, missing local surface details. To address these limitations, we propose ToCo-Mesh, a dynamic reconstruction framework that maintains topology consistency over time while achieving high-fidelity geometry. Specifically, we introduce a dual-mesh representation, where a canonical template mesh is tightly bound to time-varying coarse guide meshes via barycentric parameterization. While keeping guide meshes fixed to condition the deformation, we perform error-driven split-and-merge on the template mesh to progressively increase reconstruction fidelity. Furthermore, to suppress surface irregularities and achieve photorealistic rendering, we incorporate a Surface-Aligned 2DGS module. By anchoring flattened Gaussians to mesh faces, we utilize their rendered normals to guide inverse geometric fine-tuning. To our knowledge, ToCo-Mesh is the first framework to enable adaptive mesh refinement while maintaining strict topological consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves SOTA geometric accuracy while maintaining competitive rendering quality.

title: Variable Selection for Feature-Based Newsvendor
abstract: Feature-based newsvendor models use observable covariates to tailor inventory decisions, aiming to balance holding and shortage costs under demand uncertainty. However, high-dimensional feature sets often hinder interpretability and inflate data collection and implementation costs. This paper studies variable selection for the feature-based newsvendor problem under a hard cardinality constraint on the number of selected features. We formulate the resulting $\ell_0$-constrained empirical newsvendor problem with $\ell_2$-regularization, establish its computational hardness, and develop a mixed-integer second-order cone programming reformulation that strengthens the standard Big-$M$ formulation. To enable scalability beyond exact optimization, we develop a randomized-rounding algorithm with a bi-criteria guarantee and a greedy heuristic. Statistically, we provide theoretical analysis of the resulting sparse policy estimator, including finite-sample estimation error, out-of-sample risk bounds, and support recovery guarantees. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real data illustrate the computational and statistical trade-offs among various baselines. Our results demonstrate that the proposed variable selection framework achieves competitive out-of-sample operational costs while using substantially fewer covariates.

title: Completing or Refusing Low-Dimensional Records of Structured Quantum Circuits: Measurement Loss, Compression Loss, and Hardware Drift
abstract: Structured quantum circuits are often represented by low-dimensional records such as occupation numbers or constraint feasibility rather than by full outcome distributions. A record loses control-dependent information when it merges outcomes whose probabilities respond differently to circuit parameters. We assess this loss without assuming a parametric hardware-noise model. Quantum Fisher information bounds premeasurement sensitivity; Fisher metrics of measurements and recorded statistics describe device-attainable sensitivity. For finite control changes, a Hellinger residual measures the response removed by a record, while its local quadratic term is the conditional covariance of the full-outcome score. Simultaneous confidence bounds support approval, refusal, or deferral. We prove a finite-library completion theorem: executable augmentations terminate either with a record preserving every declared response or with proof that no library augmentation removes the loss. For an analytic control germ, integral closures characterize preservation along every analytic control arc, and finitely many Rees valuations detect failure. This connects the state--measurement--record chain to an executable completion-or-refusal procedure, an attainable-Fisher kernel criterion, and finite-sample decisions. A three-qubit calculation separates measurement loss from record loss. Prospectively fixed IBM Kingston and Marrakesh experiments test decisions in four-qubit fixed-particle-number and GHZ families, including negative controls. In two-epoch IQM Garnet data, median record-level drift is 0.0797 times full-distribution drift, but a significant residual remains in 35 of 36 settings. On these circuits, the rules detect loss and approve records only within stated tolerances; they do not establish universal compression performance or device quantum Fisher information.

title: VOIM: Training-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Instance Mapping for RGB-D and Monocular SLAM
abstract: We present Voxel-Grounded Online Instance Manager (VOIM), a training-free voxel-grounded instance manager that builds open-vocabulary 3D instance maps from RGB-D or from monocular RGB alone, a regime no prior training-free system addresses. Online systems typically segment object instances and label them at first detection, committing when evidence is weakest. VOIM instead defers label and instance decisions until soft evidence from unmodified, off-the-shelf perception has accumulated per voxel across views. We show that the mapping stage, rather than the particular perception models, carries the result: across four perception configurations on ScanNet++, varying the region descriptor, the detector label prior and the mask source, the map exceeds the strongest online RGB-D system, OVO-SLAM, by between 4.8 and 11.7 mIoU. Perception is not neutral, and substituting that baseline's own descriptor family costs 4.1 of the margin, yet the baseline carries the marginally better 2D descriptor (33.7 vs. 31.5 mIoU over three scenes) and still realizes the weaker map. Under a like-for-like protocol VOIM reaches 44.07 mIoU on ScanNet++ against 32.37, winning all ten scenes and both aggregations (pooled 33.31 vs. 25.97), and the same system runs unchanged to fully monocular RGB, matching that baseline pooled on Replica (27.80 vs. 27.50). The advantage is regime-specific: under Replica's all-classes scoring, matched inputs give a split result, 28.60 vs. 27.50 pooled against 24.59 vs. 30.11 on the per-scene mean. Room scale is label-limited and building scale drift-limited. Labeling does not run in real time, dominated by per-class detection over the full vocabulary. The maps export occupancy grids and resolve free-form queries to object instances.

title: Enabling Vulnerability Detection in RISC-V based Binaries through Lifting RISC-V ISA to LLVM
abstract: Binary analysis techniques are commonly used to identify security vulnerabilities in software. However, many established analysis tools rely on intermediate representations that are primarily designed for specific architectures or require dedicated front ends. The growing relevance of the RISC-V instruction set architecture therefore motivates the development of approaches that enable the analysis of RISC-V binaries using existing analysis infrastructures. This thesis investigates the lifting of RISC-V binaries to LLVM IR as a foundation for subsequent vulnerability detection. A prototype lifting pipeline was developed that processes RISC-V ELF binaries in multiple stages. First, executable code and function information are extracted from the input binary. The contained instructions are then identified using a custom decoder and transformed into an internal representation. Based on the decoded instructions, basic blocks and a control-flow graph are constructed. SSA form is subsequently generated using a dominator-based approach, including the placement of φ-nodes and variable renaming. Finally, the resulting repre­ sentation is translated into LLVM IR. The implementation focuses on the RV64I base instruction set and supports a selected subset of instructions identified through an analysis of representative compiled pro­grams. The generated LLVM IR was evaluated using several test programs and compared with the expected program structure and behavior. The results demonstrate that the implemented pipeline can successfully reconstruct control flow and translate supported RISC-V instructions into valid LLVM IR for the considered examples. The prototype also reveals limitations of the current approach, particularly regarding incomplete instruction coverage, indirect control-flow transfers, interprocedural analy­sis, and the simplified memory model. Consequently, the presented implementation does not perform vulnerability detection directly, but provides a basis for integrating RISC-V binaries into LLVM-based analysis frameworks. Future work can extend the instruction coverage, improve the modelling of memory and control flow, and connect the generated LLVM IR to established vulnerability detection techniques.

title: Interpreting Text-Enriched Dual-Head Multitask Learning for Indonesian Hateful Meme Detection Using Explainable AI
abstract: Internet memes in Indonesia are frequently weaponized to disseminate implicithate speech through sarcasm and cultural nuances. Automatically detectingsuch content is computationally challenging, and existing deep learningframeworks predominantly operate as opaque black boxes, lacking decisiontransparency. This study implements and optimizes a text-enriched dual-headmultitask learning architecture utilizing IndoBERTweet to concurrently classifyhatefulness and appropriateness within the INDOMEME dataset. Ratherthan processing raw image pixels, we employ a text-enrichment strategy wherevisual semantics are transcribed into textual descriptors via Optical CharacterRecognition and vision-language captioning. To bridge the interpretability gap,we deploy Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) to decodethe internal feature attributions of the architecture. Furthermore, advancedtraining optimizations, encompassing cosine annealing, gradient accumulation,class-weighted loss, and dynamic threshold calibration, were engineered toenhance model generalization. Experimental evaluations demonstrate thatthe optimized model achieves a Macro-F1 score of 0.812 for hatefulness and0.820 for appropriateness, surpassing the established baseline. Crucially, theLIME analysis unveils a pivotal finding: despite sharing an identical textualbackbone, the hate-specific head predominantly focuses on lexicons carryingsocial agitation, whereas the appropriateness head prioritizes general normviolations. These empirical findings substantiate that multitask learning enrichessemantic representation quality, offering a transparent framework fortrustworthy content moderation.

title: A Trusted Computing Framework for Intelligent Employment Recommendation of Industrial Talents Integrating Differential Privacy
abstract: Intelligent employment recommendation for industrial talent must process multi-source data − profiles, certificates, behavior logs, and company sources − yet existing methods emphasize accuracy over privacy and high-concurrency deployment. This study designs DP-TCERS, a differential-privacy trusted computing framework: it perturbs user/job features via local differential privacy and gradient noise against inference attacks, builds attention-fused towers for matching, scores trustworthiness from consistency and reliability, and lowers overhead via caching and parallel inference. Simulations show precision@10/recall@10/F1@10/NDCG@10 of 0.773/0.732/0.752/0.765 − below non-DP matching but above CF, NCF, DeepFM − with attack success rates falling to 0.198-0.231 and latency at 10,000 users reaching 294 ms versus 1,486 ms single-node.

title: On-Premise vs. Cloud: Local LLMs for Vulnerability Extraction from Security Scanner Reports
abstract: Cloud LLMs extract structured data from vulnerability-scanner reports accurately, but each report maps an organization’s attack surface, so routing it to a third-party API trades confidentiality for that accuracy. We evaluate nine local models (4B to 21B) against a DeepSeek cloud reference on three ground-truth baselines. The best local model, on a consumer GPU, trails the cloud by only 1.2 points in free-text fidelity and matches it on structured fields; the spread across local models far exceeds this gap, making model choice the decisive factor for private, on-premise extraction.

title: From Snapshot to Sequence: How Physical Bandwidth Shapes Sensory Modalities in Biological and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: I propose a layered AI architecture model grounded in a systematic analogy with the human nervous system, mapping the large language model (LLM), the agent, and specialized small models to the brain, the spinal cord, and the peripheral nerves / effector organs, respectively. Within this framework we introduce a Law of Sensory Differentiation: in the ideal information-theoretic limit, every sense is fundamentally an instantaneous spatial tensor that captures the full field at once. However, the absolute physical limits on medium properties and propagation velocity impose graded degradations: only vision preserves the ideal form (thanks to the high speed and low interaction cross-section of electromagnetic waves), audition is forced into a continuous time series, and olfaction collapses into a noisy turbulent sampling. We attribute this differentiation to a fundamental effective-bandwidth limit set by the physical and chemical channel: although the raw bit rates of the afferent fibers are of comparable order, the multipath effects of acoustic waves and the Brownian motion of odorant molecules consume most of the bandwidth on describing the channel's own fluctuations, so the bandwidth available to encode external spatial information is severely compressed. We further treat touch (hand / skin) as a special case forced to convert global spatial perception into temporal scanning by the physical sampling aperture (skin area), and illustrate it with the 'eyes-closed table' intuition experiment. At the structural level we argue that full-coupling (the LLM) and pruning (specialized small models) are not points on a spectrum but the necessary consequence of two unreconcilable design philosophies serving thinking versus execution. We further show that the pruning of specialized models is the natural result of a memory-consolidation dynamic, not a static hardware prior. The aim of this work is to provide an intuitive yet self-consistent theoretical reference for the modular design, controllability optimization, and multimodal integration of AI systems.

title: Opening the Black Box a Crack: A Critical Survey Review of Explainability and Interpretability of Black-Box Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Explainability and Interpretability of Black-Box Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of explainable AI and interpretability as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Quantum Information Encryption: A Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Based on Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper explores the design of a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance key security and improve key distribution efficiency. Traditional QKD protocols rely on static key generation, presenting vulnerabilities to potential eavesdropping. This research proposes a dynamic entanglement-based approach that introduces inherent security through the continuous alteration of quantum states. We detail the core mechanism, its advantages, and potential challenges associated with this new protocol. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications for future QKD systems, emphasizing the potential for enhanced security and efficiency.

title: ## Celebes Macaque-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Celebes Macaque Algorithm (CMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the critically endangered Celebes macaque. The algorithm leverages the macaque's unique social structure and exploration-exploitation strategy to address complex optimization challenges. CMA incorporates a population-based approach with a dynamic agent ranking and a novel adaptive mutation operator designed to mimic the macaque's efficient movement patterns within a foraging environment. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over existing metaheuristic methods, particularly in scenarios requiring robust exploration and exploitation. The core of CMA lies in the 'Social Hierarchy' and 'Adaptive Movement' components, represented mathematically as follows: Let *N* be the population size, *xi* represent the position of the *i*-th agent in the search space, *ri* represent the rank of the *i*-th agent based on fitness, and *μi* be the movement vector for the *i*-th agent. The Social Hierarchy is modeled by the rank update rule: *ri* = ∑j=1N *wj* *I(xj > xi)* where *wj* are weights assigned to each agent, and *I(condition)* is an indicator function equal to 1 if the condition is true and 0 otherwise. The Adaptive Movement is defined as: *μi* = *α* * (xi - xbest)* + *β* *ri* * (xbest - xworst)* where *α* and *β* are adaptive parameters controlling the exploration and exploitation phases, and *xbest* and *xworst* represent the best and worst fitness values in the population, respectively. The algorithm's performance is demonstrated through simulation results, showcasing its capability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time.

title: 基于量子纠缠的并行计算算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel parallel computing algorithm based on quantum entanglement. Traditional parallel computing methods often struggle to fully exploit the unique capabilities of quantum computers, and this research aims to achieve enhanced computational power through the strategic application of quantum entanglement. The core mechanism involves decomposing complex computational tasks into smaller, entangled sub-tasks, and leveraging the correlated nature of quantum systems to facilitate significantly faster and more efficient parallel computation. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's potential for improved performance compared to existing parallel computing paradigms. The core claim is that this algorithm offers a path towards unlocking the full potential of quantum computers.

title: Caracal: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Caracal Hunting Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Caracal, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting behavior of caracals, wild cats known for their strategic and adaptable hunting techniques. Caracal leverages elements of caracal's stalking, pouncing, and pursuit strategies to create a robust and efficient optimization process. The algorithm utilizes a novel exploration-exploitation balance mechanism, termed "Adaptive Stalking and Pounce" (ASP), which dynamically adjusts the search intensity based on the perceived level of convergence. Furthermore, Caracal incorporates a "Territorial Defense" mechanism to mitigate premature convergence and enhance the algorithm's ability to escape local optima. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive nature against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that Caracal exhibits superior performance in terms of solution quality and convergence speed for several challenging problems. Keywords: Metaheuristic, Optimization Algorithm, Caracal, Hunting Behavior, Adaptive Stalking and Pounce, Territorial Defense, Evolutionary Algorithm.

title: Cansdale's Swamp Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Swamp Rat Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Cansdale's Swamp Rat (CSR), inspired by the foraging behavior of swamp rats. These rodents are known for their efficient and adaptable foraging strategies within complex environments. CSR leverages key aspects of this behavior, including path exploration, resource prioritization, and adaptive movement patterns, to develop a robust optimization algorithm. The algorithm incorporates elements of simulated annealing, particle swarm optimization, and a novel "territory defense" mechanism to enhance exploration and exploitation capabilities. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations across a range of benchmark optimization problems. The core of CSR lies in its dynamically adjusted search space and the strategic allocation of computational resources based on perceived environmental complexity. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results indicate that CSR presents a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic methods, particularly in scenarios demanding adaptability and efficient exploration of large, complex search spaces. Further research will explore the algorithm's adaptability to diverse problem domains and its potential for integration with machine learning techniques.

title: Canary Shrew: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Scapanus carolinensis*
abstract: This paper presents Canary Shrew, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed for optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the foraging behavior of the canary shrew (*Scapanus carolinensis*), a small rodent known for its efficient and adaptive search strategies while seeking food resources. Canary Shrew employs a combination of adaptive step size adjustment, a novel exploration mechanism mimicking the shrew's territorial marking, and a dynamic population management system reflecting its resource allocation strategy. The algorithm's core components include a position vector representation, a fitness evaluation function, and a convergence criterion. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail these components. The algorithm's performance is demonstrated through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its effectiveness in achieving optimal or near-optimal solutions within a reasonable computational time. We aim to demonstrate that the observed behavior of the canary shrew can be effectively translated into a robust and adaptable metaheuristic algorithm.

title: 基于量子纠缠的概率计算框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic calculation framework predicated on the principles of quantum entanglement. We propose a system for analyzing complex systems by leveraging the dynamic nature of entangled states to simulate probabilistic processes and predict outcomes. The framework emphasizes the unique capabilities of quantum entanglement in providing a fundamentally different approach to probability assessment compared to traditional, classical methods. This research explores the potential of quantum entanglement to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of probabilistic modeling, offering a fundamentally new perspective on the limitations of classical probability calculations. The core mechanism involves the creation and manipulation of entangled states, followed by a sophisticated algorithm to extract meaningful predictions from these states. This work lays the groundwork for a more robust and potentially transformative approach to probabilistic analysis across a range of complex systems.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum-based geometric tensor learning approach leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement and superposition. This research explores the practical implications of this approach within the context of quantum algorithms and their application to various machine learning tasks. The investigation highlights the potential of quantum entanglement and superposition to fundamentally alter the landscape of quantum machine learning.

title: Probability Logic Matrix for Adaptive Geometric Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic geometric optimization algorithm based on probability logic matrices. Traditional geometric optimization techniques often rely on manually defined parameters, limiting flexibility and potentially hindering the exploration of complex shapes. This paper proposes a framework where a probability logic matrix dynamically adjusts optimization parameters to achieve optimal results across diverse geometric forms. The core mechanism utilizes probabilistic guidance to navigate away from local optima and enhance the adaptation of solutions to complex shapes. This approach offers improved robustness, adaptability, and potential for more efficient material design and robot control. The presented algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in optimization quality compared to existing methods, particularly in handling intricate geometries.

title: Geometric Data Compression and Acceleration via Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Geometric data, encompassing complex geometric shapes and their associated properties, represents a significant challenge in various fields, from computer graphics and scientific visualization to data analysis and pattern recognition. Traditional data compression techniques often struggle to effectively handle the inherent complexities of geometric data, leading to limitations in compression ratios and computational efficiency. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to revolutionize geometric data compression and acceleration. We introduce a novel algorithm, Quantum Geometric Compression (QGC), that utilizes entanglement to efficiently transfer and manipulate geometric data, resulting in significantly improved compression ratios and accelerated geometric computations. The core mechanism centers on exploiting the correlated properties of entangled qubits to represent and manipulate geometric data in a fundamentally different manner than conventional methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QGC through extensive experimental analysis, showcasing substantial compression gains and speedups in key geometric operations. The research contributes to a paradigm shift in data compression and computation, paving the way for more efficient and robust geometric processing.

title: Quantum Entanglement Communication Protocol: Adaptive Information Propagation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental quantum phenomenon, offers the potential for instantaneous and secure communication. This paper introduces a novel quantum communication protocol predicated on the dynamic adjustment of information transmission rates and quality, leveraging quantum entanglement's inherent self-adaptability. We explore a system that proactively modulates entanglement properties to optimize communication fidelity and resilience in the face of environmental fluctuations. Our analysis demonstrates the protocol's ability to achieve significant improvements in key communication metrics through adaptive information management. This research emphasizes the potential of self-adaptive entanglement-based communication to revolutionize quantum communication.
