title: Formal Modeling of Collective Intelligence via Agent-Based Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a formal mathematical model of collective intelligence (CI) developed using agent-based simulation (ABS). The core challenge in understanding CI lies in its emergent nature within distributed systems. This work addresses this challenge by constructing a model that explicitly incorporates key mechanisms – communication, learning, and reputation building – among a population of autonomous agents. The model is built upon a discrete-time framework, utilizing mathematical notation to represent agent states, interactions, and the evolution of collective behavior. We define key variables such as agent influence, knowledge levels, and reputation scores, and formulate equations governing their dynamic changes. The primary contribution is a rigorous mathematical framework enabling the systematic study and simulation of CI emergence. The model allows for the investigation of various parameters and configurations to identify conditions conducive to intelligent collective action. The research provides a novel approach to formally analyzing and predicting CI behavior, offering potential insights for designing and optimizing distributed systems exhibiting CI characteristics. The model is parameterized for a variety of agent interaction scenarios.

title: Deep Learning Analysis of Drug Reviews: Identifying Patient Conditions, Predicting Drug Ratings, and Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Understanding patients' experiences with medications is essential for improving drug effectiveness, detecting potential side effects, and enhancing overall patient satisfaction. This research investigates applying machine learning to patient drug reviews across three main tasks: Identifying patient conditions, predicting drug ratings, and performing sentiment analysis. We implemented and evaluated Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) using a large dataset of patient reviews collected from reputable medical platforms. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score for classification tasks, Mean Squared Error (MSE), and coefficient of determination (R²) for rating prediction. For patient condition identification, the RNN achieved the highest accuracy of 96.50%, followed by the ANN (96.30%) and CNN (95.80%). In the drug rating prediction task, the CNN outperformed the other models, achieving an MSE of 0.0296 and an R² of 0.9692. For sentiment classification, the RNN achieved the best performance with an accuracy of 94.82%. Cross-validation results demonstrated the robustness and stability of all models, with standard deviations below 0.3%. The findings indicate that deep learning models can effectively extract meaningful insights from unstructured patient-generated reviews. Moreover, the results suggest that model effectiveness is task-dependent: RNNs excel at tasks that require sequential text understanding, such as condition identification and sentiment classification, while CNNs perform better at predicting drug ratings through efficient local feature extraction.

abstract: Network intrusion detection for the Internet of Things increasingly relies on deep-learning classifiers, yet their reported adversarial robustness rests on an untested networking assumption: that a feature-space perturbation corresponds to a packet or flow an attacker can actually transmit on the wire. We propose PAVE (Protocol-Validity-Aware Evaluation), a framework that judges robustness at the realizable network artifact (CAN frames, MQTT packets, IP flows) rather than the normalized feature tensor, coupling a protocol-space validity test, a gradient-masking audit, and seventeen imbalance-aware metrics with corrected paired tests over three IoT datasets, five architectures, and six defenses. PAVE revises standard conclusions: adversarial examples produced by standard unconstrained continuous feature-space attacks (FGSM, PGD, Square) retain only 0%–3% validity in protocol space, so most of the vulnerability these attacks report cannot occur on the wire (enforcing validity shows that unconstrained evaluation overstates the MCC degradation of a Transformer under FGSM by 0.18–0.20: 0.39 vs. 0.56 and 0.30 vs. 0.50 on two benchmarks, i.e. a measurement of evaluation bias, not a defense); its imbalance-aware gradient-masking audit screens for majority-class collapse, a risk we observe for an untuned defense configuration and which principled penalty tuning resolves; and two of three common benchmarks are saturated or leakage-prone (CICIoV2024 reduces to ≈ 3 . 6 k unique flows from 1.4M). Among low-cost defenses, a feature-space Mahalanobis detector gives strong non-adaptive separation (PR-AUC ≈ 1 . 0 , FPR@95%TPR ≈ 0 ), though it degrades under an adaptive attacker, which PAVE recommends as a complement to, not a replacement for, adversarial training. PAVE provides a realizability-grounded protocol and a more accurate estimate of adversarial risk for IoT intrusion detection.

title: g-vamp: Improving sequence labelling frameworks for multiword expressions identification
abstract: Annotated corpora such as the parseme collection frequently contain Multiword Expressions ( mwe s) that share tokens within a sentence, meaning that a single token may belong to two or more mwe s. This phenomenon is widespread across languages and poses a significant challenge for machine learning models that rely on standard sequence-labelling formulations. Token sharing increases training complexity and often leads to systematic prediction errors. As a result, most existing approaches resolve these conflicts by retaining only one of the overlapping mwe s and discarding the others, which entails substantial information loss and can be particularly detrimental in low-resource settings. This paper introduces g-vamp (Generate Variants and Merge Predictions), a general framework that enables mwe identification systems to handle token sharing without discarding annotated expressions or relying on complex encodings. g-vamp operates by generating multiple variants of the training corpus in which token-sharing conflicts are eliminated in a controlled manner. A Transformer-based model is trained independently on each variant, and the resulting predictions are subsequently merged to recover mwe s that involve shared tokens at inference time. We evaluate g-vamp on version 1.3 of the parseme multilingual corpus, covering 26 languages with diverse structural and typological characteristics. The results show that g-vamp consistently improves over a strong baseline in 24 languages and surpasses state-of-the-art systems in 16 languages, despite relying exclusively on a single multilingual Transformer model and no language-specific linguistic resources. These findings demonstrate that controlled corpus diversification constitutes an effective and language-agnostic strategy for addressing token sharing in mwe identification.

title: Document-level relation extraction via self-correcting prompt optimization and preference alignment
abstract: Document-level relation extraction (DocRE) finds relations across a whole document. It often needs evidence from several sentences. It also needs to link repeated entity mentions and follow multi-hop clues. Many large language model (LLM) based DocRE methods use fixed relation descriptions. They make little use of confident errors or samples with missing labels. We propose SPO-PA, which combines self-correcting prompt optimization (SPO) and preference alignment (PA). SPO compares LLM predictions with reference annotations. It then revises relation descriptions, clarifies relation boundaries, and adds role constraints. PA uses false negative (FN) conflicts as the main supervision signal. It also tests false positive (FP) conflicts under similar constraints. PA applies source-specific constraints to these signals. The constraints help smaller DocRE models separate correct relations from wrong candidates. On Re-DocRED, SPO improves F1 to 26.23% and Precision to 41.93%. It also achieves 37.60% F1 on HacRED. Both are the best LLM-only scores in our comparison and reproduce on a second, more recent backbone, though both stay far below supervised encoders; the extraction stage supplies conflict signals rather than final predictions. Among the PA variants, $$\text {PA}_{FN}$$ gives the most stable gains on ATLOP, KD-DocRE, DREEAM, and DAATF. The largest gain is 2.89%.

title: RAFT-DVC: Resolution-Aware Machine Learning-Based Digital Volume Correlation
abstract: Digital volume correlation (DVC) provides three-dimensional full-field displacement measurements from volumetric images, but how the internal resolution of a machine-learning-based DVC model affects accuracy and operating range remains poorly understood. Here, we present RAFT-DVC, a resolution-aware family of recurrent all-pairs field transforms (RAFT)-based DVC solvers with encoder downsampling factors s = 2, 4, and 8. Using a matched design, we find that the three solvers localize displacement to approximately 0.017 feature-grid voxel, giving an empirical raw-volume error scaling of approximately 0.017s voxel. The solvers exhibit complementary operating regimes governed jointly by displacement reach and volumetric-texture compatibility. Synthetic benchmarks show that RAFT-DVC achieves errors of the same order as tuned classical DVC under fine-texture, small-to-moderate-displacement conditions and becomes competitive or advantageous under coarse-texture, large-displacement conditions. Frequency-swept tests quantify deformation spatial resolution, while tiled inference enables dense estimation on large volumes. Evaluation on confocal volumetric images acquired during indentation illustrates the importance of matching solver operating regime to deformation magnitude and image texture. Tests on micro-CT images of elastomeric foam, despite training only on particle-labeled synthetic data, provide evidence of cross-texture transfer. We also identify coordinate-order inconsistencies in three-dimensional RAFT correlation sampling and introduce a non-cubic impulse test to verify sampler geometry independently of network training. Correcting the sampler improves native-input accuracy and generalization to unseen volume dimensions. Together, these results establish RAFT-DVC as a fast, resolution-aware framework for dense DVC with characterized accuracy and operating regimes.

title: Quantum Sparse Autoencoders for Q-Matrix Estimation in Cognitive Diagnosis
abstract: Q-matrices play a central role in cognitive diagnosis within educational data mining (EDM), specifying which latent skills each assessment item requires. Data-driven Q-matrix estimation remains challenging when assessments involve many correlated skills and when real response patterns depart from idealized generative assumptions. We introduce a novel quantum sparse autoencoder (QSAE) for Q-matrix estimation, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first application of quantum machine learning (QML) to cognitive diagnosis. Overall, the QSAE embeds each student's binary response vector into a quantum circuit using an encoder, compresses it into a sparse latent representation, and maps that representation to the Q-matrix. We benchmark the QSAE against a classical autoencoder (CAE) across 60 simulated datasets and 9 real-world assessment datasets. The results reveal complementary strengths. Although the CAE partially achieves higher average accuracy under several simulation conditions, the QSAE is substantially more stable across replications, exhibiting lower variance in 49 of the 60 conditions. Moreover, on real assessment data, the QSAE outperforms the CAE on 6 of the 9 datasets. These findings suggest that the principal advancement of QML in this setting is not universal accuracy improvement, but enhanced robustness and capability to explore latent-structure complexity in real datasets.

title: A Network Science Perspective on Evaluating Deep Graph Generative Models
abstract: Traditional network models from network science, such as the Erdos-Renyi and configuration models, generate random networks that reproduce few selected topological properties observed in real-world networks. Deep graph generative models emerge as a data-driven approach, leveraging deep neural network architectures to learn complex structural distributions directly from real-world networks to generate more realistic synthetic networks. Because real social contact networks cannot be shared due to privacy risks, synthetic networks serve as an alternative for developing and evaluating epidemic mitigation strategies. In this work, we evaluate deep graph generative models as well as the configuration from a network science perspective by assessing both the topological similarity between generated and real-world networks and their utility in identifying effective node immunization strategies to sup- press epidemic/misinformation spreading. It is found that two deep graph generative models produce synthetic networks that closely resemble the structural properties of real-world networks, enabling them to identify effective immunization strategies.

title: Hybrid VQE-CVQE algorithm using diabatic state preparation
abstract: Abstract We propose a hybrid variational quantum algorithm that has variational parameters used by both the quantum circuit and the subsequent classical optimization. Similar to the variational quantum eigensolver, this algorithm applies a parameterized unitary operator to the qubit register. We generate this operator using diabatic state preparation. The quantum measurement results then inform the classical optimization procedure used by the cascaded variational quantum eigensolver. We demonstrate the algorithm on a system of interacting electrons and show how it can be used on long-term error-corrected as well as short-term intermediate-scale quantum computers. Our simulations performed on IBM Brisbane produced energies well within chemical accuracy.

title: Evaluating the Robustness of Small Language Models in Portuguese under Red Teaming with Linguistic Perturbations
abstract: Small Language Models are increasingly deployed in resource-constrained settings, yet their safety behavior under linguistic perturbations remains underexplored for Brazilian Portuguese. This work evaluates three open-box Small Language Models (SLMs), Llama 3.2 3B Instruct, Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct, and TucanoBR Tucano-2b4, against 480 adversarial prompts spanning six risk categories, each subjected to five character-level perturbations at three intensity levels, totaling 1,440 model runs. An automated pipeline, using Phi-4-mini-instruct as judge model, measures Objective Satisfaction Rate (OSR), Unsafe Compliance Rate (UCR), Intent Understanding Rate (IUR), and Noise Failure Rate (NFR) to separate genuine safety from refusals caused by incomprehension. Overall unsafe compliance was low across all models (0.42% – 2.71%), with TucanoBR exhibiting the highest UCR despite strong intent understanding, while heavy corruption degraded comprehension rather than eliciting unsafe outputs. Our findings indicate that literal pattern-matching filters are insufficient safeguards against surface-level adversarial evasion.

title: SUN'IY INTELLEKT ASOSIDA AXBOROT TIZIMLARIDA MA'LUMOTLARNI QAYTA ISHLASH SAMARADORLIGINI OSHIRISH
abstract: Ushbu maqolada axborot tizimlarida katta hajmdagi ma'lumotlarni qayta ishlash samaradorligini oshirishda sun'iy intellekt va mashinaviy o'qitish texnologiyalaridan foydalanish masalalari tadqiq etilgan. Zamonaviy axborot tizimlarida ma'lumotlar hajmining tez sur'atlarda ortib borishi ularni yig'ish, tozalash, tasniflash, tahlil qilish va prognozlash jarayonlariga qo'yiladigan talablarni kuchaytirmoqda. An'anaviy deterministik algoritmlar ma'lum turdagi masalalarda yuqori samaradorlikni ta'minlasa-da, katta hajmdagi, murakkab va o'zgaruvchan ma'lumotlar bilan ishlashda ularning imkoniyatlari cheklanishi mumkin. Tadqiqotda ma'lumotlarni qayta ishlashning an'anaviy va sun'iy intellektga asoslangan yondashuvlari tahlil qilinib, AI komponentlarini axborot tizimining ma'lumotlar oqimiga integratsiya qilish modeli taklif etiladi. Shuningdek, ma'lumotlarni oldindan qayta ishlash, xususiyatlarni ajratib olish, klassifikatsiya qilish va natijalarni baholash bosqichlari ko'rib chiqilgan. Python dasturlash tilida mashinaviy o'qitish modelini amalga oshirish namunasi keltirilgan. Samaradorlikni baholash uchun bajarilish vaqti, aniqlik, xotira sarfi va F1-mezon kabi ko'rsatkichlardan foydalanish taklif etilgan. Tadqiqot natijalari sun'iy intellekt texnologiyalarini axborot tizimlariga to'g'ri integratsiya qilish ma'lumotlarni qayta ishlash jarayonlarini avtomatlashtirish va qaror qabul qilish sifatini oshirish imkonini berishini ko'rsatadi.

title: Borrowing Knowledge Across Tasks: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Transfer Learning and the Pretraining Paradigm
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Transfer Learning and the Pretraining Paradigm in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of transfer learning and pretraining as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Dynamic Dependency Graph Computation Semantic Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to analyzing the semantic information of program execution by focusing on dynamic dependency graphs (DDGs). The core idea is that the structure and characteristics of DDGs can provide a rich source of information about how a program behaves during its execution. We propose a method to construct DDGs, capturing dependencies between variables as they change during program execution. Subsequently, we apply computational semantic analysis techniques, including abstract interpretation and program reasoning, to these DDGs. This analysis aims to uncover deeper insights into the program's semantics. The primary contribution lies in the synergistic combination of DDGs and computational semantic analysis, enabling a more precise and comprehensive understanding of program execution semantics compared to traditional approaches. The paper outlines the key components of this framework and suggests potential future research directions.

title: Cape York Rock Wallaby-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CYRWMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Cape York Rock Wallaby-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CYRWMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm motivated by the unique foraging behavior of the Cape York Rock Wallaby. These wallabies exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food resources in a complex and dynamic environment. CYRWMA leverages this behavior through a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework. The core innovation lies in incorporating a 'memory' component inspired by the wallabies' spatial memory and their tendency to revisit previously successful locations. This memory is represented as a probabilistic distribution over the search space, influencing the movement and update rules of the particles. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high solution quality and convergence speed. The algorithm's parameters are tuned to mimic the wallabies' foraging strategies, resulting in a robust and adaptable optimization method. title: Quantum Entanglement Adaptive Topology Networks
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a revolutionary approach to quantum information processing, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical communication. This paper explores the design of a novel quantum entanglement network utilizing adaptive topology to optimize quantum state transmission and manipulation. We propose a dynamic architecture based on entangled pairs, where the network topology adjusts to maintain entanglement fidelity and robustness. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to automatically reconfigure the network's structure, enhancing data transfer efficiency and security. This work introduces a framework for creating robust quantum networks capable of dynamically adapting to complex environments, promising significant advancements in quantum information technologies.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology of Computational Landscapes
abstract: The optimization of complex systems, particularly those involving computational algorithms, often encounters challenges due to the inherent difficulty of finding optimal solutions. Traditional optimization methods frequently operate on static landscapes, potentially limiting the effectiveness of subsequent algorithms. This research proposes a novel adaptive topology system, designed to continuously optimize the computational landscape, thereby facilitating more efficient search spaces for various algorithms. We introduce a 'gradient-based topology adjustment' mechanism, dynamically modifying the landscape's structure to guide search algorithms toward better solutions. This system leverages feedback from optimization process to refine the landscape's topology, resulting in improved convergence and performance across a range of problem domains. This work offers a fundamental shift in how computational landscapes are shaped, promising to enhance the performance of optimization algorithms across diverse applications.

title: Nonlinear Geometric Topology for Machine Learning Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-linear geometric topology to machine learning optimization. Traditional optimization techniques often rely on local optimization strategies, which may struggle to effectively adapt to evolving data landscapes. We propose a novel framework that leverages non-linear geometric transformations to dynamically adjust model parameters, fostering improved model adaptability and robustness. The core mechanism hinges on automatically generating and applying geometric transformations to the model's parameters, allowing the system to explore a wider range of parameter spaces and better handle complex data variations. This approach addresses limitations of current optimization methods by offering a fundamentally different perspective on parameter space exploration, leading to enhanced model performance and adaptability. We present a theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments demonstrating the effectiveness of this framework in optimizing various machine learning models, highlighting its potential for advancements in data-driven problem-solving.

title: Probability Geometric Optimization for High-Dimensional Chaos Systems
abstract: This paper explores the application of probability geometric optimization techniques to the challenging problem of optimizing high-dimensional chaos systems. Traditional optimization methods often rely on locally optimal solutions, limiting their ability to discover novel solutions. We propose a novel approach that leverages probability geometric principles to reduce the search space and enhance the exploration of chaotic systems. The core mechanism involves incorporating probabilistic distributions into the optimization process, specifically focusing on parameter adjustment to minimize the likelihood of getting stuck in local optima. This research aims to provide a more robust and potentially insightful method for understanding and controlling the behavior of high-dimensional chaotic systems, offering a departure from conventional optimization strategies.

title: Brooks' Dayak Fruit Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of a Fruit Bat
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Brooks' Dayak Fruit Bat" (BDB), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Dayak fruit bat ( *Pteropus medius* ). Fruit bats are renowned for their efficient and adaptive search strategies when locating fruit sources in complex environments. The algorithm leverages these observed behaviors – including target selection, flight path optimization, and social interaction – to develop a robust and effective optimization technique. BDB employs a population-based approach with a novel adaptation mechanism for adjusting the exploration-exploitation balance. Specifically, the algorithm uses a "fruit attraction" mechanism, mirroring the bat's tendency to gravitate towards areas with higher fruit density, combined with a "social learning" component, mimicking the bats' collaborative foraging. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The key innovation lies in the dynamically adjusting attraction strength and the incorporation of a cooperative learning component to enhance the search efficiency. The algorithm's design provides a flexible framework that can be adapted to various problem types. The results presented here showcase the potential of bio-inspired algorithms in addressing complex optimization challenges.

title: Blue Fox: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Blue Fox Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Blue Fox, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of blue foxes. The algorithm leverages the blue fox's strategic hunting techniques, including ambush, pursuit, and territorial defense, to construct a novel search process. Blue Fox employs a dynamic territory system, an adaptive movement strategy based on perceived threats and resource availability, and a competition mechanism mimicking territorial disputes. The algorithm's core components involve a population of potential solutions, a territory representation, a movement strategy governed by a risk-reward function, and a competition mechanism. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the territory update rules, the movement probability calculations, and the competition dynamics. Simulation results demonstrate that Blue Fox achieves competitive performance across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its effectiveness and potential for future research. Keywords: Metaheuristic, Optimization, Blue Fox, Artificial Intelligence, Evolutionary Algorithm, Territory System, Risk-Reward.

title: Algorithmic Quantum Error Mitigation via Wavefunction Reconstruction
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise, but its susceptibility to errors presents a significant challenge. Traditional error correction techniques struggle with the inherent complexity of quantum systems. This paper proposes a novel algorithmic quantum error mitigation strategy centered around wavefunction reconstruction, a dynamic adaptation process that actively compensates for errors as they are detected. We introduce a method that iteratively reconstructs the quantum state, utilizing a sophisticated dynamic parameter adjustment based on the quantum system's evolving dynamics. This approach offers improved resilience compared to existing methods, potentially achieving greater error correction rates with a more efficient resource utilization. The core mechanism hinges on a continuous, adaptive process of wavefunction reconstruction, minimizing the impact of errors without requiring extensive overhead.

title: joshaku: token-set acceptance for lens readouts, fixed before any run (v1.2.0)
abstract: joshaku (jōshaku, "a fixed standard length") fixes the word-to-token-id mapping used by rank and mass readouts of language-model residual streams (logit lens, tuned lens, Jacobian lens) before any measurement is taken. One acceptance predicate: a surface variant of a word is accepted only if the tokenizer encodes it as exactly one token; every rejected variant is registered; ranks are computed inside a declared word-like pool and an id outside the pool is an error, not a number; undecidable results are None, never False. The package (seven modules in three layers: library, acceptance, inspection) implements the frozen specification SPEC_tokenset_acceptance v1.2 (md5 e95f4661…, included) and ships its contract test suite (20 tests; positive controls named in the README) and the instrument fingerprint (combined md5 89b194be… of the seven modules). It was built during the token-set defect repair registered as REVISION-ID TSD-20260826 and is the instrument named in the revision notes of the CommitStage, FaithfulProse and FidelityEight records; this record holds the instrument only, so that the three notes cite one fingerprint. MIT license.

title: Efficient Jailbreaking Attack via Experience Reuse and Coordinated Optimization
authors: CHEN Jingze, WANG Hongjie, DU Yanhui, LI Wenjin, YOU Yang
abstract: With the widespread adoption of large language models, their security vulnerabilities have become increasingly evident. Adversarial jailbreaking attacks, such as those based on the greedy coordinate gradient (GCG) method, can bypass safety alignment mechanisms and induce models to generate harmful content, serving as a key benchmark for security evaluation. However, GCG??s inherent inefficiency stemming from two main bottlenecks, namely “cold starts” that require reinitialization for each attack and “slow convergence” due to single-point optimization severely limits its practicality. To address these issues, this paper proposes an efficient jailbreaking framework that integrates experience reuse with collaborative optimization. For the “cold start” problem, an experience reuse framework is introduced: by truncating the optimization objective, transferable attack experiences are generated and stored in a suffix library, enabling efficient “warm starts” through selection of the best historical experience for new tasks. To mitigate “slow convergence”, a multi-point collaborative optimization mechanism is developed, which explores combinations of elite modification sets within a single iteration to enable parallel, coordinated updates that overcome the limitations of single-point search. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with GCG, the proposed method maintains an average attack success rate of 88% across multiple large language models while reducing attack time by 90%, demonstrating substantial efficiency gains. This approach provides a faster and more practical benchmark tool for security evaluation and supports the development of more robust safety alignment techniques.

title: Regression Analysis with Type-1 Fuzzy Functions and Feature Selection Methods
abstract: Real-world regression problems often involve noise, redundancy, multicollinearity, and nonlinear relationships that limit the effectiveness of classical models. This study investigates Type-1 Fuzzy Functions (T1FF) combined with several feature selection strategies, with particular emphasis on the integration of Lasso regression into the T1FF framework, which has not been directly examined in prior research. By incorporating Fuzzy C-Means-based membership degrees into the modelling process, T1FF provides a flexible way to capture uncertainty and nonlinear structure without relying on expert-defined fuzzy rules. The proposed framework was evaluated on six datasets, namely Boston, Auto, College, Steel Fatigue Strength, Fish Price, and Smart Pressure Control, using RMSE and MAPE as performance criteria. The results show that T1FF-based models generally outperform classical LM, Ridge, and Lasso models on most datasets, although the best-performing T1FF variant varied depending on dataset characteristics. In particular, the Lasso-based T1FF model yielded competitive results overall and achieved especially strong performance on the College and Fish Price datasets, while Full and Forward T1FF methods showed the most consistent MAPE-based ranking across datasets. Overall, the findings indicate that integrating feature selection and regularization methods into the T1FF framework provides a promising and flexible approach for regression modelling on complex real-world data.

title: Delay-embedded optical injection for enhanced photonic reservoir computing
abstract: Next generation reservoir computing (NGRC) replaces recurrent network evolution with delay coordinate features and nonlinear expansion, but these operations are usually constructed digitally. Here, we investigate delay-embedded optical injection for enhanced photonic reservoir computing (DEOI-PRC), in which the input signal modulated on a master laser is divided into multiple optical paths with different propagation delays and injected into a single reservoir laser. In this way, the reservoir laser is driven simultaneously by the current input and delayed versions of the same input, while the nonlinear response of its output optical field provides the reservoir states used for readout. This architecture uses distinct injection delays to physically supply the current and historical input states required for NGRC inspired processing. On the Santa Fe chaotic time series prediction task, DEOI-PRC improves prediction accuracy relative to conventional time-delay reservoir computing (TDRC) after parameter optimization. The optimized distribution gives the largest injection share to the shortest delay path, which carries the most recent input information, while the longer delay paths introduce historical components. DEOI-PRC broadens the low error parameter region and reduces the number of virtual nodes required for accurate prediction, supporting a compact physical implementation of photonic NGRC.

title: CT-Based Lung Cancer Detection Using Hybrid Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches
abstract: Globally, cancer kills a large portion of people, and early detection is necessary to offer a better prognosis. The orthodox modes of diagnosis- like biopsy and computed tomography- are not only expensive, requiring expert technicians, but ultimately time-consuming. In their turn, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) are promising to automate clinical analysis, including cancer detection. This paper proposes a classification of lung cancer that is trained on a collection of 9000 images divided into benign, malignant, and normal categories. Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) is a feature extraction technique, and image segmentation perfects the detection process. Classic machine learning techniques—such as Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Gaussian Naive Bayes—achieve classification accuracies of 96%, 68%, and 47%, respectively. Convolutional neural networks (CNN), DenseNet, and ResNet are then applied as deep-learning models to achieve a better performance; those results are 98 %, 87 %, and 82 % respectively. As can be seen in these findings, the Random Forest algorithm performed with an accuracy of 96 % whereas CNN, DenseNet, and ResNet performed with accuracies of 98 %, 87 %, 82 %, respectively.

title: Reinforcement Learning Driven Identification, Segregation and Disassembly of Medical Tubes for Sustainable Plastic Reuse
abstract: Autonomous robotic systems operating in real-world environments must make decisions under perception uncertainty, delayed actuation, and strict real-time constraints, yet most reinforcement learning (RL) methods assume fully observable and synchronous dynamics.We study these challenges in the context of high-frequency robotic sorting, formulating pneumatic object segregation as a latency-constrained Partially Observable Markov decision process (POMDP) in which noisy visual observations must be mapped to timecritical actions under delayed feedback.A previously underexplored regime in RL consists of a simulation-driven framework that integrates deep visual localisation, RL based pneumatic control, and stochastic object dynamics, allowing for RL behaviour analysis in unpredictable scenarios.The environment models perception latency, actuation timing uncertainty, and variable object transitions, creating a realistic test bed for studying RL behaviour in industrial embodied systems.Our study makes three contributions: (1) we formulate real time sorting as latency-constrained sequential control problem under partial observability; (2) we introduce a paradigm where detection relies on actuation and control policies of reinforcement learning; and (3) we provide comparative insight into how onpolicy and entropy regularised RL methods behave in this regime.Experimental results show that SAC's entropy-driven exploration improves adaptation but amplifies timing-sensitive errors while PPO produces more stable and temporally consistent policies better suited to deterministic embedded deployment.We further show that perception errors propagate nonlinearly into control decisions, reinforcing suboptimal action mappings and exposing a fundamental limitation of modular perception-control pipelines.

title: Unsupervised machine learning–driven REE prospectivity mapping across the Purulia Shear zone, eastern India
abstract: North and South Purulia Shear Zones (NPSZ–SPSZ) form a paired deformation belt that hosts Rare Earth Element (REE) mineralization within Chhotanagpur Granite Gneissic Complex (CGGC) and Singhbhum Craton (SC) of eastern India. This belt is characterized by carbonatite–apatite–magnetite systems, yet large parts of the belt remain unexplored due to complex structural overprints, deep weathering and limited surface exposure. Therefore, in this study, an attempt is made to delineate REE mineralization across NPSZ-SPSZ areas of eastern India based on unsupervised machine learning methods combining geological, geophysical, geochemical and remote-sensing evidential layers. Two clustering algorithms namely K-means and self-organizing maps (SOM) were developed to derive prospectivity models from the evidential layers. Prospective/mineralized clusters were extracted based on spatial associations with 22 known REE occurrences and available geological knowledge. title: Low-latency deep learning framework for real-time conventional Pap smear cytology using YOLO-based instance segmentation
abstract: Abstract Purpose Compact YOLOv11 nano/small variants were trained on public cervical cytology datasets, harmonized via Bethesda labeling for cells and nuclei at high resolution. Models performed joint detection and segmentation, assessed by mAP, recall, and F1-score per category. Real-time use was tested on video from CMOS cameras on a microscope, tracking inference time and frame rate. Methods Compact YOLOv11 nano and small variants were trained on public cervical cytology images. These datasets were aligned using a unified Bethesda labeling scheme for whole cells and nuclei at high resolution. The models were trained for joint box detection and segmentation, and their results were assessed via mAP, recall, and F1-score for each Bethesda category. The real-time use of the models was tested by deploying them on video streams from low-cost CMOS cameras on a microscope, recording the per-frame inference time and frame rate. Results The YOLOv11 small model achieved high mAP and recall for both bounding-box and mask predictions across Bethesda classes while maintaining low latency for real-time applications. Inference on microscope video sequences showed frame rates above the 25 fps threshold for real-time performance, even under tough conditions with overlapping cells and complex inflammatory or hemorrhagic backgrounds. Conclusion These findings suggest that lightweight YOLOv11-based models can offer fast and reliable analysis of conventional Pap smears directly at the microscope, which can support the development of affordable, point-of-care computer-assisted screening tools for cervical cancer, notably in low- and middle-income countries where access to liquid-based cytology and whole-slide scanners is limited.

title: Epistemic Sybil Resistance: Multiplying AI Agents Without Multiplying Evidence
abstract: Multi-agent AI systems improve inference by spawning agents and synthesizing reports. But another agent is not another observation: apparently independent reports may descend from the same evidence, and genuinely independent evidence can produce nearly identical reports. We formalize this as an epistemic Sybil problem. A report Z is an epistemic Sybil extension relative to reports R when I(Theta; Z | R) = 0. No report-only aggregator can generally distinguish replication from independent corroboration: identical reports can warrant different posteriors under unobserved ancestry. A Gaussian shared-root model shows common ancestry does not imply complete redundancy. Repeated extraction adds information toward a source-level ceiling, and correlated extraction errors, which a shared base model can induce among independent agents, lower that ceiling further. We test these predictions with more than 20,000 controlled LLM-agent report and extraction calls on synthetic evidentiary documents. Holding one evidence root fixed while report multiplicity rises from 1 to 32 collapses naive posterior coverage from 0.940 to 0.263. Holding report count fixed while evidence-root multiplicity rises from 1 to 16 closes the gap, and the aggregators are statistically indistinguishable at k = 16. The agent's replicate extraction errors are correlated (gamma_cal = 0.719, estimated out of sample), and a correlated-extraction aggregator restores calibration accordingly. A controlled manipulation isolates representation similarity from evidential ancestry. It changes a report-space deduplication mechanism's mean inferred cluster count by 1.425 (95% CI [1.363, 1.485]), whereas a fourfold change in true ancestry changes it by only 0.040 ([-0.045, 0.120]). Collective inference should therefore track evidential ancestry and dependence, not agent or report multiplicity or similarity.

title: Can LLMs Design Video Coding Tools? A Case Study on Planar Mode
abstract: This paper explores whether large language models (LLMs) can design video coding tools, a highly challenging task due to the intricate algorithmic coupling of tool modifications. In particular, we present an empirical case study on the Planar mode, a long-standing intra prediction tool in video coding standards. Our experiments operate within a generation-and-evaluation loop, with the LLM generating new Planar predictors, encoder trials evaluating their coding performance, and the LLM re-generating refined implementations based on the evaluation feedback. We first examine directly replacing the default Planar mode in the Fraunhofer Versatile Video Encoder (VVenC) under its faster preset. Experimental results demonstrate that the LLM-generated mode can outperform the conventional Planar mode on this lightweight toolset, achieving 0.18% bitrate savings with 0.4% complexity overhead on the standard benchmark. We further extend our evaluation to the Enhanced Compression Model (ECM). Leveraging newly introduced directional Planar modes, we investigate two integration strategies: directly replacing them, and introducing the LLM-generated predictor as an additional prediction mode with new syntax elements. The empirical results suggest that both strategies can yield coding gains under a constrained low-resolution setting. Overall, this study offers preliminary evidence and practical insights, highlighting both the potential and open challenges of LLM-based coding tool design.

title: Quantum time-flip beats adaptive metrology: Asymptotic benefit, activation, and unsimulability
abstract: In quantum metrology, adaptive and causal-superposition strategies are proven to be beneficial over parallel schemes for a finite number of channel uses, but their advantages disappear in the asymptotic limit. We show that quantum operations with indefinite time direction, specifically, time-flip (TF)-assisted strategies, referred to as indefinite time-directed metrology (ITDM), can overcome this asymptotic equivalence. Using semidefinite programming, we rigorously demonstrate that TF-assisted protocols can achieve quantum Fisher information (QFI) strictly exceeding the maximum value attainable by parallel, adaptive, and causal-superposition strategies, both for finite and asymptotically many channel uses. Moreover, we identify a class of Pauli noise channels for which ITDM achieves Heisenberg scaling, while all parallel, adaptive, and causal-superposition strategies remain restricted to standard scaling. We call this phenomenon as metrological activation. Interestingly, this activation can be used to exhibit that the quantum time-flip and transposition supermaps cannot be simulated by conventional quantum circuits or causal-superposition strategies using any finite number of channel queries, thereby establishing indefinite time direction as a genuine resource for quantum metrology.

title: Low-Quality Face Recognition using Center Aligned Representations and Local Margin Constraints
abstract: Low-quality face recognition (LQFR) remains challenging due to the difficulty of matching degraded query (probe) images against low-quality (LQ) enrollment (gallery) imagery and the scarcity of training data for large-scale models. While recent face recognition (FR) models perform well on high-quality (HQ) imagery, their accuracy drops significantly on LQ images with extremely low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Moreover, fine-tuning HQ-pretrained models on LQ data often improves LQ recognition at the expense of HQ generalization. This trade-off becomes more pronounced in modern evaluation settings spanning multiple datasets with varying image quality levels. To address these limitations, we propose a unified framework that combines three main components: (1) Local Probability Margin (LPM), which estimates per-sample difficulty directly from the model's discriminative landscape; (2) Nested Attention Module (NAM), a new low-rank adapter module that embeds a self-attention mechanism within selected transformer layers; and (3) Quality Gating Protocol (QGP), where an off-the-shelf image quality estimator modulates the adapter contribution at test time, enabling a single model to handle the full quality spectrum without sacrificing HQ performance. Experiments on surveillance (TinyFace, SurvFace) and standard (IJB-B, IJB-C) face recognition benchmarks demonstrate consistent gains in both identification and verification. Code and models will be released at github.com/candllq/nam.

title: SoK: Motion Data Privacy in Extended Reality
abstract: Extended Reality (XR) provides immersive, interactive 3D experiences. To enable these experiences, the devices must track user motion so the system can respond to actions such as grabbing, looking at, or moving an object. However, motion tracking has raised privacy concerns since it records a person's motion patterns. These motion patterns have been studied extensively across various fields (i.e., gait identification and profiling) and have been shown to reveal sensitive information. With the adoption of XR, these patterns became easier to record and obtain than ever. This creates a fundamental privacy tension: motion tracking enables core XR functionality yet requires users to compromise their privacy. Prior systematization-of-knowledge (SoK) studies on XR privacy have examined the field broadly, with motion-related research distributed across several privacy domains rather than treated as a distinct area of study. However, XR motion privacy has gained significant momentum since the prior SoK, with the literature nearly quadrupling in size and thereby warranting a dedicated systematization of this topic. This SoK examines 134 relevant papers on privacy concerns in motion patterns recorded by XR headsets, including how adversaries can obtain users' motion patterns, the inferences they can draw from them, and methods for protecting users. Based on this review, we synthesize a taxonomy of motion modalities, representations, and inference risks; develop an XR motion threat model; systematize the attack and defense approaches in the XR motion literature; identify gaps in the literature; and provide guidelines for future studies evaluating motion privacy mechanisms. Together, our SoK clarifies the state of XR motion privacy and provides recommendations for future evaluations.

title: Potential-Guided Particle Steering for Negation-Constrained Dexterous Grasping
abstract: Language-driven dexterous grasp models, such as DextER, perform well when instructions specify where to grasp, but we find they fail systematically when an instruction also specifies where not to grasp (e.g., "grasp the handle but avoid the body"). Existing training corpora, DexGYSNet among them, contain virtually no avoidance instructions, and collecting examples for every possible constraint is impractical. Moreover, because every part mentioned during training denotes a contact target, models may interpret a forbidden part as another region to grasp rather than one to avoid. We therefore introduce an inference-time framework for negation-constrained dexterous grasping that requires no negation-specific training examples. Combining Sequential Monte Carlo with classifier-free guidance, our method guides sampling toward the instructed part while pruning candidates headed for the forbidden region, without any negation examples during training. A frozen 3D part-grounding model localizes the forbidden region from the language instruction. To evaluate this setting, we construct NegGrasp, a benchmark of paired positive/negative instructions with constraint-aware metrics that credit a grasp only if it both accomplishes the task and respects the stated constraint. On NegGrasp, our method reduces the violation rate of the strongest baseline from 57.9% to 17.2% while improving both constraint-aware and physical success.

title: AI-POWERED MARKETING ANALYTICS AND CUSTOMER MANAGEMENT
abstract: With the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the marketing tactics are developing at a significant rate. The AI has significantly transformed the way of marketing in the ultra modern era by allowing the businesses to understand their customer needs and analyzing the customer needs while making effective marketing decisions. With the large availability of the customer data, the AI Powered marketing analytics enables the organization to identify the consumer preferences, predict their behavior, personalizing the marketing tactics and customer engagement. While there is a huge development in the modern marketing sector, there is also a decline in the trust of the modern customers. The increasing use of AI has raised concerns in the marketing field related to data privacy, trust and transparency. This research paper titled “AI POWERED MARKETING ANALYTICS AND CUSTOMER MANAGEMENT” examines the role of AI in analyzing the customer behavior and preferences, and the role in shaping modern marketing techniques and effective customer management. The study focuses on how AI is used in analyzing the customer data, targeted and personalized marketing, consumer loyalty and privacy. This study also aims to understand how the customer perceives the increasing use of AI in targeted advertising and ethical use of their data. The study adopts a quantitative research approach using the primary data collected through a structured questionnaire. The collected data will be analyzed to know the perception of the customers in relate to the development of AI in marketing field, and to understand the relationship between AI powered marketing analytics and customer management. The study is expected to provide the perspectives of customers about how AI is used to perform targeted advertisements by analyzing the customers past data to predict the future outcomes, while maintaining the customer trust and ethical usage of their data. The findings may help the organizations and marketers to understand the views of customers and the opportunities and challenges associated with AI for maintaining sustainable growth in marketing analytics and customer management.

title: The Replay Tax: auditing the privacy cost of continual-learning strategies in object detection — per-image attack scores, splits, buffers and analysis code
abstract: This archive is the replication package for a membership-inference audit of continual-learning strategies in object detection. Six training arms (naive, no adaptation, joint, replay, elastic weight consolidation, learning without forgetting) are evaluated across two datasets and two detector architectures with three seeds each, under three adversaries of increasing realism: a loss threshold, a difficulty-calibrated attack against a reference model, and a label-free attack that observes only detection confidences. The primary cell additionally carries a likelihood-ratio attack with 32 shadow models. The archive contains the per-image attack scores for every arm, seed and cell; the member, non-member, control and validation-fitting split listings; the exact buffer contents for every buffer size and seed; per-arm utility measurements; the likelihood-ratio scores and shadow-membership tables; and all analysis code, including the scripts that generate every table and figure in the paper. The images themselves are not redistributed. Both corpora are third-party public research datasets (a weapon-detection corpus on Roboflow Universe and the Teledyne FLIR Free ADAS Thermal Dataset), and the archive supplies the file lists needed to reconstruct our exact splits from them. The replay buffers are additionally reproducible from their seed alone. A verification script, independent of the analysis code, recomputes every headline number in the paper from the raw per-image scores and reports 37 of 37 claims reproduced. It runs on CPU in about a minute and needs no images and no GPU. The package distinguishes throughout between two buffer constructions, because they give different answers: an audit buffer drawn from the audited member set, and a deployment buffer drawn from the whole first task with no reference to the audit. Arms of the second kind are tagged replayU.

title: Cariri Climbing Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Climbing Behavior of the Cariri Climbing Mouse
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Cariri Climbing Mouse (CCM) algorithm, inspired by the unique climbing behavior of the Cariri climbing mouse ( *Aecomys cariri*). This rodent species exhibits a remarkable ability to navigate steep, often vertical, rock faces with minimal effort. The CCM algorithm leverages this natural adaptation to develop a novel search strategy. The core of the algorithm revolves around a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating a 'climbing' mechanism that dynamically adjusts particle velocities based on the slope of the objective function landscape. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a stochastic gradient descent-like approach to determine the direction and magnitude of particle movements, aiming to efficiently explore and converge towards optimal solutions. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional PSO and other established metaheuristics in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The key innovation lies in the adaptive velocity update rule, which mimics the mouse's strategic use of small, incremental movements to overcome obstacles. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be easily tunable, allowing for flexibility in adapting it to different problem domains. Future research will focus on incorporating elements of the mouse's sensory perception – specifically its ability to detect subtle variations in texture – into the algorithm to further enhance its performance.

The core of the algorithm revolves around a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating a 'climbing' mechanism that dynamically adjusts particle velocities based on the slope of the objective function landscape. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a stochastic gradient descent-like approach to determine the direction and magnitude of particle movements, aiming to efficiently explore and converge towards optimal solutions. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional PSO and other established metaheuristics in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The key innovation lies in the adaptive velocity update rule, which mimics the mouse's strategic use of small, incremental movements to overcome obstacles. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be easily tunable, allowing for flexibility in adapting it to different problem domains. title: Camiguin Bullimus: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bullfighting Tradition
abstract: This paper presents Camiguin Bullimus, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the traditional Spanish bullfighting ritual. The algorithm leverages the strategic movements and adaptive behaviors of the bull and matador to establish a robust search strategy. Camiguin Bullimus combines elements of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms, incorporating a novel 'Territory Defense' mechanism mimicking a bull's protective instincts and a 'Dynamic Adaptation' component reflecting the matador's tactical adjustments. The algorithm's core components include a population of candidate solutions (particles), a fitness function representing the objective function, and a dynamic adjustment strategy based on the concept of territory defense and adaptability. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's key operations, including velocity update equations, inertia weight adjustment, and the territory defense mechanism. Simulation results on benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that Camiguin Bullimus exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence speed, solution quality, and computational efficiency. Future research directions are discussed, including the exploration of different parameter settings and the integration of the algorithm with machine learning techniques.

title: Self-Organizing Neural Network Evolution Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm designed to optimize the structure and parameters of neural networks, focusing on enhancing their self-organization capabilities and generalization ability. The algorithm leverages genetic algorithms to iteratively refine network configurations, promoting a dynamic and adaptable system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing improved performance in complex, non-linear scenarios. The core mechanism involves continuous adaptation of network architecture and weights based on a fitness function that incentivizes self-organization. This results in networks that exhibit robust and flexible behavior. The study highlights the potential of evolutionary algorithms to overcome limitations of traditional optimization methods, offering a promising pathway for advanced neural network design.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement for Hyperdense Network Communication
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement for revolutionizing network communication, specifically within the context of hyperdense networks. Traditional communication networks face limitations due to bandwidth constraints and security vulnerabilities inherent in classical information transfer. This research posits that leveraging quantum entanglement offers a pathway to overcome these challenges. The core concept involves generating and distributing cryptographic keys using entangled quantum states, thereby facilitating high-efficiency key transmission. We detail the theoretical framework, outlining the key components and protocols involved. The primary focus is on demonstrating how the inherent properties of quantum entanglement – specifically, the instantaneous correlation between entangled particles – can be exploited to establish secure and high-capacity communication links within a dense network environment. The research emphasizes the potential for significantly increased bandwidth and enhanced security compared to existing technologies. We examine the challenges and potential solutions associated with realizing this vision, including the complexities of maintaining entanglement over long distances and scaling the system to accommodate a large number of nodes. Ultimately, this work advocates for a paradigm shift in network communication, driven by the fundamental principles of quantum mechanics.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的动态图论模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed Dynamic Graph Theory (DGT), that leverages the principles of dynamic graph theory to enhance the learning and optimization capabilities of neural networks. The core concept is to represent neural network nodes and connections as nodes and edges within a dynamic graph, allowing for continuous and adaptive adjustment of network structure through a learned graph transformation process. The proposed model aims to overcome limitations of traditional neural network design by offering improved adaptability, generalization, and performance through dynamic structural optimization. We present a comprehensive framework incorporating a novel graph transformation algorithm and a dynamic adjustment mechanism based on graph connectivity and node attributes. The paper details the implementation of the DGT model, demonstrating its effectiveness through experimental results on benchmark datasets. The resulting model exhibits superior performance in complex tasks compared to established neural network architectures.

title: Quantum State Vector Reconstruction with Adaptive Compression
abstract: Quantum state vector reconstruction is a fundamental challenge in quantum information processing, crucial for tasks like quantum state estimation and quantum error correction. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent redundancy present in quantum states, leading to high storage and communication costs. This paper introduces a novel quantum state vector reconstruction algorithm, Quantum State Vector Reconstruction with Adaptive Compression, designed to intelligently compress the state vector by identifying and eliminating redundant information. The algorithm leverages quantum state representations to pinpoint these redundancies and reconstruct the state vector with a significantly reduced size. This approach promises substantial improvements in storage and transmission efficiency, particularly for large quantum states.

title: Hyperdimensional Entanglement Dynamics
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of hyperdimensional entanglement, exploring a novel algorithm for dynamically mapping and manipulating high-dimensional entanglement states. The core claim is that a 'quantum state gradient' mechanism, iteratively refining entanglement relationships through subtle geometry and energy adjustments, allows for unprecedented precision in controlling quantum correlations across complex systems. We present a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the potential for this approach to surpass existing entanglement analysis techniques. The research focuses on modeling and controlling entanglement within high-dimensional spaces, specifically leveraging the concept of a 'quantum state gradient' to achieve fine-grained control over correlations.

title: Bolivian River Dolphin Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "River Dolphin Navigation Algorithm" (RDNA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bolivian river dolphin (Inia geoffrensis). These dolphins utilize a unique, collaborative navigation strategy in murky river waters, exhibiting remarkable efficiency in locating prey. RDNA leverages the core principles of this behavior – cooperative exploration, information sharing, and adaptive adjustment – to solve complex optimization problems. The algorithm employs a population of agents, each simulating a dolphin, navigating a search space. Agent interactions are governed by a 'communication' mechanism mimicking the dolphins' sonar-based information exchange. Adaptive adjustment is modeled through a dynamically adjusted movement strategy based on local search results and global population trends. We demonstrate the effectiveness of RDNA on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results indicate that RDNA performs competitively against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in high-dimensional and complex landscapes. The algorithm's key components, including the communication protocol and adaptive movement strategy, are thoroughly described, and its performance is analyzed. Future research directions include exploring the algorithm's applicability to real-world engineering and scientific optimization challenges.

title: Self-Adaptive Topology for Quantum Computation – Based on Topological Quantum Computation
abstract: Quantum computation offers unprecedented computational power, but its implementation faces significant challenges due to the fragility of quantum states. Self-adaptive topology is a promising approach to enhance the robustness and scalability of quantum systems. This paper explores the application of self-adaptive topology to quantum computation, focusing on the design of a novel quantum algorithm that leverages the unique properties of topological quantum states. We present a framework for modeling complex topological structures, utilizing quantum topological properties to construct a tailored quantum algorithm for solving problems with intricate topological landscapes. The core mechanism centers around the strategic manipulation of quantum states to mimic and exploit topological constraints, leading to enhanced computational capabilities. This work demonstrates the potential of self-adaptive topology to unlock new avenues in quantum algorithm design and offer solutions for tackling computationally challenging problems.

title: Jincheng Zhang
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to matrix computation leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. We propose a method that transforms matrix operations into a sequence of non-linear quantum operations, guided by the inherent properties of entangled states. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the non-linearity inherent in entangled quantum states to generate a fundamentally different computational paradigm. The study explores the potential of this technique for advancing quantum algorithms and offering a pathway to novel quantum computations. This paper provides a detailed mathematical framework for the proposed method and discusses its implications for quantum information processing.

title: Machine Intuition
abstract: Can an artificial intelligence system select the right action before it can articulate a valid reason for that action? Addressing this question at the intersection of reasoning, interpretability, agent safety, and latent computation, we develop a non-anthropomorphic definition of machine intuition as pre-explanatory competence: an action-relevant internal state that is sufficiently informative and causally involved to support a correct decision before a faithful natural-language explanation is available. Synthesizing evidence from chain-of-thought prompting, faithfulness interventions, hidden-state probing, activation steering, mechanistic interpretability, and latent-reasoning systems through 8 August 2026, we note that while final answers and tool-use choices can sometimes be decoded from activations before explicit reasoning begins, difficult multi-step problems are often solved during the generated reasoning trace itself - making token-level deliberation computationally consequential rather than merely explanatory. To separate these regimes, we introduce the Action-Explanation Timing (AET) framework and MINT-Eval, a causal evaluation protocol that distinguishes the earliest causally validated action state from the earliest sufficient, faithful, and interventionally supported explanation, while categorizing faithful latent competence, opaque success, rationalized error, and genuinely deliberative reasoning. The resulting answer is qualified: AI can sometimes act correctly before explaining why, but correctness alone does not establish human-like intuition or trustworthy reasoning; because the same timing gap can arise from useful latent computation, learned heuristics, shortcut features, or post-hoc rationalization, explanations must be treated as evidence to test rather than automatic proof of process, requiring high-consequence actions to undergo external verification, authority controls, and causal audits even when the model's first move is right.

title: PENGEMBANGAN SISTEM INFORMASI E-VOTING BERBASIS WEB UNTUK PEMILIHAN KETUA KARANG TARUNA SEMARANG SELATAN DENGAN PENERAPAN KEAMANAN DATA MENGGUNAKAN METODE HASHING
abstract: The election of the South Semarang Youth Organization (Karang Taruna) Chairperson is a democratic organizational process that plays a crucial role in leadership renewal. However, conventional election methods relying on paper ballots face several challenges, such as limited member access, operational costs, the risk of counting errors (human error), and lengthy vote tabulation processes. This study aims to develop a web-based e-voting information system for the South Semarang Youth Organization Chairperson election, incorporating the SHA-256 hashing method as a security mechanism for vote data. The research employs a Research and Development (R&D) methodology using a mixed-methods approach and the Waterfall development model, comprising stages for requirements analysis, design, implementation, testing, and evaluation. The system is designed to manage user authentication, voter and candidate data, the voting process, data storage, and automated result tabulation. Applying the SHA-256 algorithm to vote data generates a hash value acting as a digital fingerprint, which preserves data integrity and detects alterations through the avalanche effect mechanism. Research findings indicate that the system enhances the efficiency and transparency of the election process. An analysis of tabulation times reveals that the manual method takes approximately 110 minutes, whereas the e-voting system requires only 2–3 minutes, achieving a time efficiency rate of 97.27%. Consequently, the developed system offers a faster, more accurate, secure, and transparent election solution while supporting the digitalization of the youth organization's electoral processes.

title: An Ontological Approach to Designing a Microservice Architecture
abstract: Abstract Despite the widespread use of microservice architecture in the development of software systems, there is no formalized approach that ensures the consistent and guaranteed interaction of microservices at the level of transmitted data, which leads to errors in integration and complicates the maintenance of distributed systems. The purpose of this study is to develop an approach to the organization of interaction of microservices based on ontological modeling, providing formalization of data structures and automated validation of messages. The paper presents a method for converting formal descriptions of data schemas into ontological models based on the GraphQL schema specification. This method allows the data validation process to be automated and the number of integration errors to be reduced. An ontological model has been developed that provides an analysis of dependencies between microservices and a mechanism for validating message contracts. The practical significance of the work lies in achieving a consistent description of microservices, operations, and message formats as a result of using an ontological approach. The representation of the ontology in the form of a graph makes it possible to analyze the dependencies between microservices and simplifies the maintenance of large distributed systems.

title: A lightweight model for modulation recognition of integrated underwater acoustic sensing and communication signals
abstract: Under the stringent resource constraints of underwater edge nodes and the severe impairments of underwater acoustic channels, automatic modulation recognition of integrated underwater acoustic sensing and communication signals (UISAC) remains challenging, especially when both lightweight deployment and robust performance are required. To address this issue, we propose Mixer, an ultra-lightweight network that combines signal enhancement with efficient feature representation. First, the impulsive-noise preprocessing and adaptive spectral block suppress impulsive noise and selectively enhance informative frequency subbands. Second, spatial density functions are coupled with complex-valued convolutions to capture local signal patterns and amplitude-phase coupling in the received signal. Third, the DWMG backbone integrates grouped depthwise-separable convolutions with an MLP-Mixer to efficiently fuse local and global features with low computational overhead. Experimental results under standard, generalization, and robustness evaluation settings show that Mixer remains competitive in the low-signal-to-noise ratio regime and provides a favorable balance between lightweight design and recognition performance. Compared with ULCNN, Mixer reduces the parameter count by 46.96%, and its single-sample CPU inference latency is 18.5 ms, demonstrating its potential for real-time deployment on UISAC edge nodes.

title: Bidirectional controlled quantum teleportation of two-qubit states via an eight-qubit entangled channel
abstract: Abstract Using an eight-qubit entangled state as the quantum channel, we propose a novel bidirectional controlled quantum teleportation scheme involving three participants: a controller, Charlie, and two communicators, Alice and Bob. Alice can teleport an arbitrary two-qubit target entangled state to Bob, while Bob simultaneously teleports another two-qubit entangled target state back to Alice conditional on Charlie’s authorization and assistance. Compared with some existing schemes, the proposed scheme achieves higher intrinsic efficiency with lower operation complexity. Moreover, this scheme is practically feasible with currently available quantum technologies.

title: Lexical diversity and translation literalness in machine translation: a comparative study of pretrained, fine-tuned, and few-shot approaches
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a comparative study of neural machine translation (MT) models and large language models, emphasizing translation literalness, lexical diversity, and translation quality. We evaluate open-source neural machine translation (NMT) models, LLaMa 3.1 Instruct, and GPT-4o across nine language pairs in pretrained, fine-tuned, and few-shot prompting settings. This comprehensive analysis underscores the differential strengths of each model, contributing valuable insights into their respective utility in MT. Our findings in the literary and news domains show that fine-tuning reduces translation literalness, allowing freer translations across models, most strongly for LLaMa, which produces the least literal translations across domains. The effect of fine-tuning on lexical diversity is model-dependent: it decreases consistently for LLaMa but remains stable or is improved for NMT. Few-shot prompting, on the other hand, enhances GPT-4o’s lexical diversity across domains and significantly boosts its translation quality in the literary domain, yielding the highest overall COMET scores. Furthermore, our correlation analysis reveals a distinct domain effect: literary translation evaluation rewards diversity, whereas news translation evaluation favors literalness. Overall, the results highlight complementary strengths: few-shot GPT-4o for high-quality, lexically rich translations with low error rates, and fine-tuned LLaMa for freer, less literal translations.

title: Systematic assessment of text summarization methods for biomedical literature from frequency methods to language models
abstract: The rapid expansion of biomedical literature demands automated summarization tools that reliably condense research articles into concise, accurate summaries. We benchmarked 62 summarization methods, ranging from frequency-based and TextRank extractors to encoder-decoder models (EDMs) and large language models (LLMs), on 1,000 biomedical abstracts from 20 journals across ScienceDirect and Cell Press , using author-written highlights as reference summaries. Models were evaluated with a composite suite of lexical, semantic, and factual metrics, including ROUGE, BLEU, METEOR, embedding-based similarity, and factuality scores. General-purpose models (e.g., Mistral, GPT, and Llama) achieved the highest overall performance across lexical and semantic dimensions, outperforming reasoning-oriented (e.g., DeepSeek and Magistral) and domain-specific (e.g., BioGPT and BioMistral) models. Notably, medium-sized models outperformed large-scale models, suggesting an optimal balance between model capacity and efficiency, while classical extractive methods lagged behind neural approaches. These findings provide a systematic reference for selecting biomedical summarization tools and highlight that broad pretraining outperforms narrow domain adaptation.
