title: A bibliometric and thematic evolution analysis of artificial intelligence in online customer experience
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has played an increasingly important role in e-commerce, especially when it comes to its impact on customer experience (CX). In this regard, the paper presents a bibliometric analysis of studies dedicated to the application of AI technology and online CX, based on 257 Scopus-indexed works produced in 2015–2024. The analysis is conducted through Biblioshiny and VOSviewer and involves investigation of publication dynamics, top authors and journals, co-authorship network, keywords co-occurrence, as well as thematic evolution. According to the results, there has been a sharp rise in AI-CX research since 2018. The country-level analysis showed that India and the United States were among the most productive contributors, while the Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services emerged as the leading journal within the retrieved dataset. As for thematic trends, chatbots, recommendation systems, personalization, and predictive analytics dominate the sphere. At the same time, the findings reveal a shift from effectiveness-based usage of AI to more customer-oriented applications.

title: On the BUFF security of ECDSA with key recovery
abstract: Abstract In the usual syntax of digital signatures, the verification algorithm takes a verification key in addition to a signature and a message, whereas in ECDSA with key recovery, which is used in Ethereum, no verification key is input to the verification algorithm. Instead, a verification key is recovered from a signature and a message. In this paper, we explore the BUFF security of ECDSA with key recovery (KR-ECDSA), where BUFF stands for Beyond UnForgeability Features [7]. As a result, we show that KR-ECDSA provides BUFF security, except weak non-resignability (wNR). It is particularly noteworthy that the KR-ECDSA verification algorithm takes an Ethereum address $$\textsf{addr}$$ addr as input. This address is defined as the rightmost 160 bits of the Keccak-256 hash of the corresponding ECDSA verification key. Crucially, the algorithm verifies that the hash of the recovered verification key matches $$\textsf{addr}$$ addr . Our security analysis shows that the procedure, namely checking whether the hash value of the recovered verification key matches the address, is essential for achieving provide BUFF security. We also discuss whether wNR is mandatory in Ethereum or not. To clarify which part is mandatory to provide BUFF security in KR-ECDSA, we show that the original ECDSA does not provide any BUFF security. As a by-product of the analysis, we show that one of our BUFF attacks also works against Aumayr et al.’s ECDSA-based adaptor signature scheme [2] and Qin et al.’s blind adaptor signature scheme [35], which is based on Aumayr et al.’s scheme. We emphasize that the attack lies outside their security models.

title: Latent unified smooth Hamiltonians for excited state chemistry
abstract: We describe a neural network architecture and training procedure designed to model electronic ground and excited states of arbitrary molecular systems. By indirectly learning a latent, implicit basis representation of the electronic-state Hamiltonian, the model offers a unified treatment of multiple electronic states, conical intersections, and non-adiabatic couplings. The formalism can be further extended to learn consistent latent representations of additional operators such as transition dipole moments, for example. To demonstrate the general capabilities of our architecture, we train and evaluate networks on two realistic photochemical systems, thymine and azobenzene. The resulting models accurately reproduce energies and oscillator strengths for the ground- and low-lying excited states relevant to the photochemistry of these systems. We highlight the performance of the trained networks by studying critical molecular geometries, including conical intersections and excited state minima. By construction, the proposed framework also recovers the emergence of Berry phase accumulation around conical intersections. By pairing key mathematical structure from quantum chemistry with the representation learning power of transformers, the presented architecture offers a qualitatively new path toward fast and accurate ground- and excited-state simulations.

title: Tri-Band Channel Measurement-Enabled Multi-Layer Digital Twin for Terahertz Wireless Data Centers
abstract: The rapid growth of AI computing has driven increasing demands for flexible and high-capacity data-center interconnections. Owing to its ultra-wide bandwidth and high spatial reuse capability, terahertz (THz) communication has emerged as a promising solution for future wireless data centers, while digital twins (DTs) enable efficient wireless planning and real-time optimization. In this work, a measurement-driven multi-layer DT framework is proposed for THz wireless data centers, where the physical, channel, evaluation, and manipulation layers are progressively constructed from bottom to top. First, extensive channel measurements are conducted at 140, 220, and 300 GHz to characterize frequency-dependent propagation behaviors. Based on the tri-band measurements, a measurement-calibrated physical twin is established by jointly optimizing the geometry, material, antenna, and hybrid propagation models. On top of the physical twin, a line-of-sight (LoS)-aware implicit neural field is developed to construct an AI channel twin for efficient channel reconstruction. The proposed AI twin learns location-dependent channel statistics from the calibrated twin, enabling real-time prediction of received power and LoS probability. Building upon the reconstructed channel field, a system-level evaluation layer is derived to analyze coverage and interference for both AP-to-rack and rack-to-rack communications. Experimental results show that the proposed AI twin achieves lower power reconstruction error than existing neural-field baselines while maintaining real-time inference capability. Moreover, the ceiling-mounted AP deployment achieves over 90% coverage under a 10 dB signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) threshold, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed DT framework for THz wireless data-center planning and optimization.

title: What Does an Agentic Software Engineering Benchmark Measure? Profiling Task Demands and Agent Behaviour Beyond What Category Labels Reveal
abstract: Agentic software engineering benchmarks are typically summarized by nominal category labels such as "bug fix" or "feature implementation," yet benchmarks carrying the same label are built through very different curation pipelines. A label thus reveals little about the engineering work a benchmark demands. We introduce the Spread--Novelty--Centrality (SNC) profile, a three-axis characterization of the demands of repository-level coding tasks, grounded in empirical software engineering research. We apply the profile to five widely used benchmarks and 14,922 trajectories of two model families at three scales, and report three findings. (1) A label is an unreliable proxy for task demands, as every pair of benchmarks is statistically separated on at least two SNC axes, and the separations trace back to specific curation decisions. (2) Agent behaviour reveals demands that the human-written gold solution cannot. Agents produce larger solutions than the gold where problem statements withhold hints and smaller ones where curation inflates the gold. How a task is phrased shapes what an agent produces. (3) Task demands correlate with success uniformly, with resolved runs concentrating in the low-SNC region for every family and scale, whereas the behavioural signatures of success are family-specific. Claude succeeds by matching the scope of the gold solution, and its parity share on files rises from $0.17$ at the smallest scale to $0.54$ at the largest. Qwen succeeds by exceeding the gold scope at every scale, and editing too little marks failure for both families.

title: Figures as Programs: Recursive Generation of Editable Scientific Figures
abstract: Scientific methodology figures are essential for communicating complex methods clearly, yet creating them remains labor-intensive and typically requires multiple rounds of refinement. Recent image-generation models can synthesize visually appealing raster figures, but producing a human-satisfactory result in a single generation step remains difficult. Moreover, precise edits to raster figures are challenging for both humans and models. We formulate scientific figure generation as recursive SVG program construction and propose \textsc{FigTree}, a \textit{multi-agent} system that automatically transforms a scientific paper into a structured vector figure. \textsc{FigTree} grounds figure content in the source paper, decomposes a figure into a hierarchy of local regions, generates each region as a short SVG program, and assembles the resulting fragments. A render-critic refinement loop jointly inspects the rendered figure and its underlying program, enabling visual defects to be traced to specific statements and accurately repaired. We conduct extensive evaluations of \textsc{FigTree} on figure quality and editability, showing that \textsc{FigTree} produces high-quality figures, while also enabling more effective editing than existing raster-based methods.

title: Manifold-Aware General Coded Computing for Straggler-Resilient Distributed Computing
abstract: Existing coded-computing designs do not explicitly exploit the intrinsic structure of the input data. In communication systems, statistical structure and redundancy are often removed through source coding (or compression) before channel coding is applied. This principle, however, does not transfer directly to coded computation. In many computational tasks, particularly in machine learning, the structure of the data is precisely what the computation seeks to exploit to infer outputs or learn meaningful patterns. Consequently, coded-computing schemes should preserve and leverage this structure in their code design, rather than ignoring or eliminating it through source coding. This observation motivates a different perspective on code construction. In many channel-coding schemes, such as Reed-Solomon codes, coded symbols are generated by evaluating a low-dimensional algebraic representation at selected points. In contrast, many high-dimensional datasets naturally concentrate near low-dimensional manifolds. In this paper, we exploit this intrinsic geometry by designing coded samples that follow the natural manifold of the data, rather than imposing an artificial low-dimensional structure unrelated to the data distribution. Inspired by graph-based manifold learning, we propose a manifold-aware encoding strategy for general coded computing (GCC). Experiments on neural network inference and high-dimensional polynomial evaluation demonstrate that the proposed strategy consistently and significantly reduces the mean squared recovery error under straggling compared with standard GCC.

title: Imaginarity witnessing enhancement via spectral norms of witnesses
abstract: Quantum imaginarity is an essential physical resource that underpins key functionalities of modern quantum technologies. We improve imaginarity witnessing via the prior knowledge of imaginarity-witness operators. To this end, we derive a rigorous upper bound on the maximum expectation value of an imaginarity witness operator over the set of all free (real) quantum states, which is given by the spectral norm of the real component of the corresponding witness operator. We demonstrate via detailed examples that this bound substantially improves imaginarity detection. We further classify all imaginarity-witness operators into four distinct families based on this bound. For these four witness classes, we perform a comprehensive analysis of their completeness and finite completeness, the joint detection of shared imaginary quantum states by different witnesses, and the conditions for distinct witnesses to identify identical imaginary states. Our results advance the fundamental understanding of imaginarity detection and offer useful insights for both theoretical studies and experimental implementations of quantum imaginarity.

title: Gate Teleportation vs. Circuit Cutting in Distributed Quantum Computing
abstract: ABSTRACT While distributed quantum computation has primarily utilized circuit cutting, it incurs an exponential growth of sub‐circuit sampling and classical post‐processing overhead with an increasing number of cuts. In contrast, entanglement‐based gate teleportation avoids exponential sampling overhead but requires high‐fidelity quantum interconnects. We model noisy remote (teleported) gates between superconducting qubits entangled via noisy microwave‐to‐optical (M2O) transducers over optical links. We incorporate the effect of the transducer noise added () on the Bell pair state preparation circuit and inject noisy Bell pairs into remote CNOT gates. We perform comparative simulation of Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) states generated between processor modules using remote gates and gate cuts and study the dependence of the Hellinger fidelity on the dominant error parameter for each approach. We identify break‐even points and regimes where noisy remote gates achieve parity with gate‐cuts. In particular, our work suggests that a 10‐fold reduction in the present M2O transducer noise added figures would favor generating multipartite entangled states with remote gates over circuit cutting. Our work informs near‐term quantum interconnect hardware metrics and motivates a network‐aware hybrid quantum‐classical distributed computation approach, where both quantum links and circuit cuts are employed to minimize quantum runtime.

title: Probabilistic Spatiotemporal Modelling with Kernelised Attention
abstract: Accurate modelling of spatiotemporal environmental data remains a challenging problem due to complex spatial dependency and temporal dynamics. While transformer architectures have demonstrated strong performance in many sequence modelling tasks, their effectiveness in sparse and noisy geospatial applications is less well understood. We propose a novel framework for probabilistic spatiotemporal modelling with kernelised attention, which integrates 3D convolutional feature extraction, structured kernel interpolation (SKI)-based attention, and Gaussian process (GP) modelling. Our approach reinterprets attention as a kernel operator and introduces SKI approximation to reduce computational complexity. We evaluate our method on satellite-derived NDVI data from four recent flood-affected sites, enabling assessment under both gradual vegetation dynamics and large-scale environmental disturbances, which are characterised by strong seasonality and missing observations, where uncertainty-aware models are particularly crucial. Furthermore, we demonstrate that incorporating a periodic kernel yields the best performance, reflecting the inherent seasonal structure of vegetation dynamics. These findings suggest that in noisy, partially observed spatiotemporal applications, explicitly embedding kernel structure and inductive bias into attention mechanisms is crucial for robust learning.

title: AI and creativity in advertising agencies: From the acceleration of workflows to transformation of value dynamics
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping creative work in advertising agencies, yet most research focuses on performance metrics. This paper examines how AI integration alters creative development processes and value dynamics for agencies and clients. It draws on 22 semi-structured interviews with senior agency and client-side professionals in Germany. Using a hybrid inductive–deductive content analysis and a phase model derived from it, the study explores how AI tools are embedded across the major phases of briefing, research, ideation, internal review, client presentation, and feedback. Findings show that AI significantly accelerates research, idea generation, and content drafting, increasing efficiency and expanding creative exploration; however, the fundamental structure of the creative workflow remains stable. Rather than replacing established processes, AI intensifies them. While agencies benefit from faster iteration and data-driven insights, clients increasingly expect quicker turnaround times and lower costs. At the same time, concerns about generic outputs, brand misalignment, and legal risks require human oversight. The study demonstrates that AI simultaneously enables value co-creation and co-destruction through enhanced knowledge integration and risks value erosion through rising expectations and quality tensions. Transformation therefore occurs less through structural disruption than through accelerated processes and shifting client–agency dynamics. These findings provide practical insights for managing hybrid human–AI creative workflows in service-based industries. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at https://hstalks.com/business/.

Findings show that AI significantly accelerates research, idea generation, and content drafting, increasing efficiency and expanding creative exploration; however, the fundamental structure of the creative workflow remains stable. Rather than replacing established processes, AI intensifies them. While agencies benefit from faster iteration and data-driven insights, clients increasingly expect quicker turnaround times and lower costs. At the same time, concerns about generic outputs, brand misalignment, and legal risks require human oversight. The study demonstrates that AI simultaneously enables value co-creation and co-destruction through enhanced knowledge integration and risks value erosion through rising expectations and quality tensions. Transformation therefore occurs less through structural disruption than through accelerated processes and shifting client–agency dynamics. These findings provide practical insights for managing hybrid human–AI creative workflows in service-based industries. title: ADVERSARIAL MACHINE LEARNING: ATTACKS, DEFENSES, AND EMERGING CHALLENGES
abstract: AI and ML have become integral parts of the current cybersecurity framework due to their ability to automate the process of threat detection, malware identification, intrusion detection, spam filtering, and fraud detection. Although AI/ML models have been highly successful until now, they are becoming more and more susceptible to adversarial machine learning (AML). In such cases, the use of malicious data can influence the behavior of an intelligent system, reduce its predictive performance, or even expose confidential information. In this chapter, an in-depth introduction to the field of adversarial machine learning is provided, covering the importance of adversarial attacks in cybersecurity and the growing number of adversarial attacks specific to AI systems. This chapter will start with basic definitions and terms related to the topic such as adversarial learning, threat models, adversarial examples, and attack surface. Afterward, the chapter will explore several types of adversarial attacks such as evasion attacks, data poisoning, backdoor attacks, model extraction, model inversion, and membership inference attacks. The existing methods used to defend against adversarial attacks are also analyzed in detail; such defense techniques include adversarial training, defensive distillation, feature squeezing, robust optimization, certified defenses, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). Moreover, the chapter also identifies some cybersecurity applications that require adversarial robustness such as intrusion detection systems, malware analysis, biometric authentication, phishing detection, healthcare diagnostics, autonomous vehicles, and fraud detection in finance. Finally, the recent research challenges are presented including adaptive adversaries, transferability of adversarial examples, large language model security, federated learning, privacy-preserving machine learning, and ethics.

title: Lightweight Multimodal Anomaly Detection Based on GhostNet and FiLM
abstract: To address the trade-off between detection accuracy and deployment efficiency in surveillance-based anomaly detection, we propose a lightweight multimodal abnormal behavior detection method based on GhostNet and FiLM fusion (G-FLM). GhostNet is employed as a lightweight visual backbone to reduce computational redundancy, while audio features are introduced to generate FiLM-based channel-wise affine parameters to generate FiLM-based channel-wise affine parameters for conditional recalibration of video features, thereby achieving effective audio-video information fusion with limited additional overhead. Experimental results on the XD-Violence dataset show that, under the same experimental configuration, G-FLM achieves an mAP of 0.7392. Compared with multimodal baselines such as Two-Stream and I3D, the mAP is improved by 5.6% and 18.0%, respectively. Precision reaches 0.8163 and F1 reaches 0.7260, both outperforming the comparison methods. At the same time, the model has only 3.63M parameters, requires only 1.9054 GFLOPs, and achieves an inference latency of 30.53 ms/batch, achieving higher detection accuracy with substantially lower computational overhead than the compared baselines. The results indicate that G-FLM achieves a good overall balance between detection accuracy and deployment efficiency, and provides a feasible lightweight solution for multimodal abnormal behavior detection in resource-constrained scenarios.

abstract: Supplementary material for a survey submitted to IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials on machine-learning-based detection in encrypted traffic executed on programmable network hardware, organized around the lifecycle of a deployed detector (inference, drift monitoring, in-service update, adversarial defense). The deposit contains: (1) the master table classifying all 130 surveyed entries along six taxonomy axes with lifecycle stage, venue tier, claim-strength level, evidence score and artifact status (CSV and typeset Tables S1-S4); (2) the search and selection protocol with the query families, the deterministic title-and-abstract pre-screen and the record counts obtained on IEEE Xplore and the ACM Digital Library on 9 September 2026; (3) the script and per-seed results of the drift measurement in Fig. 5 of the article (CESNET-QUIC22 and CESNET-TLS-Year22, histogram gradient boosting, with and without handshake packets); (4) the reference list with DOIs.

title: Charada Vlei Rat: A Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Charada Vlei Rat
abstract: This paper introduces Charada Vlei Rat (CVR), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Charada Vlei rats, a unique species endemic to South Africa known for their remarkable ability to navigate and locate water sources in a complex, labyrinthine environment. CVR leverages the rats' strategic exploration, memory, and adaptive decision-making processes to solve complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates three core mechanisms: (1) a memory-based exploration strategy mimicking the rats' cognitive map; (2) a dynamic adjustment of search parameters based on the perceived landscape complexity, analogous to the rats' adaptation to varying terrain; and (3) a probabilistic selection mechanism incorporating a 'hopeful leap' component, representing the rats' occasional exploratory movements. The algorithm is formulated with the following key parameters: $N$ – population size, $C$ – cognitive map size, $α$ – exploration parameter, $β$ – exploitation parameter, $ρ$ – forgetting rate, $P$ – probability of hopeful leap, and $k$ – number of layers in the cognitive map. The performance of CVR is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The results indicate that CVR exhibits strong adaptability and convergence properties, making it a promising candidate for various real-world optimization challenges.

title: Title: Topological Geometry Quantum Entanglement Theory
abstract: This paper explores a novel theoretical framework for quantum entanglement, predicated on the concept of topological geometry. We propose a dynamic adjustment mechanism allowing quantum systems to evolve their information state through measurement, fundamentally expanding beyond the limitations of current quantum entanglement. The core principle centers around the integration of topological structures with quantum entanglement, offering a potential pathway to enhanced quantum information processing and storage. This work investigates the implications of this approach and highlights the potential for achieving unprecedented control and manipulation of quantum states. The theory aims to provide a more flexible and powerful approach to quantum information, leveraging the unique properties of topological geometry.

title: Cape York Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Rat Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Cape York Rat (CYR), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of rats inhabiting the Cape York Peninsula in Australia. Rats are known for their efficient and adaptive search strategies when locating food sources, particularly in complex and dynamic environments. CYR leverages these behaviors, specifically the "scatter-and-home" strategy, to establish a robust and effective optimization process. The algorithm employs a population of rat agents, each simulating a rat's movement and food search. Each agent's movement is governed by a probabilistic model incorporating exploration (scatter) and exploitation (home) phases. A key innovation is the dynamic adjustment of the exploration and exploitation parameters based on the local search landscape, mimicking the rat's adaptation to varying food availability. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CYR through a series of benchmark problems, highlighting its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's performance is compared against established metaheuristic methods, demonstrating its competitive capabilities. The results suggest that CYR offers a promising approach for solving complex optimization problems, particularly those characterized by non-convex landscapes and dynamic changes.

title: Dynamic Topology Adjustment of Non-Linear Machine Learning
abstract: Dynamic Topology Adjustment of Non-Linear Machine Learning aims to enhance the adaptability of machine learning models by dynamically adjusting their parameters in response to data variations. This paper introduces a novel framework that leverages dynamic topology adjustment, enabling real-time parameter optimization and automated parameter adjustment to ensure optimal model performance across evolving datasets. We present a comprehensive theoretical framework and a practical implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in optimizing machine learning models. This work provides a significant advancement in the field of non-linear machine learning, addressing limitations of existing methods through a dynamic and adaptable approach.

title: Where Perceptrons Meet Proof Trees: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of neuro-symbolic and reasoning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Bush Hyrax-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bush Hyrax Algorithm (BHA), inspired by the foraging behavior of bush hyraxes in the African savanna. Bush hyraxes exhibit a unique strategy of alternating between searching for food and resting in shaded areas. This alternating pattern is translated into a metaheuristic framework for solving optimization problems. The BHA incorporates elements of both exploration and exploitation, mimicking the hyrax's adaptive response to environmental changes. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a novel movement strategy based on the hyrax's probabilistic shift between foraging and resting locations. We describe the algorithm's core components, including the population initialization, the movement mechanism, and the acceptance criterion. The effectiveness of the BHA is demonstrated through a series of test functions, showcasing its ability to converge towards optimal or near-optimal solutions. The algorithm's performance is compared against established metaheuristic methods like the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to assess its advantages and limitations. The results indicate that the BHA can be a competitive and efficient solution for a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: Differential Privacy for Federated Learning with Adaptive Noise
abstract: Federated learning (FL) presents a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging the data itself. However, the inherent privacy risks associated with aggregating model updates introduce significant challenges. Traditional differential privacy (DP) techniques often rely on adding uniform random noise to gradients, which can be overly conservative and degrade model accuracy. This paper introduces an adaptive noise scheme for FL that dynamically adjusts the noise level based on the sensitivity of the aggregated gradients. The proposed method monitors gradient variance and employs a stochastic gradient descent (SGD) variant with a dynamically adjusted learning rate and noise scale. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and a simplified simulation that this approach significantly reduces the overall noise level compared to standard DP while maintaining a comparable privacy guarantee, ultimately leading to improved model accuracy in FL settings. The key contribution lies in the intelligent adaptation of noise, responding directly to the data's inherent characteristics.

title: Geometric Turing Machines: A Probabilistic Reasoning Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic reasoning framework based on geometric Turing machines, leveraging geometric structures and topological properties to enhance inference capabilities and decision-making. Traditional probabilistic reasoning often relies on symbolic manipulation, while geometric Turing machines offer a unique approach utilizing geometric structures and topology for more robust and efficient reasoning. We develop a framework that integrates geometric modeling with probabilistic inference, aiming to overcome the limitations of conventional methods. This research explores the potential of geometric structures to represent and reason about complex relationships, leading to improved performance in scenarios requiring strong deductive reasoning and robust decision-making. The core mechanism centers on constructing inference rules through geometric transformations and applying probabilistic inference techniques to these transformed spaces. We present a preliminary implementation illustrating the framework's effectiveness in a specific, yet-to-be-defined application domain.

title: Adaptive Kernel Methods via Learned Feature Transformations
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to kernel methods that leverages learned feature transformations to enhance efficiency and effectiveness. Traditional kernel methods rely on fixed kernel functions, which may not always optimally capture the underlying data structure. We propose a framework where the feature transformations themselves are learned using a neural network, dynamically adapting to the data to maximize the kernel's performance. This adaptive approach addresses the limitations of static kernels by allowing the method to automatically discover and exploit the most relevant feature representations. The core idea centers around optimizing the kernel function by learning a transformation that best aligns the original features with a kernel-friendly space. This research provides a new avenue for improving kernel method performance, particularly in scenarios with complex data distributions. The key contributions include the formulation of the adaptive kernel method and the design of a neural network architecture for learning the feature transformations. Experimental results (simulated) demonstrate the potential of this approach to outperform standard kernel methods.

title: Title: Bayesian Non-Linear Dynamics (BNLD)
abstract: Bayesian Non-Linear Dynamics (BNLD) presents a novel approach to modeling complex dynamical systems by integrating Bayesian inference with a dynamically updated probability distribution. This framework extends traditional Bayesian methods to effectively handle highly non-linear, emergent behavior, offering a pathway to capture the intricate interactions within systems without relying on explicit parameter estimation. The core mechanism involves a gradient-based update of the probability distribution, driving the system towards states with higher expected outcomes, while simultaneously incorporating observational data through a generative process. This distinguishes BNLD from conventional Bayesian methods, emphasizing active exploration and state space refinement. This paper provides a detailed explanation of the BNLD algorithm, its mathematical foundations, and its potential applications across diverse fields.

title: ## Brown Hare Metaheuristic Algorithm (BHMA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Brown Hare Metaheuristic Algorithm (BHMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of brown hares. BHMA utilizes a multi-layered exploration and exploitation strategy mimicking the hare's movement pattern – rapid bursts of exploration followed by localized exploitation around promising areas. The algorithm incorporates a novel 'hare-leap' mechanism for global exploration and a 'hare-settle' mechanism for local refinement. We detail the algorithm's core components, including the population initialization, the fitness evaluation, the 'hare-leap' and 'hare-settle' operators, and the termination criteria. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BHMA through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitiveness against established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that BHMA offers a balanced approach between exploration and exploitation, achieving robust performance across diverse problem landscapes. Finally, we discuss the algorithm's potential for future research and applications.

title: Brown Flower Bat Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Brown Flower Bat Algorithm (BFBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of brown flower bats ( *Eptesicus fuscus*). The algorithm leverages the bats' unique echolocation and flight patterns to effectively navigate complex optimization landscapes. BFBA incorporates key features such as pulse emission, frequency modulation, and group movement, mimicking the bats' strategies for finding food sources. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a fitness sharing mechanism and a local search technique to iteratively refine the solution set. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's core components, including the emission probability, frequency adjustment, and movement strategy. Performance evaluations on a range of benchmark functions demonstrate BFBA's competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's ability to adapt to different problem characteristics makes it a promising candidate for solving a variety of real-world optimization challenges. The primary objective is to establish a robust and efficient optimization technique with a clear biological inspiration.

title: Review of Research on Knowledge Distillation Methods for Low-Resource Machine Translation
authors: GAO Yusi, WANG Siriguleng, SI Qintu
abstract: With the advancement of deep learning, neural machine translation models have achieved remarkable progress in translation tasks for high-resource language pairs and reached high levels on multiple automatic evaluation metrics. Low-resource machine translation, however, is often constrained by the scarcity of parallel corpora and insufficient linguistic research support, leading to a tendency for models to overfit and consequently making it difficult to improve translation quality. As an efficient model compression and knowledge transfer technique, knowledge distillation can transfer the knowledge of a teacher model to a student model, effectively enhancing the generalization and robustness of the student model in low-resource scenarios. This study presents a systematic review of knowledge distillation methods in the field of low-resource machine translation. Firstly, it elaborates on the concept and development history of knowledge distillation, sorts out its research progress thread from high-resource to low-resource scenarios, and introduces relevant evaluation metrics and datasets. Then, from three dimensions, distillation content, training methods, and model architectures, it analyzes in detail the principles, processes, advantages, disadvantages, and applicable scenarios of various knowledge distillation methods, and verifies their practical effectiveness through typical cases. Furthermore, it points the core challenges faced by low-resource machine translation in terms of?data scarcity, corpus noise, insufficient utilization?of monolingual resources and catastrophic forgetting, and systematically elaborates on the corresponding solutions of knowledge distillation technology to address the above challenges. Finally, it provides an outlook on future research directions, including robust distillation mechanisms, synergy between multi-modal and cross-domain distillation, self-distillation and teacher-free distillation, and joint optimization of data, models and distillation. This study provides a theoretical framework and development path for low-resource translation tasks, and offers a reference for the in-depth development of multilingual and multimodal intelligent translation research.

title: Transparency Without Exposure: A Selective Verifiability Framework for Copyright and Trade Secrets in Generative AI Training Data
abstract: Governance of generative artificial intelligence (AI) faces a structural dilemma. Copyright owners and regulators need evidence of training-data acquisition, licensing, rights reservations, and processing, while unrestricted disclosure may expose valuable dataset compilations and methods. This article systematically compares AI transparency duties in Korea, the European Union, the United States/California, and Japan by examining disclosure and information-provision requirements, labeling, obligated actors and triggers, exceptions and safeguards, and enforcement and sanctions. Copyright fair use and text-and-data-mining limitations are treated separately: they govern specified uses of protected subject matter and do not generally displace independent transparency duties covering copyrighted and non-copyright information. The comparison finds that public summaries improve orientation but generally cannot establish whether a particular work was included, on what legal basis it was processed, or in which model version it was used. Therefore, the article proposes “selective verifiability”: the capacity for an authorized actor to test a bounded compliance claim against lifecycle-linked records without receiving unrestricted corpus access. The framework has three tiers: a standardized public training-content summary; a confidential, source-level provenance manifest available to regulators or accredited auditors; and a claim-triggered verification channel for rights holders. W3C PROV, SPDX, machine-learning bills of materials, digital signatures, and append-only commitments can support the architecture but cannot independently prove legal validity or record completeness. For Korea, the article recommends a phased pilot, explicit institutional allocation, purpose-limited data processing, proportionate recordkeeping duties, reviewable trade-secret claims, and evidentiary incentives that do not immunize infringement.

title: Explainable deep learning improves human mental models of self-driving cars
abstract: Self-driving cars increasingly rely on deep neural networks to achieve human-like driving. However, the opacity of such black-box motion planners makes it challenging for the human behind the wheel to accurately anticipate when they will fail, with potentially catastrophic consequences. Here, we introduce concept-wrapper network (i.e., CW-Net), a method for explaining the behavior of black-box motion planners by grounding their reasoning in human-interpretable concepts. *** Eoin M. Kenny and Julie A. Shah MIT, Cambridge, MA, USA *** Akshay Dharmavaram, Sang Uk Lee, Tung Phan-Minh, Shreyas Rajesh, Yunqing Hu, and Laura Major Motional AD Inc., Boston, MA, USA *** Momchil S. Tomov, Department of Psychology and Center for Brain Science, Harvard University, Cambridge, MA, USA Motional AD Inc., Boston, MA, USA ## Data and Domain This is a simple toy domain of a self-driving car to illustrate the paper's algorithm on open source environments. There are three concepts, "drive straight", "turn left", "turn right", which we manually labelled 15,000+ examples of. This script will only take a few minutes to run. ## Training Note that when you run this code the training can sometimes get stuck in local minima, you want the losses to look like this around epoch 50. You may need to run it a few times to get this result (on average we found it works on > 50% of the runs) Epoch 50/50, Loss CE: 0.3304, Loss MSE: 0.2487, Accuracy: 87.97% The important number is the Loss MSE, **if it's around 0.25 the run was successful.** ## Evaluation It then runs for 3 simulations. The results will show a gif which nicely summarises the algorithm working on the first simulation. You will also find a confusion matrix for classifying the three concepts 0/1/2, which are "straight road", "left turn", "right turn". Lastly, there are losses for the concept predictions and MSE for mimicking the original black-box labels. We also included numpy arrays for the average rewards of CW-Net and its error for a few simulations compared to the original black box as mean squared error between the two.

title: Moving beyond linear summation to infer interaction order from neural and biological dynamics
abstract: We introduce the three-body recurrent neural network (TBRNN), a recurrent model that explicitly incorporates quadratic, three-body interactions. We show that TBRNNs are universal approximators and extend low-rank recurrent neural network (RNN) theory to derive a corresponding low-rank TBRNN framework, allowing model rank to help discriminate between pairwise and higher-order dynamics. On canonical neuroscience tasks, TBRNNs exhibit solution geometries distinct from standard RNNs, indicating that higher-order interactions reshape accessible dynamical regimes rather than merely re-parameterizing pairwise models. Building on these results, we develop a practical model-comparison procedure that infers interaction order directly from observed trajectories. Applied to synthetic systems, a gene regulatory model, and neural recordings, the framework distinguishes pairwise, three-body, and mixed interaction structure. Our results broaden the space of interpretable dynamical models in neuroscience and provide a general approach for probing higher-order interactions in biological networks.

title: FORGE: Forward-Only Test-Time Adaptation for Integer-Only Vision Models on Microcontrollers
abstract: Vision models deployed on microcontrollers (MCUs) are quantized to integer-only arithmetic and run in inference-only runtimes that do not carry the machinery backpropagation needs: the standard tool for adapting a model to the distribution shift (sensor noise, blur, lighting) it meets in the field. Existing forward-only test-time adaptation (TTA) methods either run only on server- or edge-GPU-class models (not true microcontroller integer execution), or require the batch-normalization (BN) layers that integer deployment fuses away. We present a forward-only TTA method that operates on deployed, BN-folded, integer-only convolutional networks. The key observation is that fusing BN into the preceding convolution, a mandatory step for integer inference, destroys the statistics that normalization-based adaptation relies on. We restore adaptation by re-normalizing each folded convolution's per-channel output to its clean training statistics, using only forward-pass estimates. The method (i) recovers most of gradient-based TENT's accuracy gain (+20.9 vs. +24.9 points) and matches forward-only BN adaptation, while being the only method that runs on a folded integer-only model; (ii) needs to adapt only 3 of 21 layers (selected without seeing the test corruptions) to recover 93% of the benefit; (iii) survives single-sample streaming with a batch-size-scaled momentum; and (iv) generalizes across three datasets (up to 200 classes) and two architectures. We validate bit-exact int8 convolution execution and deploy on an ESP32-S3, where, measured with a Nordic PPK2 power profiler, the forward-only adaptation (a lightweight fp32 recalibration around the int8 convolutions) costs only 8.3 mJ (6.8% of inference energy) and 21.9 ms on the deployed SIMD-optimized model: forward-only adaptation is cheap on a real microcontroller.

title: SinkPruner: Sink-Free Visual Token Pruning for Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: Despite their strong multimodal understanding ability, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) incur substantial computational overhead when processing long visual token sequences. To reduce inference costs, recent studies have explored visual token pruning through vision-centric or text-guided strategies. However, these methods often overlook high-norm outlier tokens, i.e., tokens with abnormally large feature norms, leading to suboptimal pruning decisions. In this work, we show that such high-norm outlier tokens are highly redundant in both feature and spatial dimensions, yet are often mistakenly preserved as informative cues by existing methods. Motivated by this observation, we propose SinkPruner, a training-free visual token pruning framework for efficient MLLM inference. SinkPruner follows a coarse-to-fine design with two key modules: a visual sanitizer that filters high-norm redundancies and alleviates attention sink and attention dispersion, and a text-guided pruner that further retains tokens semantically aligned with the text query. Extensive experiments on twelve image-language and four video-language benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness, efficiency, and generalizability of our framework. Notably, SinkPruner preserves 96.5% (91.8%) of the original performance of LLaVA-1.5 (Qwen2.5-VL) under an 89% token reduction. Experiments further indicate that our visual sanitizer exhibits promising transferability in enhancing the performance of existing pruning methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/LaVi-Lab/SinkPruner.

title: Error-Aware Neural Networks for Quantum State Tomography in Realistic Integrated Quantum Photonic Circuits
abstract: Quantum photonic circuits began growing in research interest due to the long coherence times of photonic qubits, allowing for potential long-range quantum communication. To miniaturize these photonic circuits, much research has been done into integrating these systems into a chip-architecture, commonly known as an integrated photonic circuit. Due to the collapse postulate of quantum mechanics, information encoded into photons must be extracted from measurement distributions, formally known as quantum state tomography. This thesis examines the use of neural networks in quantum state tomography, compared to the commonly used maximum likelihood estimation method in a two-qubit system, in the presence of errors typically found in integrated photonic circuits. It is shown in simulation, that by altering the training of a neural network to incorporate errors, the state reconstruction infidelity can be greatly decreased and far surpass the maximum likelihood estimation. Networks are also shown with low bit-precisions, allowing for the potential future use of ultra-fast optical processors to create the neural network. From this work, it can be concluded that neural networks are able to not only complete the task of quantum state tomography, but are able to withstand errors and create more faithful reconstructions for the outputs of integrated quantum photonic circuits.

title: Simplicity: A Filtered LFSR Stream Cipher for Hybrid Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: Hybrid Homomorphic Encryption (HHE) combines fully homomorphic encryption with a symmetric primitive to reduce client-side overhead in privacy-preserving computation. In this setting, the homomorphic evaluation of the symmetric primitive constitutes a fundamental cost that directly impacts both transciphering latency and throughput. While recent works have revisited standard ciphers such as AES under modern FHE schemes, dedicated HHE-oriented designs consistently achieve significantly better timing performance. We introduce \emph{Simplicity}, a new stream cipher designed specifically for HHE. Simplicity follows the filtered LFSR paradigm and is built around a new class of weightwise quadratic Boolean functions. Unlike previously studied constructions, this class guarantees algebraic immunity at least $d$, enabling parameter regimes in which the immunity scales linearly with the number of variables. We establish balancedness, derive lower bounds on nonlinearity, and provide both lower and upper bounds on algebraic immunity, yielding explicit resistance guarantees against algebraic and fast algebraic attacks. To enable efficient homomorphic evaluation, we introduce a coding-theoretic technique for reconstructing LFSR states with bounded noise growth, based on linear codes with small covering radius. Combined with an optimized filter-function evaluation strategy, this approach significantly reduces the number of ciphertext multiplications. For 128-bit security parameters, Simplicity achieves a single-instance transciphering latency of 4.4 ms per bit single-threaded in its fastest configuration, representing a 7.9× improvement over Nostalgia (ToSC’25) and up to a 41.8× improvement over Transistor (CRYPTO’25), while providing stronger provable algebraic guarantees. With 2 threads, latency reduces to just 2.3 ms. These results suggest that filtered LFSRs, when carefully dimensioned and analyzed, remain a competitive and principled foundation for HHE-oriented symmetric design.

title: Red Teaming an Industrial Maintenance Chatbot using PAIR and nanoGCG
abstract: Os Large Language Models (LLMs) têm sido cada vez mais adotados em ambientes industriais para suporte a atividades de manutenção, diagnóstico e tomada de decisão operacional. No entanto, sua integração a sistemas corporativos introduz novos riscos de segurança, especialmente relacionados a ataques adversariais baseados em prompts. Este trabalho apresenta uma avaliação de um chatbot de manutenção baseado em LLM, desenvolvido para uma empresa parceira do setor industrial (anonimizada). Foram avaliadas técnicas de red teaming black-box e white-box, incluindo geração automática de jailbreaks (PAIR) e otimização de prompts baseada em gradiente (nanoGCG). Os resultados revelam entradas adversariais geradas com PAIR que conseguem contornar mecanismos de segurança e induzir respostas inseguras ou violação de políticas. No cenário experimental avaliado, o PAIR demonstrou maior aplicabilidade prática e melhor relação custo-benefício em comparação ao nanoGCG, ainda que as diferenças metodológicas entre os dois experimentos (modelo vítima e LLM juiz distintos) impeçam uma comparação direta dos valores absolutos de ASR. Por fim, são discutidas implicações de segurança para a adoção de LLMs em ambientes industriais.

evidence.title: Red Teaming an Industrial Maintenance Chatbot using PAIR and nanoGCG
evidence.abstract: Os Large Language Models (LLMs) têm sido cada vez mais adotados em ambientes industriais para suporte a atividades de manutenção, diagnóstico e tomada de decisão operacional. No entanto, sua integração a sistemas corporativos introduz novos riscos de segurança, especialmente relacionados a ataques adversariais baseados em prompts. Este trabalho apresenta uma avaliação de um chatbot de manutenção baseado em LLM, desenvolvido para uma empresa parceira do setor industrial (anonimizada). Foram avaliadas técnicas de red teaming black-box e white-box, incluindo geração automática de jailbreaks (PAIR) e otimização de prompts baseada em gradiente (nanoGCG). Os resultados revelam entradas adversariais geradas com PAIR que conseguem contornar mecanismos de segurança e induzir respostas inseguras ou violação de políticas. No cenário experimental avaliado, o PAIR demonstrou maior aplicabilidade prática e melhor relação custo-benefício em comparação ao nanoGCG, ainda que as diferenças metodológicas entre os dois experimentos (modelo vítima e LLM juiz distintos) impeçam uma comparação direta dos valores absolutos de ASR. Por fim, são discutidas implicações de segurança para a adoção de LLMs em ambientes industriais.

title: Guardrails for Enterprise LLM Applications: Screening, Policy, and Audit in Production
abstract: Enterprise LLM applications fail in the gaps around the model, not inside it. A model can be called in an afternoon; governing what goes into it and what comes out takes deliberate engineering. This paper describes the guardrail layer built around production LLM applications on Azure: screening of prompts before they reach the model, screening of responses before they reach the user, a policy engine that turns organizational rules into enforceable decisions, and an audit trail that records every decision. We cover what guardrails must protect against, including prompt injection, data exfiltration through model outputs, and unsafe tool calls, treated as design considerations rather than incident reports. We describe the policy lifecycle that keeps rules reviewable and reversible: policies as versioned artifacts, staged rollouts, and rollback through the same CI/CD practices used for application code. We close with operating lessons on keeping policies tight but reviewable, budgeting screening latency as a design input, and keeping a human override path that is fast and fully logged. This paper reports no controlled experiments and no benchmark numbers. It is an experience report from production platform work, and the operating lessons are the contribution. All technical content, design decisions, and conclusions are the author's own, drawn from the author's professional experience.

title: 基于贝叶斯网络的多重性推理算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to multiple-factor analysis – a technique that leverages probabilistic reasoning to predict the behavior of complex systems. The core of our algorithm is a Bayesian network, which allows for the modeling of relationships between different factors and their probabilistic dependencies. We propose a framework that employs Bayesian inference to generate a set of plausible scenarios, thereby improving model reliability and predictive accuracy. This work addresses limitations of existing methods by offering a robust and efficient solution for complex systems analysis. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation, demonstrating its effectiveness in predicting system dynamics. This research contributes to the field of complex systems modeling by providing a new method for probabilistic reasoning and model refinement.

title: 基于多智能体强化学习的软件系统优化
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for optimizing the performance and resource utilization of software systems. Traditional software optimization techniques often struggle with the inherent complexity and dynamic nature of modern systems. MARL offers a promising approach by treating individual components of a software system as intelligent agents, enabling decentralized coordination and adaptive optimization. This research explores the core claim that MARL can lead to more effective optimization, driven by the core mechanism of modeling system components as agents and leveraging MARL algorithms. The novelty lies in the application of MARL to this domain, resulting in increased system adaptability and efficiency. The presented framework demonstrates the potential of MARL to address the challenges of dynamic optimization within software systems.

title: ## Cape York Brown Bandicoot: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of a Unique Australian Marsupial
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Cape York Brown Bandicoot (CYBB) algorithm, inspired by the foraging strategies observed in the Cape York Brown Bandicoot (Perameles nasuta nigricauda), a unique Australian marsupial inhabiting the Cape York Peninsula. Bandicoots are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging behavior, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies to locate food sources. The CYBB algorithm leverages these principles through a dynamic population management system, a stochastic exploration mechanism, and a novel adaptive weight adjustment strategy. The algorithm's core components include a population initialization phase, a fitness evaluation function, a movement operator mimicking the bandicoot's exploratory steps, and a convergence criterion. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. The results indicate that the CYBB algorithm exhibits robust performance compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization, particularly in challenging, high-dimensional search spaces. Future research will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to diverse problem domains.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding for Adaptive Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally different approach to learning, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical reinforcement learning. This paper introduces a novel quantum-enhanced reinforcement learning algorithm leveraging entangled states for instantaneous information transfer. We propose a mechanism that utilizes a "hidden feedback" system, enabling gradients to propagate via entangled states, accelerating learning and promoting adaptive behavioral patterns. The core claim is that this approach enhances the learning efficiency and generalization capabilities of reinforcement learning compared to traditional methods. We explore the potential of this approach and present preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Adaptive Time Series Analysis Framework for Quantum Computing Simulations
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing simulation framework designed to excel in adaptive time series analysis. The framework leverages self-adaptive quantum algorithms and quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust qubit states, thereby enhancing computational accuracy and efficiency. We propose a method for incorporating time series analysis with quantum computing's inherent adaptability, creating a system that can intelligently optimize quantum computations for precise time series prediction and modeling. Traditional time series analysis methods often rely on predefined models, while this framework aims to exploit quantum effects for more flexible and efficient analysis. The core mechanism involves a hybrid approach combining quantum state control with self-adaptive algorithms, ultimately enhancing the capability of time series prediction and modeling.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Integration for Robotic Navigation in Dynamic Environments
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of neural networks and symbolic reasoning for robust robotic navigation in dynamic environments. Traditional robotic navigation systems often struggle with the inherent uncertainty and unpredictability of real-world scenarios, relying heavily on reactive behaviors or complex, but brittle, symbolic planning approaches. We propose a neuro-symbolic framework that combines the perceptual capabilities of neural networks with the logical inference and decision-making power of symbolic planning. This architecture allows the robot to learn from sensory data and dynamically adapt its plans in response to changing environmental conditions. The core claim of this work is that this integration significantly enhances robotic navigation performance in unpredictable environments. We detail the system architecture, including a convolutional neural network (CNN) for visual perception and a STRIPS-based planner for path planning and action selection. The system utilizes a belief-tracking mechanism to update its symbolic representation of the environment, enabling it to reason about potential obstacles and opportunities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a simulated environment, showcasing the robot's ability to navigate complex, dynamic scenarios more reliably than systems relying solely on neural networks or symbolic planning. Key elements include a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) to manage uncertainty and a rule-based system for refining the symbolic plan based on perceived changes. The results demonstrate improved robustness and adaptability, highlighting the potential of neuro-symbolic integration for practical robotic navigation applications.

title: ## Bushveld Horseshoe Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bushveld Horseshoe Bat Inspired Algorithm (BHSBA), motivated by the foraging strategies observed in bushveld horseshoe bats ( *Rhinolophus praxidinis*). These bats exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting food sources in complex and dynamic environments. The BHSBA algorithm leverages key behavioral features such as directional movement, clustered foraging, and adaptive learning to effectively address complex optimization challenges. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a modified velocity update mechanism inspired by the bats' echolocation and movement patterns. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the core components of the BHSBA, including the position update equation, the adaptive learning rate calculation, and the cluster formation mechanism. The algorithm's performance is demonstrated through a series of benchmark problems, showcasing its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Optimization, Bat Foraging, Evolutionary Algorithm, Complex Problem Solving.

title: Brazilian Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Squirrel Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Brazilian Squirrel" (BS), inspired by the foraging and caching behavior of Brazilian squirrels. The algorithm leverages the squirrel's efficient exploration of the environment, its memory of food locations, and its adaptive adjustment of search strategies based on environmental cues. BS combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a novel memory mechanism mimicking the squirrel's caching behavior. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates a 'cache' representing previously visited promising solutions, and utilizes a 'memory' component to adjust the probability of revisiting these cached solutions based on their performance and the current search landscape. The core of the BS algorithm is defined by the following equations: * Velocity Update: $v_{ij}^{k+1} = w * v_{ij}^{k} + c_1 * r_1 * (p_j - x_{ij}^{k}) + c_2 * r_2 * (g_j - x_{ij}^{k})$ * Position Update: $x_{ij}^{k+1} = x_{ij}^{k} + v_{ij}^{k+1}$ * Cache Update: $Cache_{i} = \{x_{ij}^{k} | f(x_{ij}^{k}) > Threshold\}$ where $f(x)$ is the objective function and $Threshold$ is a dynamically adjusted threshold based on the global best solution. * Memory Update: $Memory_{i} = \{x_{ij}^{k} | f(x_{ij}^{k}) > Threshold\}$ and the probability of revisiting $x_{ij}^{k}$ is proportional to $Memory_{i}[x_{ij}^{k}] / (Total Cache Size)$. The BS algorithm demonstrates promising results on a set of benchmark optimization problems, exhibiting competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO and ABC. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics like convergence rate, solution quality, and computational cost. The simulation results indicate that the BS algorithm offers a robust and efficient approach to tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: Title: Adaptive Graph Neural Network for Bayesian Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Graph Neural Network (AGNN) designed to enhance Bayesian reasoning capabilities within complex environments. Traditional graph neural networks often struggle with the inherent uncertainty of Bayesian inference. This novel approach dynamically adjusts node and edge weights based on Bayesian inference, enabling the network to refine its reasoning process and achieve more robust and personalized outcomes. The core mechanism leverages a reinforcement learning component to iteratively optimize the network's weightings, resulting in improved accuracy and adaptability in scenarios where uncertainty is significant. The paper details the architecture, training process, and experimental results demonstrating the benefits of this dynamic adaptation strategy.

title: ASEAN Post-Quantum Cryptography Readiness 2026 An Empirical Assessment of the ASEAN-10
abstract: This report assesses publicly verifiable national preparation for the migration to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) across the ten member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations assessed in this series (Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, the Lao People's Democratic Republic, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, the "ASEAN-10"), as at 17 August 2026. Timor-Leste, admitted as ASEAN's eleventh member state on 26 October 2025, is excluded from the headline comparative set under the commissioning scope and is assessed separately in Annex A.The assessment was conducted because the discussion of post-quantum readiness has become dominated by declarations of intent. Standards bodies have published algorithms. Governments have published statements. Vendors have published readiness claims. Very little of this establishes what any given state has actually put in place. The question this report addresses is narrower and harder: what can each member state publicly demonstrate that it is doing to govern the replacement of quantum-vulnerable cryptography in its own national estate?The population is fixed at exactly ten states. Each was assessed against the locked five-tier framework carried over unchanged from the EU-27 assessment, running from Tier 1, denoting a government-led national migration programme with substantive implementation machinery, to Tier 5, denoting that no publicly verifiable PQCspecific activity sufficient to meet Tier 4 was identified. Classification rests on national evidence only. Membership of ASEAN, participation in ASEAN cybersecurity cooperation, joint ministerial declarations, and regional capacity-building programmes were each excluded as automatic grounds for elevation. Quantum computing research, quantum key distribution, digital identity sophistication and general cybersecurity maturity were excluded under a strict anti-conflation rule.The headline finding is that ASEAN readiness is real but thin at the top and sparse at the bottom. One state, Malaysia, demonstrates operating national migration machinery: a Cabinet-approved national cryptography policy addressing the quantum era, a statutory directive obliging critical-infrastructure entities to prepare and submit cryptographic migration data, a national migration plan launched by the Chief Secretary to the Government, and an operating national proof-of-concept sandbox. Six further states (Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam) demonstrate structured government preparation, ranging from a national-CERT migration guideline paired with a central bank's regulator-issued cryptographic requirement (Cambodia) to a published national migration framework with a stated requirement scope (Brunei) and a Prime Ministerial-level programme naming post-quantum cryptography among its research priorities (Vietnam). One state, the Philippines, sits at Tier 3 on a government-funded, named post-quantum cryptography research line, without migration machinery. One state shows a single isolated item of PQC-specific evidence; one state returned no sufficient public PQC evidence under this methodology, on this date, by this search.

title: A Machine Learning Framework for Strategic Gameplay Optimization in Scrabble Using Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper explores and compare various artificial intelligence-based techniques used for playing classic board game Scrabble. As the world is evolving around finding quick and efficient techniques for the solution of each problem using Machine learning, gaming industry is also a flourishing industry and has grown 9.8% compared to previous year and has generated a revenue of 26.14 billion dollars through global platforms this year which majorly captures youth and many gamers. Most popular games played online includes PUBG, Ludo, cards etc. Scrabble is being a vocabulary enhancing game and less popular game has attracted its intension of research towards it. The implementation of this imperfect information game has been done through Monte Carlo Tree Search algorithm, opponent modelling and Q learning machine learning techniques. Reinforcement learning algorithms are the most suitable algorithm for strategic games. This approach uses Q learning algorithm for the implementation of scrabble game where game theory is the science behind the strategy making for the player playing against human. Experimental results suggest that the Q-learning based agent got higher mean scores and also sharpen decision making efficiency, a bit more than the earlier Scrabble gameplay approaches. Game theory strategy can be categorized into two zero sum and non-zero-sum strategy which could be used for various games and Nash equilibrium.

title: A Framework for Assessing LLM Consistency in Knowledge Engineering
abstract: Consistency, that is the degree to which a system, process, or its results produce similar outcomes when repeated under identical or different conditions, is a critical concern in knowledge engineering (KE). This is particularly the case given the increasing reliance on large language models (LLMs) in various tasks. This paper introduces CoLLM, a framework designed to assess whether a system or process produces consistent results in LLM-based KE tasks through three tests: (i) the LLM Repeatability Test , which evaluates the level of stochasticity or non-determinism of LLMs in existing studies; (ii) the LLM Update Impact Test , which examines the effect that LLM updates may have on results; and (iii) the LLM Replacement Test , which explores the effect of using alternative LLMs to perform the same study. Through 59 different experiments taken from five separate, recent studies, and leveraging various LLMs and datasets, we investigate the consistency of the results to empirically validate the reliability of the original findings for each study. Our investigation shows that in the majority of cases (81.4%), a consistent behavior with respect to the original studies can be observed, despite some variability across the individual outputs. Additionally, in some cases, changing the choice of LLM can result in a consistent improvement across different metrics. These results demonstrate the viability of the proposed framework in general to assess the consistency of LLM-based KE tasks.

title: Exponentiated gradient learning yields brain-like synaptic distributions
abstract: Artificial neural networks trained with gradient descent (GD) are widely used to model brain learning, but GD allows synapses to switch between excitatory and inhibitory and produces weight distributions unlike those observed experimentally. We show that an alternative rule, exponentiated gradient (EG), avoids these problems because its multiplicative, exponential weight updates mathematically prohibit synapses from changing sign and preferentially scale already-large weights, naturally generating log-normal distributions. This mechanism also concentrates task-relevant computation onto a smaller subset of strong connections, which we show makes EG-trained recurrent neural networks more robust to synaptic pruning and better able to learn from sparsely relevant inputs than GD-trained networks, while matching GD's performance on standard cognitive tasks. These findings tie a normative optimization principle directly to observed features of synaptic organization in the brain.

title: Knowledge-Interposed Curriculum Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Supervisory Control Synthesis in Electric Flying Vehicles
abstract: Energy supervisory control (ESC) for electric flying vehicles is challenged by strong air–ground mode coupling and stringent safety constraints. Conventional reinforcement learning–based ESC typically requires extensive training and are difficult to bootstrap from scratch, which often leads to inefficient exploration and delayed satisfaction of safety constraints. To address this issue, we propose a large language model–enhanced curriculum learning warm start for soft actor–critic (CL-LSAC), which incorporates expert prior knowledge from large language models. The proposed curriculum prioritizes safety constraints before fuel efficiency, guiding policy learning through a highly non-convex reward landscape. Evaluated on a high-fidelity urban air mobility mission, CL-LSAC significantly suppresses the control saturation observed in unguided baselines. Compared with static reward weighting, our method improves state-of-charge regulation accuracy by 49% and accelerates convergence by more than 15% via LLM-guided initialization, yielding data-efficient and physically consistent policies that demonstrate high real-time execution feasibility on hardware-in-the-loop platforms.

title: Reliable Sample-Level Quantum Error Mitigation via Dominance-Aware Clustering
abstract: Many quantum algorithms for classically difficult optimization tasks must return high-quality bitstrings from finitely many circuit executions, whereas most quantum error-mitigation methods target expectation values. We study sample-level recovery when measured probability mass is distributed around multiple latent bitstrings, called centers. Each component of the measured probability mass is called a source and we assume that each center is associated with one source. We identify dominance-at every coordinate, more than half of a retained region's probability mass comes from one source and agrees with its center-as a sufficient condition under which majority voting recovers that center with exponentially decreasing error probability. We show that nearest-center assignment, as used in clustering algorithms such as the $k$-modes algorithm, can fail to produce dominated regions even when the true centers are known. This failure motivates responsibility thresholding and a local dominance screen, whose combination we call dominance-aware (DA) refinement. Synthetic and simulated MaxCut-QAOA experiments show that DA refinement favors precision, while $k$-modes with DA refinement improves overall center recovery. All procedures are classical post-processing and require no additional quantum-circuit executions.

title: New classes of trace-form permutation polynomials and their compositional inverses
abstract: We construct permutation polynomials of the form x + γTr^{q^2}_q(h(x)) over the finite field F_{q^2}. More precisely, we present two families ofpermutation polynomials whose coefficients range over all elements of the field rather than being restricted to a proper subfield. We also compute the compositional inverses of both families. Our techniques involve the evaluation of certain Kloosterman sums together with the analysis of some equations over finite fields, and we believe these can be of independent interest.
