title: Quantum Error Correction Coding and Complementary Utilization of Non-Classical Correlations
abstract: This paper investigates the complementary relationship between quantum error correction (QEC) coding and non-classical correlations, specifically quantum entanglement and quantum teleportation. The core claim is that integrating redundant information inherent in QEC codes with the unique properties of non-classical correlations can dramatically enhance error correction efficiency and information transmission rates. We propose a novel architecture, termed a "Quantum Channel Amplifier," based on a specific QEC code, designed to leverage non-classical correlations for information amplification. The amplifier utilizes entanglement to boost signal fidelity and employs a tailored error decoding algorithm to correct errors introduced by the channel. Our approach addresses a critical gap in current QEC research by explicitly considering and exploiting the potential information gain provided by non-classical correlations, moving beyond the traditional focus on classical noise. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for future research into hybrid QEC strategies that combine the strengths of both classical and quantum approaches. We demonstrate, through mathematical analysis and conceptual design, the potential for significant improvements in quantum communication and computation.

The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for future research into hybrid QEC strategies that combine the strengths of both classical and quantum approaches. We demonstrate, through mathematical analysis and conceptual design, the potential for significant improvements in quantum communication and computation.

title: Adaptive Bayesian Networks for Anomaly Detection in Streaming Data
abstract: Anomaly detection in streaming data presents significant challenges due to the continuous evolution of data distributions and the difficulty in identifying novel, unseen anomalies. Traditional Bayesian Networks (BNs) often rely on pre-defined structures and struggle to adapt effectively to these dynamic environments. This paper introduces an Adaptive Bayesian Network (ABN) framework designed specifically for anomaly detection within streaming data. The ABN dynamically adjusts its structure and parameters through a novel adaptation rule that prioritizes changes linked to potential anomalies. The core mechanism leverages Bayesian inference and a learning rate parameter to update the BN's conditional probability tables (CPTs) based on incoming data. This approach enables the ABN to continuously learn and respond to changes in the data stream, improving its ability to detect both known and novel anomalies. We present a formal description of the ABN, outlining its key components and the adaptation rule. The theoretical framework is demonstrated through a conceptual analysis and a discussion of potential implementation considerations. The ultimate goal is to provide a robust and adaptable solution for real-time anomaly detection in dynamic streaming environments.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Optimization for Complex Model Selection
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Bayesian optimization (QEBO) offers a promising approach to accelerate the model selection process, particularly for complex models, by harnessing quantum mechanics for enhanced efficiency in parameter space exploration. This paper proposes a novel QEBO algorithm utilizing quantum state estimation to rapidly approximate the fitness of model configurations, thereby reducing computational cost and improving the selection of optimal models. We introduce a quantum-enhanced Bayesian optimization framework, focusing on the exploitation of quantum entanglement and superposition to efficiently map the parameter space. The core mechanism involves quantum state estimation to quickly assess the suitability of each model configuration, significantly reducing the search time compared to classical methods. This paper details the theoretical foundation, algorithm implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the potential of QEBO to outperform traditional Bayesian optimization in complex model selection scenarios.

title: Title: Non-Local Graph Neural Networks for Semantic Representation
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-local graph neural networks to enhance semantic representation learning. Traditional graph neural networks primarily focus on node features, often struggling to capture the nuanced relationships within a graph. We propose a novel architecture that explicitly models the *meaning* of the graph, achieved through a mechanism that learns representations sensitive to the graph's structure and content. This approach aims to improve generalization and robustness compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios with complex, high-dimensional graphs. The core of this work involves a modified attention mechanism integrated within the graph neural network to facilitate the propagation of information across the graph, thereby strengthening the representation of semantic connections. We present a series of experiments evaluating the performance of this architecture on various graph datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in semantic understanding and overall accuracy.

title: Silent negatives — corrected VUA-18 split and audit materials
abstract: Companion data and code release for the paper Silent negatives: when partial annotation becomes supervision. A label integrity audit of the VU Amsterdam Metaphor Corpus benchmark (submitted to Language Resources and Evaluation). Fragment b1g-fragment02 of the VU Amsterdam Metaphor Corpus was annotated only in part (3,006 lexical units per Appendix A of Steen et al., 2010), while the distributed VUAMC.xml contains the full 20,170-word section. The VUA-18 benchmark conversion assigned negative gold labels to the never-annotated section — 9,287 target tokens, 12.8% of the all_pos training set. This record contains the boundaries of the two coded sentence spans (738–765 and 1485–1584), the token-identifier exclusion lists implementing the corrected split (TRIM condition), the conversion-reconstruction and audit scripts, and per-run provenance files. The official VUA-18 test set is not modified.

title: Leveraging Gaussian Mixture Models for Detecting Anomalies in Time-Series Data
authors: Sandia National Laboratories (SNL-NM), Albuquerque, NM (United States)
abstract: Test systems must be capable of classifying measured data as expected or anomalous in real time. Anomalous results may portend system failure, and, if undetected, may result in damage to the unit, test equipment, or potential harm to personnel. This report investigates the use of Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) as a clustering tool in classifying time-series data.

title: Prompting Techniques for Large Language Models
abstract: This chapter surveys how prompt engineering techniques shape the quality, accuracy, and controllability of large language model (LLM) outputs. It begins with foundational methods, including zero-shot and few-shot prompting, and highlights when simple instruction is sufficient and when examples are needed to stabilize format and intent. It then advances to reasoning-oriented techniques, including chain-of-thought (CoT) variants, self-consistency, automatic CoT (Auto-CoT), tree-of-thought, self-ask, generated knowledge prompting, role-play, and ReAct, emphasizing how structured reasoning and tool-grounded actions reduce errors and improve transparency. Finally, this chapter introduces prompt orchestration approaches, meta-prompting, prompt chaining, and synthetic prompting to manage complex, multistage tasks and concludes with a comparative summary of their strengths and limitations.

title: Estimating the performance of the infotaxis search strategy for changing beamwidth
abstract: Infotaxis was compared with maximum a posteriori (MAP) search in active sensing for varying sonar beam widths on one-dimensional grids. The active sensing model incorporated missed detections and false alarms typically found in sonar. Monte Carlo simulations were run across detection probabilities for a fixed false alarm probability, and experiments validated the simulations. Infotaxis outperformed MAP for high and low detection probabilities for medium beam widths. Infotaxis also showed faster recovery for missed first-detections compared to MAP for medium beam widths. Furthermore, Infotaxis exhibited information-maximizing behavior, confirming the strategy's effectiveness relative to MAP.

title: ZOETROPE: A Decentralized Framework for Licensing Visual Content for Generative AI
abstract: Generative AI models are commonly trained on large-scale datasets of visual content scraped from diverse sources across the open internet. Yet, creators currently lack effective ways to express consent or to be recognized and rewarded when their work is included in such datasets. We present ZOETROPE, a decentralized framework that enables the discovery and licensing of visual content for AI training and usage. Viewing the copyright and AI challenge as a content supply chain problem, we show how open media provenance standards can be extended to support fair and transparent reuse of visual content in AI pipelines. ZOETROPE combines watermark-based provenance persistence, cascading licensing for downstream residual payments, and privacy-preserving visual search across decentralized repositories. By integrating discovery, creator consent, licensing, and compensation without recourse to a central marketplace, ZOETROPE offers a pathway toward more transparent and economically aligned relationships between creators and AI developers in the age of generative AI.

title: From local to global XAI: Do local regression contributions correspond to spatially adjusted SHAP (SA-SHAP)?
abstract: The SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method, which originates from game theory, is a widely used explainable AI (XAI) technique for quantifying the importance of independent variables in machine learning and deep learning models applied to regression problems in data science and engineering. This method has also been applied in the field of geospatial information science, where incorporating spatial dimension into model inputs enables the extraction of spatial effects. However, some researchers argue that while raw coordinates may be useful for prediction, they are undesirable as substitutes for causal factors and may lead to a positional surrogate effect. This raises a key question: to what extent are local regression models, which incorporate spatial variation in an indirect manner, consistent with such geo-SHAP-based explanations? Moreover, global SHAP outputs can become difficult to interpret due to the decomposition of geographic components and their interactions with non-spatial features. This challenge is particularly pronounced when spatial encoding extends beyond raw x–y coordinates to higher-order representations. To address these gaps, this study proposes the Spatially Adjusted SHAP (SA-SHAP) approach, which combines the interaction between each feature and spatial components with the contribution of that feature. The study demonstrates that, both locally and globally, the contributions from SA-SHAP offer explanatory power that strongly corresponds to that of local regression, in which feature values are weighted by spatially variable coefficients. This study applies SA-SHAP to various simulated datasets and presents a real-world application using online taxi orders from the city of Chicago. In this respect, we employ XGBoost as one of the most powerful machine learning methods and MGWR as a powerful local regression benchmark. For spatial encoding, we extend beyond x–y coordinates to include techniques such as Moran eigenvectors, interactive basis expansion with radial basis functions (RBF), and space2vec. Experimental results indicate that SA-SHAP remains robust across different spatial encoding strategies considered in this study. This perspective enables the derivation of both local and global measures of feature importance that jointly capture spatial effects, thereby providing a robust bridge between spatial econometric models and XAI.

title: Federated learning-based privacy-preserving and secure mobility and handover prediction in MEC-integrated cellular networks
abstract: Efficient and secure mobility and handover prediction are inevitable for seamless connectivity and optimal performance in mobile networks. Traditional centralized approaches raise privacy concerns and impose high communication overhead, making them less effective in modern heterogeneous environments. Moreover, recent distributed solutions have not adequately addressed the complexity issues of model training and comparative performance evaluation in terms of computational cost and predictive accuracy. By considering these drawbacks, this paper proposes a lightweight Federated Learning (FL) architecture for privacy-preserving, secure, and more accurate mobility and handover prediction in multi-access edge computing (MEC)-integrated cellular networks. The architecture employs several ensemble models, including XGBoost (XGB), Random Forest Regressor (RFR), and CatBoost, for local training at user equipment (UE) and edge nodes, with model updates aggregated at the global level. To ensure security, lightweight encryption and secure aggregation protocols are integrated during both local update transmission and global model distribution. Experimental results using real mobility datasets collected from legacy cellular networks (3G GSM/4G LTE) demonstrate that the employed FL-based global mobility model achieves the best performance with 0.9869 of R 2 , 0.003416 of MAE , 0.000108 of MSE , and 0.010400 of RMSE , while the global handover model achieves 0.9632 of R 2 , 0.0052 of MAE , 0.0003 of MSE , and 0.0182 of RMSE . These results outperform existing non-FL approaches, confirming that the proposed method provides superior accuracy, reduced error, and enhanced scalability while safeguarding user privacy and ensuring robust protection against adversarial threats. Although the experimental evaluation is conducted using 3G/4G-based datasets, the proposed FL architecture is radio-technology agnostic and does not rely on Radio Frequency (RF)-specific parameters, making it readily extensible to 5G and beyond mobile networks.

title: A monolithic segmented 3D ion trap fabricated from fused silica by selective laser-induced etching
abstract: We present the design, fabrication, and characterization of a monolithic, segmented, three-dimensional linear Paul ion trap for quantum science applications. The trap is fabricated from a single fused-silica block using selective laser-induced etching (SLE) and is subsequently metallized, forming electrodes isolated by self-shadowing trench structures without the need for layer alignment or external shadow masks. The segmented electrodes allow for shaping of the axial potential, enabling the creation of anharmonic potential wells, such as those required for equidistant ion strings. In addition, they enable shuttling and splitting of ion chains. We discuss key design choices and SLE-imposed constraints on achievable feature sizes, and evaluate electron-beam evaporation and magnetron sputtering as metallization approaches. Across two independent experimental setups, we demonstrate stable trapping and control of linear chains of up to 33 $^{40}$Ca$^+$ ions, including approximately equally spaced configurations. The measured secular frequencies in both traps agree with boundary-element simulations at the percent level, with residual deviations attributed to stray electric fields in the presence of anharmonic axial potentials, rather than fabrication imperfections. We measure axial micromotion field strengths on the order of 100 V/m along the trap axis, in approximate agreement with simulations. For radial mode frequencies near 2 MHz and an ion-electrode distance of 300 um, we measure heating rates of the order of 10 quanta/s in all but one motional mode, which is elevated by a technical noise source. The presented trap design is thus suitable for a wide range of quantum science applications and demonstrates the viability of SLE for the fabrication of finely segmented, monolithic, three-dimensional ion traps.

title: Irreducibility and regularisation properties of Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
abstract: We study regularisation and irreducibility properties of Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups (GQMSs) acting on continuous-variable quantum systems. We first identify a natural notion of regularity for operators in this setting, which allows us to formulate and characterise the smoothing effects of GQMSs in terms of algebraic conditions involving the drift and quantum diffusion matrices. These conditions establish a connection with the controllability theory of quantum linear systems and with the structure of decoherence-free subsystems. We then characterise irreducibility through several equivalent algebraic criteria: one formulated in terms of the drift and quantum diffusion matrices, one in terms of the operators appearing in the generalised GKLS representation of the generator, and a third given by a quantum analogue of Hörmander's condition. A central and somewhat surprising consequence is that, in contrast with the classical case, irreducibility is strictly stronger than conditions ensuring regularisation. Our results provide an algebraic framework for analysing these properties and lay the groundwork for a broader study of reducible Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups and, more generally, more general relevant quantum Markov semigroups on continuous-variable systems.

title: Relational-Core Graph Analytics Querying graphs at SQL scale, and why the node/edge model is a performance tax, not a truer picture of connected data
abstract: A durable assumption holds that graph analytics requires a purpose-built graph engine, and that relational systems are ill-suited to connected data. We argue the opposite for the workloads enterprises actually run. A columnar relational engine fronted by a graph query language matches or exceeds native graph engines on analytical graph queries, and - decisively - scales past the point where in-memory graph engines fail. We further argue that the node/edge property graph is not a more faithful model of connected data but a re-encoding of relationships that already exist explicitly in relational tables; reconstructing them at query time is pure overhead. We present ClickGraph and its Databricks-dialect sibling DeltaGraph, systems that translate Cypher directly onto the native relational schema - the tables, columns, and foreign keys as they already exist - and execute in place on ClickHouse, Databricks, or in-process on lakehouse files, with no import and no separate cluster. Because the output is ordinary SQL, an underperforming query is an open optimization surface: it can be rewritten, and the engine itself extended. We support the argument with a peer system's own published benchmark, in which a columnar engine outruns Neo4j by two-to-four orders of magnitude, and with reproducible measurements across the LDBC Social Network Benchmark suite.

evidence.title: Relational-Core Graph Analytics Querying graphs at SQL scale, and why the node/edge model is a performance tax, not a truer picture of connected data
evidence.abstract: A durable assumption holds that graph analytics requires a purpose-built graph engine, and that relational systems are ill-suited to connected data. We argue the opposite for the workloads enterprises actually run. A columnar relational engine fronted by a graph query language matches or exceeds native graph engines on analytical graph queries, and - decisively - scales past the point where in-memory graph engines fail. We further argue that the node/edge property graph is not a more faithful model of connected data but a re-encoding of relationships that already exist explicitly in relational tables; reconstructing them at query time is pure overhead. We present ClickGraph and its Databricks-dialect sibling DeltaGraph, systems that translate Cypher directly onto the native relational schema - the tables, columns, and foreign keys as they already exist - and execute in place on ClickHouse, Databricks, or in-process on lakehouse files, with no import and no separate cluster. Because the output is ordinary SQL, an underperforming query is an open optimization surface: it can be rewritten, and the engine itself extended. We support the argument with a peer system's own published benchmark, in which a columnar engine outruns Neo4j by two-to-four orders of magnitude, and with reproducible measurements across the LDBC Social Network Benchmark suite.

title: CQF-HMR: Continuous Quaternion Flows for Probabilistic 3D Human Mesh Recovery from a Single Image
abstract: Recovering 3D digital humans from a single 2D image is an ill-posed computer vision problem due to the loss of depth information. Probabilistic 3D human pose estimation compensates for this by estimating a set of 3D hypotheses from a prior distribution via generative models. However, most prior work focuses only on 3D keypoints, which often leads to implausible poses that are difficult to apply to downstream tasks, e.g. animation or digital humans. SMPL-based methods are more scalable thanks to the explicit body priors, but it requires more complex modeling of the generation process due to the non-additive nature of the joint rotations. In this work, we propose a novel approach for probabilistic 3D humans using quaternion-constrained continuous normalizing flows conditioned on 2D pose estimations. Our proposed quaternion flows show significant advantages over approaches using other rotation representations. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art results of our method on Human3.6M, particularly in ambiguous settings, and comparable pose estimation accuracy on challenging 3DPW and EMDB benchmarks.

title: Perceptible or Not? Diagnosing Passive Fingerprints for Speech Deepfake Attribution
abstract: Passive fingerprints (intrinsic traces naturally left by generators) have been shown to enable attribution in speech deepfake detection, yet their persistence, reproducibility, and content-independence remain unverified. Moreover, no prior work distinguishes perceptible from imperceptible fingerprints, although the two have very different implications for attribution reliability. Perceptible fingerprints, such as emotional expression, are shaped by perceptual quality objectives and may change across model updates, whereas imperceptible fingerprints are not explicitly optimised by current training objectives and are rarely considered in existing dataset design or training strategies, as they have limited influence on downstream applications. We therefore propose a Perceptible-Imperceptible Passive-fingerprint Diagnostic Protocol (PIPDP) to define and separately analyze these two fingerprint types. PIPDP comprises three complementary analyses: multi-evidence fingerprint verification through residual-energy, reproducibility, and saliency analyses, perceptually transparent perturbations preserving audio quality, and prompt-driven emotion change that modifies perceptible fingerprints without model retraining. Experiments across ten speech generators and three attribution detectors show that imperceptible fingerprints provide persistent attribution cues. Perceptually transparent perturbations reduce attribution accuracy by up to 48.2\% on HiggsAudioV3, whereas emotion-driven changes leave attribution largely unchanged, with only about a 1.0\% accuracy variation across emotions on CosyVoice2 using w2v-bert-MLP. These results suggest that imperceptible fingerprints are more reliable for trustworthy attribution.

title: GenONet: A Generative operator Network for High-Resolution Precipitation Nowcasting
abstract: High-resolution precipitation nowcasting is critical for reducing the impacts of severe weather but remains difficult because of rapid storm evolution. Deep learning models have shown great promise for this task, but their predictive skill often deteriorates over longer forecast horizons. This leads to increasingly blurry forecasts that fail to capture the complex, non-linear evolution of storm systems. In order to address these limitations, we introduce Spatio-Temporal U-DeepONet (GenONet), a novel architecture for long-range precipitation forecasting up to 3 hours, specifically designed to produce sharp and physically consistent results. GenONet's architecture pioneers the use of a Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) as a generator within a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) framework for this task. The DeepONet learns the continuous-time dynamics of precipitation, ensuring stability over long forecast horizons. Adversial training against a spatio-temporal discriminator compels the model to produce sharp, coherent forecasts, while a physics-informed loss regularizer, derived from the Moisture Conservation Equation, improves physical plausibility in our ablation setting. Quantitative evaluations show that our model achieves consistently higher scores on most of the metrics, especially for highintensity events and at longer lead times. Qualitatively, GenONet produces structurally coherent forecasts that maintain their integrity, whereas baseline models degrade into indistinct patterns. Finally, an ablation study confirms the benefit of this physics-informed loss, highlighting the strength of combining operator learning with adversarial training.

title: RESEARCHING METHODS FOR THE AUTOMATIC DETECTION OF OFFENSIVE LANGUAGE BASED ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
abstract: This study explores artificial intelligence-based methods for the automatic detection of offensive language.The research focuses on the application of Natural Language Processing (NLP), machine learning, and deep learningtechniques to identify offensive, abusive, and inappropriate content in textual data. Particular attention is given to text preprocessing,feature extraction, text classification, and neural network-based approaches for improving the accuracy andefficiency of offensive language detection. The study highlights the potential of artificial intelligence to support safer digitalcommunication and enhance automated content moderation across online platforms

title: Retroalimentación formativa con inteligencia artificial generativa y su efecto en el razonamiento matemático universitario
abstract: This study evaluates the impact of automated formative feedback using generative artificial intelligence on advanced mathematical thinking and mathematics anxiety in higher education. Using a quantitative quasi-experimental design with pretest and posttest measurements, a sample of 120 second-year engineering students was analyzed, divided equally into an experimental group (n = 60), which received adaptive socratic scaffolding based on Polya's method and Wilson's Feedback Ladder managed by a custom GPT-4o assistant, and a control group (n = 60), exposed to conventional analog teacher feedback. The post-test results revealed highly significant differences favoring the experimental group (M = 72.96; SD = 10.41) compared to the control group (M = 63.30; SD = 10.14; t = 5.147; p < 0.001), demonstrating a large effect size (d = 0.940). Likewise, a significant decrease in mathematics anxiety and an increase in self-efficacy were observed, although discrepancies remain due to qualitative system errors. It is concluded that guided algorithmic scaffolding optimizes cognitive load and promotes independent learning, provided that the direct delivery of complete answers is restricted to prevent student cognitive dependence

title: Beyond Guardrails: Tracing Cross-Layer Evidence in Local LLM-Agent Execution
abstract: Agent-facing restrictions may reduce an LLM agent’s exposed tools without making corresponding tested effects unrealizable elsewhere in the runtime environment. We evaluated three NemoClaw/OpenShell profiles through mediated trials, direct profile-level probes, and independent effect oracles. The interface-restricted profile repeatedly acquired a protected marker despite its reduced tool surface, whereas the hardened profile prevented acquisition across all induced read attempts. The permissive profile reached the controlled destination and produced one confirmed exfiltration in a post-hoc replay. These results distinguish interface restriction, profile-level realizability, destination contact, and realized effects.

title: VeriFlow: A Containment-First Architecture for Evidence-Gated Release of Language-Model Claims
abstract: Language models can produce fluent claims whose evidence does not warrant the stated certainty. Retrieval, model ensembles, and LLM-as-judge evaluation help generate and rank candidate answers, but they do not by themselves create an independent basis for certifying a claim. VeriFlow is an evidence-argument and release-gating architecture built around one invariant: model agreement is never evidence status. A claim reaches VERIFIED only when a non-LLM definitive verifier passes on the exact bound claim. Other claims travel a seven-status evidence ladder under typed ceilings, with abstention as the default when a positive predicate is incomplete. The architecture separates two failure families that require different controls. Semantic-warrant failures arise when evidence does not entail the claim, the scope shifts, causality is overstated, or assumptions disappear. Authority-boundary failures arise when model votes, judge outputs, declared provenance, or unchecked formalizations are allowed to mint evidence status. VeriFlow addresses the first with explicit decomposition, scope, admissibility, and visible uncertainty; it addresses the second with system-owned provenance, controlled trust-credential issuance, non-LLM verification, typed ceilings, and deterministic release policy. The public reference implementation contains a verification kernel, a release engine, and deterministic paths for arithmetic relations, registry lookups, propositional logic, and SEC/XBRL filed facts. Its 236-test suite includes regressions for earlier false-VERIFIED defects. The paper states five material limits of the release, including under-guarded ceiling assignment for arbitrary prose, attestation-based human binding, incomplete conclusion binding, a receipt that is an integrity record rather than a replay bundle, and an assumed out-of-process isolation boundary. The contribution is a testable containment architecture that narrows who may mint certainty, records why a release decision occurred, and refuses positive status when a required predicate is absent. Reference implementation (release tag v1.0.0, Apache-2.0): https://github.com/AMRISHERE-DEV/Veriflow

title: IIL-AS-Tagging
abstract: What this is An open Python toolkit for assigning, retrieving, and customizing tags for Autonomous Systems (ASes) using monthly AS feature snapshots. Each snapshot is a per-ASN feature table aggregating signals from routing, DNS, Internet scanning, geolocation, network topology, and organization mapping. The as_tagging package is also available on PyPI. Released monthly feature-snapshot packages are maintained in the canonical GitHub repository and mirrored on Hugging Face. This artifact accompanies the paper “Rethinking and Facilitating How We Classify Autonomous Systems by Network Properties” (ACM IMC 2026). License The toolkit, documentation, and AS feature-snapshot data are distributed under the Georgia Tech Acceptable Use Agreement (AUA). See the repository’s LICENSE file for details. Source and documentation The GitHub repository is the canonical source for the toolkit, documentation, and continuously updated feature snapshots. Please refer to the repository README for installation instructions, usage examples, and dataset documentation. Stable citation Please cite the Zenodo concept DOI for this artifact.

title: note12. Unregistered Interpretation: Successful Rule Reconstruction Without a Uniqueness Certificate
abstract: Notes 10 and 11 of the series "The Collapse of Independence" described a loss: the source had collapsed into a single source, and the act of attestation into an attribute of the very object being attested. The interpretation rule was expected to have collapsed in the same manner. Inspection showed otherwise. The rule was recovered in full — in four queries, uniquely, and verified against all five informative records of the corpus. There is no loss. The result of this note is not that the rule was lost, but that a successful reconstruction is indistinguishable from a failed one from the inside. 97% of the corpus is degenerate and carries zero discriminating information; all information about the mechanism is contained in five records out of 163. The run might not have yielded them. The rule would then have been reconstructed incorrectly — confidently, uniquely, without a single indication of error. Furthermore, even within the reconstruction that did succeed an unresolved fork remains, one that the available data cannot resolve in principle, and the note specifies the exact input configuration that would resolve it and that did not occur in the run. Claimed result: the problem of reconstruction is replaced by the problem of certifying reconstruction, and the latter is not solved by enlarging the archive. It is solved only by a commitment to a class of admissible interpretations, undertaken prior to observation. A post hoc certificate is impossible; ante hoc it is trivial. The distinction runs not between archives, but between an archive and a commitment made before observation. This is a rare case in which time enters the definition of the object rather than its metadata. Material: snapshot of omnicore_l3.verified_facts, PARAM BILIM cluster,22 July 2026.

title: 基于自适应逻辑结构的优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on a dynamically adjustable logic structure. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter settings, limiting their ability to effectively address complex problems. This work proposes a new approach that dynamically adjusts the logic structure of the optimization process, leading to significant improvements in efficiency, particularly for problems exhibiting inherent non-linearity. We detail the algorithm's core mechanism, including the implementation of a parameter adjustment scheme and its impact on the optimization process. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing its superior performance compared to existing methods in various benchmark datasets. This algorithm offers a promising step towards more efficient and robust optimization techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement Geometry Topology
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity for novel information transfer paradigms. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement's non-linear effects to construct a geometrically-based entanglement model, enabling cross-dimensional information exchange and predicting the potential geometric forms of quantum entanglement. We propose a novel approach that leverages topological structures induced by entangled states, transforming entanglement into a complex geometric topology, and employing the inherent properties of topology to facilitate communication beyond classical limits. This research investigates the implications of this approach for secure and potentially revolutionary data transmission.

title: 基于自适应的强化学习的运动控制策略
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to motion control using reinforcement learning, employing a dynamically adaptive reinforcement learning framework. Traditional motion control methods rely heavily on human-defined control parameters, which can be time-consuming and require expertise. Our proposed system leverages a self-adaptive model to automatically adjust these parameters, optimizing both precision and efficiency. The core mechanism involves training a model to learn optimal control policies based on observed data, enabling automated parameter tuning and improved control performance. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach in achieving enhanced accuracy and speed in simulated robotic tasks.

title: Burneo's Oldfield Mouse: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Oldfield Mice
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Burneo's Oldfield Mouse" (BOM), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in Oldfield mice (Mus musculus mussonius). Oldfield mice are renowned for their efficient and adaptive foraging behavior, particularly their ability to balance exploration and exploitation in resource-scarce environments. BOM leverages these behavioral traits to develop a robust optimization algorithm suitable for complex, non-convex problems. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a position-based exploration mechanism mimicking the mouse's movement patterns, a resource-based exploitation phase focusing on high-value areas, and a dynamic adaptation strategy influenced by the local resource availability. Mathematical formulations are provided for each component, detailing the parameters and underlying logic. The performance of BOM is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its competitive capabilities against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that BOM exhibits strong convergence properties and adaptability, particularly in scenarios with high dimensionality and complex landscapes. Future research directions include incorporating environmental factors and extending the algorithm to solve multi-objective optimization problems.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization via Adaptive Sampling (QIAO)
abstract: This paper introduces Quantum-Inspired Optimization via Adaptive Sampling (QIAO), a novel technique for complex system optimization. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of real-world problems, frequently requiring exhaustive search or computationally expensive approximations. QIAO leverages quantum-inspired principles to dynamically sample regions of the solution space, focusing on areas exhibiting higher potential for improvement. This adaptive sampling strategy significantly enhances efficiency compared to traditional methods, particularly in scenarios with high dimensionality and complex interactions within the system. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating its efficacy in a simulated optimization problem. The focus is on demonstrating the practical advantages of this approach through a quantifiable improvement in performance.

title: Brockman's Myomyscus: A Meta-Heuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Myomyscus
abstract: This paper introduces Brockman's Myomyscus, a novel meta-heuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Myomyscus* mice. *Myomyscus* exhibits a unique strategy of exploring a limited search space efficiently, prioritizing areas with high resource density. Brockman's Myomyscus leverages this behavior by implementing a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, utilizing a "memory" system to retain information about promising regions and dynamically adjusting search efforts. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The core mechanism involves a 'memory' matrix that stores the relative attractiveness of different search locations. The attractiveness is updated based on the fitness of solutions found within that region. This memory facilitates focused exploration of promising areas while preventing premature convergence. This paper details the algorithm's design, its underlying principles, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness on benchmark optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is compared to established meta-heuristics, highlighting its potential advantages in scenarios demanding efficient exploration and exploitation. The primary goal is to provide a robust and adaptable meta-heuristic that can effectively tackle complex optimization challenges.

evidence.title: Brockman's Myomyscus: A Meta-Heuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Myomyscus
evidence.abstract: This paper introduces Brockman's Myomyscus, a novel meta-heuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Myomyscus* mice. *Myomyscus* exhibits a unique strategy of exploring a limited search space efficiently, prioritizing areas with high resource density. Brockman's Myomyscus leverages this behavior by implementing a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, utilizing a "memory" system to retain information about promising regions and dynamically adjusting search efforts. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The core mechanism involves a 'memory' matrix that stores the relative attractiveness of different search locations. The attractiveness is updated based on the fitness of solutions found within that region. This memory facilitates focused exploration of promising areas while preventing premature convergence. This paper details the algorithm's design, its underlying principles, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness on benchmark optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is compared to established meta-heuristics, highlighting its potential advantages in scenarios demanding efficient exploration and exploitation. The primary goal is to provide a robust and adaptable meta-heuristic that can effectively tackle complex optimization challenges.

title: Brant's Gerbil: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Gerbil Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Brant's Gerbil, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging and burrowing behaviors of gerbils. Gerbils are known for their efficient navigation in complex environments, their ability to exploit food sources effectively, and their strategic use of tunnels for shelter and travel. Brant's Gerbil leverages these observed behaviors to create a stochastic search algorithm designed for solving optimization problems. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a representation of potential solutions as "burrows" and a "food source" concept to guide exploration and exploitation. Key components include a burrow generation mechanism mimicking gerbil burrow construction, a food source evaluation function reflecting resource availability, and a movement strategy based on gerbil foraging patterns. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability. The core innovation lies in translating specific gerbil behaviors into algorithmic constructs, offering a unique perspective on metaheuristic design. The algorithm's parameters are tuned through a systematic approach, focusing on balancing exploration and exploitation, resulting in robust performance across various problem types. Future research will explore extensions of the algorithm to handle multi-objective optimization and incorporate adaptive learning mechanisms.

title: Bokhara Horseshoe Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bokhara Horseshoe Bat Algorithm (BHBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bokhara horseshoe bat. These bats utilize a sophisticated Echolocation system to navigate and find food in complex environments. The BHBA mimics this process through a combination of adaptive parameter control, a multi-dimensional search space, and a novel convergence mechanism based on the bat's flight patterns. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The core of the BHBA lies in its 'Echo' component, which dynamically adjusts the search space and the probability of exploration and exploitation based on the bat's perceived environment. The algorithm's parameters are governed by a sigmoid function, ensuring a smooth transition between exploration and exploitation phases. The performance of the BHBA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. Specifically, we investigate its application to the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP), the Rastrigin Function, and the Sphere Function. Results indicate that the BHBA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods, such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The key contributions of this work include the development of a biologically inspired algorithm with a unique convergence mechanism and its successful application to various complex optimization problems. Future research will focus on incorporating advanced features, such as adaptive mutation rates and local search techniques, to further enhance the algorithm's capabilities.

title: Opening the Black Box a Crack: A Historical Development Review of Explainability and Interpretability of Black-Box Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Explainability and Interpretability of Black-Box Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of explainable AI and interpretability as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Supplementary Methods and Videos of OrbitalPSI-GPT
abstract: Description This repository contains extended technical documentation and supplementary video materials associated with OrbitalPSI-GPT, a text-driven, clinician-in-the-loop framework for patient-specific orbital implant (PSI) design. These materials provide additional implementation details, demonstrate the system's interactive design workflow, and support research transparency and reproducibility. File Descriptions 1. Extended Technical Methods for OrbitalPSI-GPT.pdf This document provides detailed technical documentation of the OrbitalPSI-GPT framework, including the region-aware multiscale Gaussian process morphable model (GPMM), automated landmark detection (ALD), dataset preparation, training and evaluation protocols, and model configuration information. It also documents anatomical constraints, reconstruction procedures, and model-version metadata to facilitate technical understanding and reproducibility. 2. Supplementary Video 1 | PSI Design Process via OrbitalPSI-GPT (Narrated Version) This video provides a concise, edited demonstration of the core PSI design workflow, accompanied by narration and voice-over. It highlights the key interactions within the OrbitalPSI-GPT interface, illustrating the progression from natural-language instructions to the final patient-specific implant design. 3. Supplementary Video 2 | PSI Design Process via OrbitalPSI-GPT (Unedited/Raw Version) This video contains the complete, unedited screen recording of a PSI design session. It documents the actual interaction sequence, system response latency, iterative design adjustments, and final design output without post-processing. The recording provides a transparent demonstration of the system's operational performance under the recorded conditions. Related Resources Source code and software updates: https://github.com/GaryGaoYao/OrbitalPSI-GPT Associated manuscript: A Text-Driven Clinician-in-the-Loop Approach to Accessible Patient-Specific Orbital Implant Design for Low-Resource Settings.

title: Long-Tail-Aware Semantic-Structural Decision Fusion for Entity Alignment
authors: PANG Jun, CHU Xiaojie, LI Tianyi, XU Yifeng, WANG Mengxiang
abstract: Entity alignment is a critical task of knowledge graph fusion, aiming to identify equivalent entities within different knowledge graphs. Although most existing related methods directly integrating structure and auxiliary information at the feature layer have achieved certain results, they have the following shortcomings: (1) Semantic modeling lacks the constraints of structure and alignment tasks. (2) Structural learning overlooks the directionality and heterogeneity of relationships, and lacks adaptive processing of cross-graph statistical discrepancies. (3) The fusion process tends to dilute the discriminative capacity of semantics and structure. Therefore, a long-tail-aware semantic-structural decision fusion for entity alignment (LT-DFEA) is proposed. Firstly, a structure-aware semantic representation strategy is proposed, which combines the entity structure description and fine-grained alignment loss to fine-tune BERT, thereby integrating structure and alignment constraints into semantic space. Secondly, an attention network with relationship direction and critical path perception is proposed, which explicitly encodes directed relationships and core dependency paths. Complementarily, a hierarchical proxy-based graph matching network is proposed for cross-graph statistical discrepancies modeling, thereby adaptively optimizing structural embeddings. Additionally, a confidence-aware decision fusion method is proposed, which adaptively assigns weights to semantic and structural decisions based on long-tail entity discrimination results to achieve complementary advantages of the two types of information. Finally, a bidirectional nearest neighbor strategy based on a threshold is introduced to generate high-confidence pseudo-seeds, iteratively optimizing structural embeddings, and using semantic signals to alleviate the hubness bias in the structural space. Experimental results on five real datasets show that the LT-DFEA model improves the Hits@1 metric by 1 to 3 percentage points compared with the baseline models.

title: Interpretable machine learning with bayesian additive models for imbalanced public-health data
abstract: Data from public health studies frequently have unusual outcomes, missing data, risk structures that are more complex and nonlinear associations between risk factors and outcomes. Conventional machine-learning models are less reliable due to these characteristics, as models optimized primarily for the overall accuracy may have good performance on the majority class, but poor performance on the minority class which may be very significant in the context of making epidemiological decisions. In this paper we present and test an interpretable Bayesian Additive Machine Learning framework for imbalanced Public-Health data. The proposed framework integrates the following methods: Bayesian additive modelling, class-sensitive priors, posterior uncertainty estimation, and posterior feature effects, among others, and attribution tools like SHAP. The goal is not just to enhance the identification of minorities, but also to offer certain, uncertain explanations to public-health researchers, clinicians and policy actors. A simulated benchmark with a public-health outcome that is controlled and is an imbalanced binary outcome is provided for comparison purposes with LASSO logistic regression, random forest and XGBoost. The results reveal that the best overall discrimination, minority class sensitivity, calibration and explanation stability was achieved by the Bayesian additive framework. The proposed model also obtained an AUC of 0.846, minor class F1 score of 0.493, and balanced accuracy of 0.768, and had the lowest calibration error value and highest explanation stability index values. The age, burden of comorbidities, previous admission, SBP and diabetes, were found as the most important risk factors for posterior effects. The paper highlights the advantages of interpretable Bayesian additive models for public-health analytics, including credible intervals, a flexible non-linear prediction and probabilistic reasoning as well as being practically transparent. The study provides a statistically-informed approach to ethical, interpretable and policy-relevant machine learning in public-health.

title: Developing AI-Powered Chatbots as Learning Assistants to Enhance Undergraduate Computer Science and Engineering Education
abstract: This paper presents the design, classroom deployment, and evaluation of AI-powered chatbots developed as learning assistants for undergraduate computer science and engineering education. To address growing concerns that large language model (LLM)–based tools encourage student over-reliance and hinder critical thinking, our chatbots emphasize guided reasoning over direct answer provision. Grounded in constructivist learning theory and instructional scaffolding principles, the systems foster conceptual understanding by providing structured hints, step-by-step explanations, and reflective prompts that guide student reasoning without revealing complete solutions. We developed multiple implementations using the Rasa framework and OpenAI GPT-based platforms, and conducted a mixed-methods study across three courses—an undergraduate C++ programming course, an assembly language course, and a freshman college experience course—to examine student interaction patterns, perceived usefulness, and learning outcomes. Data were collected via comparative testing, post-interaction surveys, and informal student interviews. The findings indicate that students value the guided approach, reporting higher engagement, improved confidence, and deeper understanding compared to direct-answer AI tools. However, challenges remain, particularly regarding students’ adjustment to non-solution-based assistance and natural language understanding (NLU) limitations that occasionally resulted in ambiguous guidance. This study contributes empirical evidence that guided AI dialogue serves as a pedagogically aligned alternative to direct-answer AI tutors. Furthermore, it offers practical insights into instructional integration, system design, and deployment challenges in authentic classroom settings. Future work will explore Google Vertex AI to support scalability and enhanced analytics, improve NLU accuracy, incorporate adaptive learning mechanisms, embed assessment instruments within workflows, and conduct controlled comparative studies across diverse AI platforms and course contexts.

title: Analysis of Noisy Environments on D‐Dimensional Quantum Secret Sharing
abstract: ABSTRACT Quantum secret sharing is a fundamental protocol for securely transmitting quantum as well as classical information. However, in practical quantum communication scenarios, the transmission of quantum information is inevitably influenced by environmental noise. Therefore, in this work, we analyze the robustness of multi‐dimensional quantum secret sharing schemes under four different noise models, namely amplitude damping (ad), depolarizing (d), dit flip (df), and phase flip (dpf). Each model captures a distinct type of quantum disturbance, providing insights into how different noise models affect the fidelity of secret reconstruction. In addition to state‐specific fidelity, we also evaluate the average fidelity over arbitrary pure qutrit secret states using the Haar, equivalently Fubini–Study, measure. This provides a state‐independent robustness indicator and allows a more meaningful comparison of the considered quantum secret sharing schemes when the dealer's secret state is arbitrary. Moreover, we observe that protocols involving a larger number of qudits generally exhibit higher implementation complexity and increased sensitivity to noise. Consequently, the fidelity degrades more rapidly. Moreover, it is observed that the amplitude damping noise shows the highest fidelity across most parameter ranges, suggesting a better preservation of quantum secret.

title: Semantic Clustering and LLM ‐Based Recommendation for Industrial Fault Diagnosis
abstract: ABSTRACT Industrial maintenance systems generate large volumes of fault records that are typically stored as unstructured textual descriptions, making automated analysis and solution recommendation challenging. This study presents an AI‐assisted framework with two complementary components for Turkish industrial maintenance data: semantic clustering of fault descriptions and LoRA‐based generation of corrective‐action suggestions. Fault descriptions are transformed into semantic representations using multiple embedding methods, reduced with Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP), and clustered with HDBSCAN. Under the fixed UMAP‐HDBSCAN configuration reported in this study, Language‐Agnostic Sentence Representations (LASER) obtained the strongest internal clustering results, including a Silhouette score of 0.8529. For recommendation generation, Meta‐LLaMA‐3‐8B, Phi‐4, Gemma‐3n‐E4B, and T5‐base were fine‐tuned with Low‐Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and evaluated using ROUGE metrics. Among the evaluated models, Phi‐4 achieved the highest lexical‐overlap scores (ROUGE‐1 = 0.3320, ROUGE‐2 = 0.1915, ROUGE‐L = 0.3128, and ROUGE‐Lsum = 0.3127), followed by Meta‐LLaMA‐3‐8B. In the reported generation experiment, cluster identifiers, LASER distances, and retrieved historical actions were not supplied as additional Large Language Model (LLM) input; consequently, the present results should not be interpreted as evidence that clustering causally improves generation quality. Moreover, ROUGE measures lexical similarity rather than technical correctness, executability, or safety. The framework is therefore positioned as a decision‐support approach whose generated recommendations require domain‐expert verification before operational use.

title: MeRoPE: Metric Rotary Position Embedding for Camera-Controlled Video Generation
abstract: In camera-controlled video generation, geometry-aware positional encodings condition tokens on camera extrinsics and per-token viewing rays. Existing schemes, however, have a scale-dependent failure mode on real-world metric camera trajectories: homogeneous projective encodings cause attention logits and feature norms to grow unbounded with physical translation baselines. We propose MeRoPE (Metric Rotary Position Embedding), a norm-preserving relative camera encoding for attention. MeRoPE encodes relative orientations between calibrated viewing rays with orthogonal rotation blocks, maps raw metric displacements into multi-frequency rotary phases, and adds a disparity-anchored correspondence prior along the epipolar arc. This design strictly preserves feature norms, bounds pre-softmax attention logits regardless of the physical translation scale, and maintains exact invariance to global rigid coordinate changes. Across nuScenes and PanShot, which cover large-baseline trajectories and diverse camera optics, respectively, MeRoPE achieves stronger camera control than prior encodings, with the best consistency between generated camera motion and conditioning poses in both rotation and translation. title: EvoGS: Modeling Deformation Evolution for Dynamic Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Recent extensions of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enable real-time novel view synthesis in dynamic scenes by learning time-conditioned Gaussian deformations. However, existing MLP-based methods typically estimate deformations independently at each timestamp, making them less robust to large or abrupt motions. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{EvoGS}, a 3DGS-based dynamic reconstruction framework that models Gaussian deformation as a temporal evolution process. EvoGS maintains persistent deformation states for each Gaussian, extrapolates future states from historical deformation states, and corrects the predictions with MLP-derived observations. The correction is adaptively weighted using a temporal residual memory and evolution statistics such as deformation velocity and trajectory deviation. To further improve reconstruction quality, EvoGS introduces deformation-aware densification. Clone and split operations are performed along corrected deformation directions, while an uncertainty-aware strategy suppresses densification for Gaussians with unstable deformation histories. Experiments show that EvoGS improves dynamic novel view synthesis quality and achieves competitive performance across benchmarks.

title: Joint Training Is Not Enough: Conditioned Cross-Granularity Training for Multimodal Document Understanding
abstract: The Mutual Reinforcement Effect (MRE) asks whether a fine, span-level and a coarse, document-level task help each other when one model handles both. We test it in multimodal document understanding on three corpora, two of receipts and one of scanned business forms, comparing single-task, joint and conditioned training, which puts one granularity's gold output in the other's prompt during training only. We build Doc-MRE, an annotation layer pairing gold field extraction (point) with four document-level facets (line), from a three-judge LLM committee under a pre-registration, validated by blind re-annotation. One predicate, fixed in advance: at a shared recipe, a regime reinforces if it beats the matched single-task model on both granularities. Mixed joint training, the arrangement prior MRE work assumes, reinforces on no corpus at the main scale: it is below both single-task models on CORD and trades one granularity for the other on the two others, as single-task tuning does. Conditioned training reinforces on two of the three, CORD (+0.5 point, +4.8 line) and the forms corpus (+7.2 point, +11.0 line), resolvably on the coarse side and directionally on the fine one, and trades on WildReceipt; at that recipe no alternative measurably beats it on either side anywhere. Two byte-identical-prompt controls separate content from format: shuffled conditioning destroys the coarse-side skill but costs the fine side far less, and a neutral-content control reproduces the whole fine-side gain on WildReceipt, which is therefore prompt structure but buys nothing resolvable on the other two. On the forms corpus conditioning buys collapse avoidance: mixed training and the neutral control both assign the majority semantic label to all 50 test documents; only conditioning recovers the gold distribution. Probes find the information decodable under every regime with no resolvable increase under conditioning.

title: GlitchLab: A Hardware-in-the-Loop Optimizer for Physical Fault Injection
abstract: Physical fault injection can turn brief hardware disturbances into security failures such as key recovery, authentication bypass, and unintended control flow. Finding effective faults is difficult because many interacting parameters create a large search space, successful settings are sparse and target-dependent, and each hardware attempt provides limited feedback. Under fixed testing time, efficient search is therefore critical for assessing fault sensitivity. We present GlitchLab, an online hardware-in-the-loop platform that treats delay as a timing gate, voltage and pulse duration as severity controls, and hardware outcomes as structured feedback. It implements RL-Q (Q-learning-based reinforcement learning), a structured bandit for discovery, and Structured-Outcome-Based Adaptive Search (SOBAS), a model-based policy for fault reproduction. Both policies find a target fault in every AES, password, and control-flow campaign. On AES and control flow, they require 2-85x fewer attempts and 26-1,237x less time than the baselines; on password, both succeed while the baselines fail within 5,000 attempts. After discovery, SOBAS reproduces faults 7.3-21x more often, while RL-Q identifies 30% more distinct AES settings.

title: Modeling and Generating Trustworthy Speech
abstract: As virtual agents become increasingly integrated into everyday communication, trust has become essential for effective human-AI interaction. Although recent advances in natural language generation and speech synthesis have significantly improved fluency and intelligibility, most systems are not designed to control how trustworthy they are perceived. As a result, a mismatch can emerge between perceived trustworthiness and actual system capability, leading to over-trust or under-trust. While trust is critical for meaningful interaction, current text-to-speech (TTS) systems are primarily optimized for naturalness and intelligibility rather than calibrated trustworthiness. This dissertation investigates the perceptual foundations of trust in both human and synthesized speech through the study of acoustic prosody, lexical style, and speaker/listener dynamics. Across multiple studies, the findings show that trust perception is highly context-dependent and shaped by the interaction of vocal, linguistic, and multimodal cues. Rather than treating trust as a property to be uniformly maximized, this work frames trust as a perceptual signal that should be calibrated to align with a system’s reliability, uncertainty, and communicative intent. Building on these insights, this dissertation introduces computational frameworks for modeling and generating trustworthy speech. The work first characterizes trust-related acoustic patterns in human speech, then extends the analysis to synthesized speech to identify both shared and modality-specific trust cues. Finally, a trust-aware speech generation framework is proposed that combines representation learning and reinforcement learning to generate speech conditioned on target trust levels, enabling adaptive control of speaking style and prosody. Overall, this dissertation advances a computational framework for understanding and generating calibrated trust in speech-based virtual agents. By connecting perceptual trust modeling with controllable speech generation, this work contributes toward intelligent virtual agents capable of dynamically adapting their communicative strategies to interact in ways that are not only natural and expressive, but also appropriately trustworthy across diverse users and interaction contexts.

title: TOMA: Türkçe Okunabilirlik ve Metin Analizi Programı’nın Geliştirilmesi
abstract: Bu çalışmada Türkçe metinlerin okunabilirliğinin ve bağdaşıklık/tutarlılık durumlarının otomatik olarak analiz edilebilmesi için bir program tasarlanması ve bu programın hesaplama doğruluğunun sınanması amaçlanmıştır. Bu amaç kapsamında Python ve çeşitli NLP araçları kullanılarak Türkçe için geliştirilmiş okunabilirlik formüllerini ve bağdaşıklık/tutarlılık formülünü otomatik olarak hesaplayan program geliştirilmiştir. 15’ten fazla parametreyi ve 8 formülü hesaplayan programın hesaplama doğruluğu 57 metinden oluşan derlem ile değerlendirilmiş ve programın, formülleri yüksek doğrulukla hesaplayabildiği saptanmıştır. Formülleri yüksek doğrulukla hesapladığı teyit edilen program, bu çalışmada verilen bağlantı ile açık erişimli olarak araştırmacıların kullanımına sunulmuştur. Geliştirilen programdan elde edilen yüksek doğruluktaki sonuçlar doğrultusunda TOMA aracının büyük derlem analizlerinde ve okunabilirlik araştırmalarında kullanılmasına ve programın sağladığı zaman tasarrufundan hareketle gerçekleştirilen metin analizi/okunabilirlik çalışmalarının kapsamının genişletilmesine yönelik önerilerde bulunulmuştur.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Financial Decision Making: Adoption, Applications and the Evolving Role of Human Judgement
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative tool in economic choice-making, reshaping how corporations and individuals make informed financial selections. This study explores the position of AI in improving economic selection making procedures, specializing in predictive analytics, danger evaluation, and portfolio management. How AI-pushed technology such as machine learning (ML), language processing (NLP), and neural networks can improve financial outcomes, reduce human bias, and provide real-time data insights. Through an analysis of current AI applications inside the financial quarter, this research goals to contribute to the body of understanding that supports higher choice-making frameworks. Overview, the adoption of AI in financial offerings has remained significant, but the present day contribution remains focused on operational efficiency and analytical assistance. While AI is being used in increasing numbers in regions that include fraud detection, credit risk modeling, and research funding, human judgment continues to play a huge role in final financial selections. The view therefore highlights the importance of a human-AI collaborative method supported by appropriate governance, transparency and duty.

title: Adversarial Effectiveness vs. Computational Cost: An Analysis of GCG and nanoGCG Adversarial Suffix Attacks
abstract: Small Language Models (SLMs) are gaining widespread adoption due to their lower computational cost, faster inference speed, and suitability for deployment on edge devices and resource-constrained environments. The adoption of SLMs in Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) applications makes security evaluation dependent on both adversarial effectiveness and computational cost. We compare Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) and nanoGCG adversarial suffix generation under equivalent experimental conditions using Python Risk Identification Tool (PyRIT). The evaluation considers Attack Success Rate (ASR), execution time, memory usage, estimated cost, and throughput. Our results support defensive red-teaming evaluations by relating attack success to the computational effort required to obtain it.

title: AI-ENABLED HOSTEL PERMISSION MANAGEMENT AND RECOMMENDATION SYSTEM
abstract: Manual, paper-based systems for managing student leave and outing requests in hostels are time-consuming, error-prone, and make it difficult for wardens to track a student’s request history. This paper presents a web-based Hostel Permission Management System that digitizes the entire leave, outing, and parent-visiting approval workflow: students submit requests through a dedicated portal, wardens review, approve, or reject them through a centralized dashboard, and administrators manage user accounts and records, all supported by role-based authentication. Parents are kept informed through automated email alerts — sent for every leave, outing, and visiting-request decision — and can themselves raise parent-visiting requests through a dedicated portal. The system’s key contribution is a two-part AI decision-support layer: a scikit-learn Decision Tree classifier that scores each incoming request as LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH risk from twelve behavioural and contextual features drawn from the student’s attendance and request history, and an AI-assisted leave summary built on Google’s Gemini API that turns that history — reason, duration, frequency, and past approval outcomes — into a concise, human-readable narrative grounded in the Decision Tree’s output. The system further introduces a time-bound QR gate pass for approved student leave, outing, and parent-visiting requests, which automatically expires once its approved time window has passed. The application is built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript on the frontend, PHP on the backend, and MySQL for storage, deployed on the XAMPP stack. Together, these components form a secure, efficient platform that reduces administrative overhead while demonstrating a practical, decision-support application of AI in educational administration.

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Development on Local Businesses: A Structured Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence has progressed from an experimental technology to a routine operational tool in a short period. This structured review consolidates evidence from industry reports and deployment cases on how recent AI developments are reshaping the operational landscape of local and small and medium sized enterprises. It examines concrete effects across customer acquisition, sales conversion, support workloads, and the role of vertically integrated platforms that package these capabilities for operators without technical staff, such as 3SELLER in the messaging based acquisition space. The findings suggest that the most reliable gains for local businesses come not from exotic model capabilities but from the disciplined automation of repetitive communication and qualification workflows. Artificial intelligence for local business, AI customer acquisition for small business, automated sales communication, conversational agents for SMEs, messaging based lead generation, AI workflow automation local business.

title: Opening the Black Box a Crack: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Explainability and Interpretability of Black-Box Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Explainability and Interpretability of Black-Box Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of explainable AI and interpretability as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Central Atlantic Tree-rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Sylvilagus brasiliensis*
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Central Atlantic Tree-rat" (CATR), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in *Sylvilagus brasiliensis* (Central Atlantic Tree-rat), a rodent known for its efficient and adaptable resource exploitation. The algorithm leverages the animal's unique approach to resource allocation, incorporating elements of spatial optimization, gradient descent, and a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance. CATR aims to provide a robust and adaptable solution for a variety of optimization problems. The core of the algorithm lies in a modified particle representation that simulates the tree-rat's spatial awareness and a novel adaptive inertia weight mechanism mimicking the animal's response to resource scarcity and abundance. The performance of CATR is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high-quality solutions with reasonable computational cost. The algorithm's adaptability and potential for further refinement are discussed.
